ἡ, olive, AP 6.299 (Phan.), Ath. 2.56a.
α, ον, perh. planted with olives, ἀγρός IG 9(1).61.20 (Daulis).
= δρυοπτερίς, Hsch.
ἀλήτην, Hsch. ; cf. δρώπτης.

E. El. 150 ; fut. δρύψω (κατα-) v.l. in AP 5.42 (Rufin.) ; aor. ἔδρυψα, Ep. δρύψα Il. 16.324 ; — Med., Hes. Sc. 243 (κατα, tm.), E. Hec. 655 (lyr.) ; aor. δρυψάμενος Od. 2.153 ; — Pass., AP 7.2 (Antip.Sid.) ; plpf. δέδρυπτο QS. 14.391 : — tear, strip, βραχίονα δουρὸς ἀκωκὴ δρύψ’ ἀπὸ μυώνων Il. l.c. ; — Med., δρυψαμένω δ’ ὀνύχεσσι παρειὰς ἀμφί τε δειράς tearing each other΄s cheeks and necks all round, Od. l.c. ; mostly in sign of mourning, δρύπτεν κάρα E. El. 150 (lyr.) ; ἑκάτερθε παρειάς ARh. 3.672 ; also δρύπτεσθαι παρειάν to tear one΄s cheek, E. Hec. 655 ; without παρειάν, X. Cyr. 3.1.13. metaph, τὴν δὲ χοῖρον αὐονὴ δρύπτει Herod. 8.2. — Poet., X. and later Prose, as Philostr. VA 3.38.

ἡ (Pelop. ὁ, acc. to Sch. Ar. Nu. 401, cf. IG 9(1).485.5 (Thyrrheum), but fem. in Arc., Schwyzer 664.23) ; gen. δρυός ; acc. δρῦν (δρύα QS. 3.280) ; nom. pl. δρύες Il. 12.132, A. Pr. 832, etc., δρῦς Thphr. CP 2.9.2, Paus. 8.12.1 ; acc. pl. δρῦς Ar. Eq. 528, Nu. 402, δρύας S. Fr. 403, Call. Del. 84, AP 7.8 (Antip.Sid.) ; gen. δρυῶν Hdt. 7.218 ; dual δρύε Hdn. Gr. 1.420. [υ, exc. in δρῦς, δρῦν ; gen. δρυός at the beginning of a verse, Hes. Op. 436] ; — originally, tree (δρῦν ἐκάλουν οἱ παλαιοὶ… πᾶν δένδρον Sch. Il. 11.86, cf. Hsch.) ; including various trees, Thphr. HP 3.8.2 ; esp. Quercus Aegilops (< φηγός) and Quercus Ilex (< πρῖνος), cf. ἡ φηγὸς καὶ ἡ πρῖνος εἴδη δρυός Dsc. 1.106 ; opp. πεύκη, Il. 11.494 ; opp. πίτυς, Od. 9.186, cf. Il. 13.389, 23.328, etc. ; στέφανος δρυός crown of oak leaves, SIG 2588.7 (Delos, ii BC) ; commonly, the oak, δ. ὑψικάρηνοι, ὑψίκομοι, Il. 12.132, 14.398, cf. 13.389, 23.328, etc. ; sacred to Zeus, who gave his oracles from the oaks of Dodona, Od. 14.328 ; αἱ προσήγοροι δρύες A. Pr. 832 ; πολύγλωσσος δ. S. Tr. 1168, cf. Pl. Phdr. 275b ; prov., οὐ γὰρ ἀπὸ δρυός ἐσσι… οὐδ’ ἀπὸ πέτρης thou art no foundling from the woods or rocks, i.e. thou hast parents and a country, Od. 19.163, cf. Pl. Ap. 34d, R. 544d, AP 10.55 (Pall.) ; but οὐ μέν πως νῦν ἔστιν ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδ’ ἀπὸ πέτρης… ὀαρίζειν ΄tis no time now to talk at ease from tree or rock, like lovers, Il. 22.126 ; ἀλλὰ τί ἦ μοι ταῦτα περὶ δρῦν ἢ περὶ πέτρην; why all this about trees and rocks (i.e. things we have nothing to do with)? Hes. Th. 35 ; also διὰ πέτρας καὶ διὰ δρυὸς ὁρᾶν ΄to see through a brick wall΄, Plu. 2.1083d. of other trees bearing acorns or mast (Paus. 8.1.6), πίειρα δρῦς the resinous wood (of the pine), S. Tr. 766 ; of the olive, E. Cyc. 615 (lyr.) ; δ. θαλασσία, = ἁλίφλοιος, Ps.-Democr. Symp. Ant. p. 5G. δ. ποντία, gulf-weed, Sargassum vulgare, Thphr. HP 4.6.9. metaph, worn-out old man, AP 6.254 (Myrin.), Artem. 2.25. (Cogn. with δόρυ; cf. Skt. dru- ΄wood΄, in compds.)
aor. part. δρυξάμενος, perh. = δρυφάσσω, δ. τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τῶν ὁρίων PGrenf. 1.11.14 (ii BC).
ον, wood-cutter, Il. 11.86, Theoc. 5.64, Philostr. Im. 2.33, al. ; cf. δρυοτόμος. [δρυ- QS. 9.163, 453, 13.56.]
αἱ, nail-parings, Hsch. ; also, = λῦπαι, ὀδύναι, i.e. lancinating pains or weals, bruises, Id.
aor. inf. δρυφάξαι· δακεῖν, Hsch.
τὸν οὐ μέγαν (Elean), Hsch.

ὁ, later τρύφακτος BCH 35.23 (Delos, iv BC), OGI 598.3 (Jerusalem), Hdn. Gr. 2.595 : — railing or latticed partition, serving as the bar of the courts of law, the council-chamber, etc., Ar. V. 380 ; mostly in pl., ὑπερεπήδων τοὺς δ. Id. Eq. 675 ; ὑπὸ τοῖς δ. Id. V. 386 ; ἐπὶ τοῖς δ. ib. 552, X HG 2.3.55 ; sg., δρυφάκτου τρόπῳ Apollod. Poliorc. 172.1.
hand-rail, Plb. 1.22.6, 10.
balcony, Arist. Ath. 50.2 ; — written δρύφρακτοι, Lib. Or. 11.217. (By dissim. for δρύφρακτος (< φράσσω), cf. Lib. l.c., Hellad. ap. Sch. Orib. 2 p. 746D., Sch. Ar. Eq. l.c.)
fence, fortify, Plb. 8.4.4.
ατος, τό, enclosure, Str. 13.4.14.
fence round, guard by a fence, Lyc. 758 (Pass.).
περαίνειν, and δρυφόμενοι· φθειρόμενοι, Hsch.
= κλάσματα, Hsch. s.v. πύρνα, cf. Suid.
ἡ, (< δρύπτω) tearing, Hsch.
οἱ, scrapings, Hsch.
οἱ, religious guild at Thessalonica (cf. δενδροφόρος), BCH 38.41 (δροι- lapis).
τό, lit. bark ; of a leaf, Parth. Fr. 26 ; δρύψαλα, Hsch.
τά, = δρύψελον, δ. τυρῶν AP 6.299 (Phan.).
οντος, ὁ, (< δρύπτω) worn-out old man, Hsch. ; also, = ἐλεεινός.
παιδος, ὁ, ἡ, coquette, Hsch.
ες, gloss on δρυόεις, Hsch.
(δροκτ- cod.) ; περιβλέπεις, Hsch. ; cf. δρωπάζω, δρώπτω.
τρέχει, and δρωμίσσουσα· τρέχουσα, Hsch.
(δράω²), gaze at, ADysc. Adv. 139.8, Hsch.
apply a depilatory, δ. μέλιτι Orib. Eup. 4.7 ; — Med., Arr. Epict. 3.22.10, Hierocl. Facet. 64 ; — Pass., Luc. Demon. 50.
ὁ, the application of a pitch-plaster, as a counter-irritant, Dsc. Ther. 3.
one must apply a pitch-plaster, Orib. Fr. 75.
οῦ, ὁ, = depilator, Gloss.
ή, όν, serving as a counter-irritant, Gal. 18(2).894.
ἡ, = παρατίλτρια, Phot.

ακος, ὁ, (< δρέπω) pitch-plaster, Hp. Ep. 19 (Hermes 53.71), Gal. 6.416, Dsc. Eup. 1.233, Archig. ap. Aët. 3.180 ; — also neut. pl. δρώπακα (sc. φάρμακα), Gal. 18(2).894. [α in Lat. gen., Mart. 3.74, 10.65.]
πλανήτης, πτωχός, Hsch.
= διακόπτω ἢ διασκοπῶ, A. Fr. 278.
ἄνθρωπος, Hsch.
Dor. for δύη.
make into a dyad, in Pass., ἡ δυαδιζομένη μονάς Dam. Pr. 147.
ή, όν, (< δύο) of or for the number two, Plu. 2.1025d ; opp. μοναδικός, Dam. Pr. 119 ; δ. πᾶσα πρόοδος ib. 47. Adv. -κῶς Procl. in Prm. p. 915 S., Herm. in Phdr. p. 151A.
ὁ, making into a dyad, Dam. Pr. 193.

express in the dual number, Eust. 47.28. Pass., to be impressed with the sense of a thing΄s being double, see double, etc., S.E. M. 7.193.
make into two, Ascl. in Metaph. 432.12 (Pass.) ; — Pass., to be halved, of the moon, Theol.Ar. 12.
double, Theo Sm. p. 29 H., Iamb. in Nic. p. 60P. δυάζει· φλυαρεῖ, Hsch., Cyr. (cf. δρυάζω) ; also δυαεῖ Hsch.
Adv. twice, Ar. Fr. 769.
οἱ, = Lat. duumviri, Wien. Stud. 24.288 (Olbasa).
ή, όν, = duumviralis, ib. 289.
ή, όν, = δυανδρικός, CIG 3979 (Antioch. Pisid.).
κρήνην, Hsch.

άδος, ἡ, the number two, Pl. Phd. 101c, Prm. 149c, Arist. Ph. 220a27, etc.
dyad, ἡ ἀόριστος δ. Arist. Metaph. 1081a14, Alex.Aphr. in Metaph. 58.12.
pair, Philostr. Im. 1.6, Lib. Or. 61.7.
(< δύη) plunge in misery, δυόωσιν… ἀνθρώπους Od. 20.195 ; — Pass., pf. part. δεδυημένη Hsch.
Dor. for ζυγός, Schwyzer 180 (Crete), 317 (Delph.), EM 316.57 ; Aeol., ib. 466.36 ; Boeot., Choerob. in Theod. 2.390.
Lacon. acc. of δύο.
ές, of the class of the dyad, μεσότης Dam. Pr. 189.
Adv. twice yearly, PAmh. 2.148.8 (V AD).
ά, όν, (< δύη) miserable, δυεροῦ θανάτοιο τυχεῖν IG 3.1337, cf. Max. 65, 182.

ἡ, Dor. (not in Trag.) δύα, poet. Noun, misery, anguish, Od. 14.215, etc. ; πῆμα δύης height of woe, ib. 338 ; πέλαγος ἀτηρᾶς δύης A. Pr. 746 ; γενναία δ. S. Aj. 938 (lyr.) ; pl., πημοναῖς δύαις τε A. Pr. 513, cf. 181 (lyr.), 525, etc. ; also in late Prose, App. BC 4.42 ; Pythag. name for two (by false etym.), Theol.Ar. 12.
[ῠᾰ] = δυηπαθία.
endure misery, Nonn. D. 26.113.
ές, much-suffering, ARh. 4.1165, Oppian. H. 2.436 ; painful, τοκετός Nonn. D. 41.411.
poet. δυηπαθίη, ἡ, misery, ARh. 4.1395, APl. 4.113 (Jul.), Hsch. ; — written δυηπάθεια, EM 291.10.
ον, = δυηπαθής, h.Merc. 486.
= δυσμή.
ή, όν, dual, DT. 635.30 ; τὸ δ. the dual number, ADysc. Pron. 10.28, S.E. M. 1.142. Adv. -κῶς in the dual number, Phoeb. Fig. 1.4, Anon. in Tht. 73.4 ; = διττῶς, Suid.
α, ον, = δυερός, A. Supp. 829 (lyr.).
ατος, τό, = ἔνδυμα, POxy. 929.8, 15 (ii/iii AD).
Ep. aor.2 inf. Act. of δύω.

2 sg. δύνασαι Il. 1.393, Od. 4.374, S. Aj. 1164 (anap.), Ar. Nu. 811 (lyr.), Pl. 574, X. An. 7.7.8, etc. ; δύνῃ Carm.Aur. 19, also in codd. of S. Ph. 798, E. Hec. 253, Andr. 239, and later Prose, Plb. 7.11.5, Ael. VH 13.32 ; Aeol. and Dor. δύνᾳ Alc. Oxy. 1788 Fr. 15 ii 16, Theoc. 10.2, also S. Ph. 849 (lyr.), dub. in OT 696 (lyr.) ; δύνῃ is subj., Ar. Eq. 491, cf. Phryn. 337 ; Ion. 3 pl. δυνέαται Hdt. 2.142 ; subj. δύνωμαι, Ion. 2 sg. δύνηαι Il. 6.229 (δυνεώμεθα, -ωνται as vv. ll. in Hdt. 4.97, 7.163) ; also δύναμαι Sappho Supp. 3.3, GDI 4952 A 42 (Crete) ; impf. 2 sg. ἐδύνω h.Merc. 405, X. An. 1.6.7 ; later ἐδύνασο Hp. Ep. 16 (v.l. ἠδ.), Luc. DMort. 9.1 ; Ion. 3 pl. ἐδυνέατο Hdt. 4.110, al. (ἠδ- codd.) ; fut. δυνήσομαι Od. 16.238, etc. ; Dor. δυνασοῦμαι Archyt. 3 ; later δυνηθήσομαι DC. 52.37 ; aor. ἐδυνησάμην Il. 14.33, Ep. δυν- 5.621 ; subj. δυνήσωνται Semon. 1.17, never in good Att., f.l. in D. 19.323 ; Pass. forms, Ep., Ion., Lyr., ἐδυνάσθην or δυνάσθην Il. 23.465, al., Hdt. 2.19, al., Pi. O. 1.56, Hp. Art. 48 (v.l. δυνηθείη), also in X. Mem. 1.2.24, An. 7.6.20 ; Trag. and Att. Prose ἐδυνήθην S. Aj. 1067, OT 1212 (lyr.), E. Ion 867 (anap.), D. 21.80, 186 ; pf. δεδύνημαι D. 4.30, Din. 2.14, Phld. Rh. 1.261S. — The double augment ἠδυνάμην is Att. acc. to Moer. 175, but Ion. acc. to An.Ox. 2.374, and is found in codd. of Hdt. 4.110, al., Hp. Epid. 1.26. β΄, al. ; ἠδύνω is required by metre in Philippid. 16 ; but is not found in Att. Inscrr. before 300 BC, IG2². 678.12, al., cf. ἠδύνασθε ib. 7.2711 (Acraeph., i AD) ; both forms occur in later writers ; ἠδυνήθην occurs in A. Pr. 208, and codd. of Th. 4.33, Lys. 3.42, etc. ; δύνομαι is a late form freq. in Pap. as UPZ 9 (ii BC), al. [υ, exc. in δυναμένοιο Od. 1.276, 11.414, Hom. Epigr. 15.1, and pr. n. Δυναμένη, metri gr.]
to be able, strong enough to do, c. inf. pres. et aor., Il. 19.163, 1.562, etc. ; fut. inf. is f.l. (πείσειν for πείθειν) in S. Ph. 1394, (κωλύσειν for κωλῦσαι) Plb. 21.11.13, etc. ; freq. abs., with inf. supplied from the context, εἰ δύνασαί γε if at least thou canst (sc. περισχέσθαι), Il. 1.393 ; also c. acc. Pron. or Adj., ὅσσον δύναμαι χερσίν τε ποσίν τε 20.360 ; [Ζεὺς] δύναται ἅπαντα Od. 4.237 ; μέγα δυνάμενος very powerful, mighty, 1.276, cf. 11.414 ; δ. μέγιστον ξείνων Hdt. 9.9, etc. ; μέγα δύναται, multum valet, A. Eu. 950 (lyr.) ; δ. Διὸς ἄγχιστα Id. Supp. 1035 ; οἱ δυνάμενοι men of power, rank, and influence, E. Or. 889, Th. 6.39, etc. ; οἱ δυνάμενοι, opp. οἱ μὴ ἔχοντες, Democr. 255 ; opp. οἱ πένητες, Archyt. 3 ; δυνάμενος παρά τινι having influence with him, Hdt. 7.5, And. 4.26, etc. ; δύνασθαι ἐν τοῖς πρώτοις Th. 4.105 ; δ. τοῖς χρήμασι, τῷ σώματι, Lys. 6.48, 24.4 ; ὁ δυνάμενος one that can maintain himself, Id. 24.12 ; of things, [διαφέρει] οἷς δύνανται differ in their potentialities, Plot. 6.3.17. of moral possibility, to be able, dare, bear to do a thing, mostly with neg., οὔτε τελευτὴν ποιῆσαι δύναται Od. 1.250 ; σε… οὐ δύναμαι προλιπεῖν 13.331, cf. S. Ant. 455 ; οὐκέτι ἐδύνατο ἐν τῷ καθεστῶτι τρόπῳ βιοτεύειν Th. 1.130 ; οὐδὲ σθένειν τοσοῦτον ᾠόμην τὰ σὰ κηρύγμαθ’ ὥστε… θεῶν νόμιμα δύνασθαι… ὑπερδραμεῖν S. Ant. 455.
enjoy a legal right, δ. τῆς γεωργίας ἀπηλλάχθαι POxy. 899.31 (ii/iii AD), etc. with ὡς and Sup., ὡς ἐδύναντο ἀδηλότατα as secretly as they could, Th. 7.50 ; ὡς δύναμαι μάλιστα κατατείνας as forcibly as I possibly can, Pl. R. 367b ; ὡς δύναιτο κάλλιστον Id. Smp. 214c ; ὡς ἂν δύνωμαι διὰ βραχυτάτων D. 27.3, etc. ; simply ὡς ἐδύνατο in the best way he could, X. An. 2.6.2 ; with relat., ὅσους ἐδύνατο πλείστους ἀθροίσας Id. HG 2.2.9 ; λαβεῖν… οὓς ἂν σοφωτάτους δύνωμαι Alex. 213.
to be equivalent to, λόγοι ἔργα δυνάμενοι words that are as good as deeds, Th. 6.40 ; hence, of money, to be worth, c. acc., ὁ σίγλος δύναται ἑπτὰ ὀβολούς X. An. 1.5.6, cf. D. 34.23 ; abs., pass, be current, Luc. Luct. 10. of Number, etc., to be equal or equivalent to, τριηκόσιαι γενεαὶ δυνέαται μύρια ἔτεα Hdt. 2.142 ; δυνήσεται τὴν ὑποτείνουσαν will be equivalent to the hypotenuse, Arist. IA 709a19. of words, signify, mean, Hdt. 4.110, al. ; τὸ πειρηθῆναι καὶ τὸ ποιεῖν ἴσον δύναται Id. 6.86. γ’ ; δύναται ἴσον τῷ δρᾶν τὸ νοεῖν Ar. Fr. 691 ; δύναται τὸ νεοδαμῶδες ἤδη ἐλεύθερον εἶναι Th. 7.58 ; in later Greek, δύναται τὸ "μνασθέντι" ἀντὶ τοῦ "μνασθέντος" is equivalent to…, Sch. Pi. O. 7.110.
avail to produce, οὐδένα καιρὸν δύναται brings no advantage, E. Med. 128 (anap.), cf. Pl. Phlb. 23d. of things, mean, ΄spell΄, τὸ τριβώνιον τί δύναται ; Ar. Pl. 842 ; αἱ ἀγγελίαι τοῦτο δύνανται they mean this much, Th. 6.36 ; τὴν αὐτὴν δ. δούλωσιν Id. 1.141, cf. Arist. Pol. 1313b25. Math., δύνασθαί τι to be equivalent when squared to a number or area, τοῖς ἐπιπέδοις ἃ δύνανται in the areas of which they [the lines] are the roots, Pl. Tht. 148b ; ἡ ΒΓ τῆς Α μεῖζον δύναται τῇ ΔΖ the square on ΒΓ is greater than the square on A by the square on ΔΖ, Euc. 10.17 ; αἱ δυνάμεναι αὐτά [τὰ μεγέθη] the lines representing their square roots, ib. Def. 4, cf. Prop. 22 ; αὐξήσεις δυνάμεναί τε καὶ δυναστευόμεναι increments both in the roots and powers of numbers, Pl. R. 546b ; τὴν ὑποτείνουσαν ταῖς περὶ τὴν ὀρθὴν ἴσον δυναμένην Plu. 2.720a, cf. Iamb. Comm. Math. 17 ; ἡ δυναμένη, Pythag. name for the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle, Alex.Aphr. in Metaph. 75.31. of numbers multiplied together, come to, Papp. 1.24, 27. impers., οὐ δύναται, c. aor. inf., it cannot be, is not to be, τοῖσι Σπαρτιήτῃσι καλλιερῆσαι οὐκ ἐδύνατο Hdt. 7.134, cf. 9.45 ; δύναται it is possible, Plu. 2.440e (s.v.l.).
ά, όν, potent, of drugs ; hence as Subst., φυσικὰ δυναμερά, title of work by Ps.-Bolus, Suid. s.v. Βῶλος, cf. Archig. ap. Aët. 3.114.

ή, όν, powerful, efficacious, ἐρωτήματα Chrysipp. Stoic. 2.90 (Comp.) ; τὸ τοῦ λόγου δ. Phld. Rh. 1.378 S. (Sup.) ; λόγος, of a magician΄s spell, Ps.-Callisth. 1.3 ; πρός τι Plb. 22.21.4, Onos. 12.2 (Comp.) ; κατὰ τὴν σωματικὴν ἕξιν Plb. 36.16.3 (Sup.) ; of wine, potent, Ath. 1.26b (Sup.).
potential, τὸ δ., opp. τὸ ὑποστατικόν, τὸ ἐνεργητικόν, Dam. Pr. 61.
Gramm., expressing possibility, δ. σύνδεσμος (of κα) Sch. Theoc. 1.4.

ἡ, gen. εως, Ion. ιος, Ion. dat. δυνάμι ; (< δύναμαι) : — power, might, in Hom., esp. of bodily strength, εἴ μοι δ. γε παρείη Od. 2.62, cf. Il. 8.294 ; οἵη ἐμὴ δ. καὶ χεῖρες Od. 20.237 ; ἡ δ. τῶν νέων Antipho 4.3.2, etc. ; generally, strength, power, ability to do anything, πὰρ δύναμιν beyond one΄s strength, Il. 13.787 ; in Prose, παρὰ δ. τολμηταί Th. 1.70, etc. ; ὑπὲρ δ. D. 18.193 ; opp. κατὰ δ. as far as lies in one, Hdt. 3.142, etc. (κὰδ δ. Hes. Op. 336) ; εἰς δύναμιν Cratin. 172, Pl. R. 458e, etc. ; πρὸς τὴν δ. Id. Phdr. 231a.
outward power, influence, authority, A. Pers. 174 (anap.), Ag. 779 (lyr.) ; καταπαύσαντα τὴν Κύρου δ. Hdt. 1.90 ; δυνάμει προὔχοντες Th. 7.21, etc. ; ἐν δ. εἶναι, γενέσθαι, X. HG 4.4.5, D. 13.29.
force for war, forces, δ. ἀνδρῶν Hdt. 5.100, cf. Pl. Mx. 240d, Plb. 1.41.2, LXX Ge. 21.22, OGI 139.8 (ii BC) ; μετὰ δυνάμεων ἱκανῶν Wilcken Chr. 10 (ii BC), etc. ; δ. καὶ πεζὴ καὶ ἱππικὴ καὶ ναυτική X. An. 1.3.12 ; πέντε δυνάμεσι πεφρουρημένον, of the five projecting rows of sarissae in the phalanx, Ascl.Tact. 5.2, al.
a power, quantity, χρημάτων δ. Hdt. 7.9. αʹ.
means, κατὰ δύναμιν Arist. EE 1243b12 ; opp. παρὰ δ., 2 Ep. Cor. 8.3 ; κατὰ δ. τῶν ὑπαρχόντων BGU 1051.17 (Aug.).
power, faculty, capacity, αἱ ἀμφὶ τὸ σῶμα δ. Hp. VM 14 ; αἱ τοῦ σώματος δυνάμεις Pl. Tht. 185e ; ἡ τῆς ὄψεως δ. Id. R. 532a ; ἡ τῶν λεγόντων δ. D. 22.11 ; c. gen. rei, capacity for, τῶν ἔργων Arist. Pol. 1309a35 ; τοῦ λέγειν Id. Rh. 1362b22 ; τοῦ λόγου, τῶν λόγων, Men. 578, Alex. 94 ; δ. στρατηγική Plb. 1.84.6 ; δ. ἐν πραγματείᾳ Id. 2.56.5 ; δ. συνθετική DH. Comp. 2 ; abs., any natural capacity or faculty, that may be improved and may be used for good or ill, Arist. Top. 126a37, cf. MM 1183b28.
elementary force, such as heat, cold, etc., Hp. VM 16, Arist. PA 646a14 ; ἡ τοῦ θερμοῦ δ. ib. 650a5 ; θερμαντικὴ δ. Epicur. Fr. 60, cf. Polystr. p. 23 W.
property, quality, ἰδίην δύναμιν καὶ φύσιν ἔχειν Hp. VM 13, cf. Nat. Hom. 5, Vict. 1.10 ; esp. of the natural properties of plants, etc., αἱ δ. τῶν φυομένων, τῶν σπερμάτων, X. Cyr. 8.8.14, Thphr. HP 8.11.1 ; productive power, τῆς γῆς Id. Oec. 16.4 ; μετάλλων Id. Vect. 4.1 ; generally, function, faculty, δύναμις φυσική, ζωική, ψυχική, Gal. 10.635 ; περὶ φυσικῶν δ., title of work by Galen. in pl., agencies, ὑπάρχειν ἐν τῇ φύσει τὰς τοιαύτας δυνάμεις (sc. the gods) Polystr. p. 10 W.
function, meaning, of part in whole, Id. p. 17 W. in Music, function, value, of a note in the scale, δ. ἐστι τάξις φθόγγου ἐν συστήματι Cleonid. Harm. 14, cf. Aristox. Harm. p. 69M. ; μέση κατὰ δύναμιν, opp. κατὰ θέσιν, Ptol. Harm. 2.5.
faculty, art, or craft, Pl. R. 532d, Arist. Metaph. 1018a30, EN 1094a10, Arr. Epict. 1.1.1 ; δ. σκεπτική the doctrine of the Sceptics, S.E. M. 7.1.
a medicine, Timostr. 7, etc. ; δ. ἁπλαῖ Hp. Decent. 9, Aret. CD 1.4, etc. ; δ. πολυφάρμακοι Plu. 2.403c, Gal. 13.365 ; in pl., collection of formulae or prescriptions, Orib. 10.33.
action of medicines, περὶ τῆς ἁπλῶν φαρμάκων δ., title of work by Galen ; also, potency, δυνάμει θερμά, ψυχρά, Id. 1.672, al.
magically potent substance or object, PMagLeid. V. 8.12 ; in pl., magical powers, Hld. 4.7.
force or meaning of a word, Lys. 10.7, Pl. Cra. 394b, Diog.Oen. 12, Phld. Sign. 31, etc. phonetic value of sounds or letters, Plb. 10.47.8, DH. Comp. 12, Luc. Jud. Voc. 5, etc.
worth or value of money, Th. 6.46, 2.97, Plu. Lyc. 9, Sol. 15.
capability of existing or acting, potentiality, opp. actuality (< ἐνέργεια), Arist. Metaph. 1047b31, 1051a5, etc. ; hence δυνάμει as Adv., virtually, ὕστερον ὂν τῇ τάξει, πρότερον τῇ δυνάμει… ἐστί D. 3.15 ; opp. ἐνεργείᾳ, Arist. APo. 86a28, al. ; opp. ἐντελεχείᾳ, Id. Ph. 193b8, al. Math., power, κατὰ μεταφορὰν ἡ ἐν γεωμετρίᾳ λέγεται δ. Id. Metaph. 1019b33 ; usu.
second power, square, κατὰ δύναμιν in square, Pl. Ti. 54b, cf. Theol.Ar. 11, etc. ; chiefly in dat., [εὐθεῖα] δυνάμει ἴση a line the square on which is equal to an area, ἡ BA ἐλάσσων ἐστὶν ἢ διπλασίων δυνάμει τῆς AK the square on BA is less than double of the square on AK, Archim. Sph. Cyl. 2.9 ; εὐθεῖαι δ. σύμμετροι commensurable in square, Euc. 10 Def. 2 ; ἡ δυνάμει δεκάς the series 12 + 22.… + 102, Theol.Ar. 64.
square number, Pl. Ti. 32a.
square of an unknown quantity (x2), Dioph. Def. 2, al.
square root of a number which is not a perfect square, surd, opp. μῆκος, Pl. Tht. 147d.
product of two numbers, ἡ ἀμφοῖν (sc. τριάδος καὶ δυάδος) δ. ἑξάς Ph. 1.3, cf. Iamb. in Nic. p. 108 P. ; δυνάμει in product, Hero Metr. 1.15, Theol.Ar. 33. concrete, powers, esp. of divine beings, αἱ δ. τῶν οὐρανῶν LXX Is. 34.4, cf. 1 Ep. Pet. 3.22, al., Ph. 1.587, Corp.Herm. 1.26, Porph. Abst. 2.34 ; sg., Act. Ap. 8.10, PMagPar. 1.1275 ; πολυώνυμος δ., of God, Secund. Sent. 3.
manifestation of divine power, miracle, Ev. Matt. 11.21, al., Buresch Aus Lydien 113, etc.
εως, ἡ, square multiplied by square, fourth power, Hero Metr. 1.17 ; fourth power of unknown quantity (x⁴), Dioph. Def. 1 (pl.), al.
τό, the fraction 1/x⁴, Dioph. Def. 3, al.
ὁ, square multiplied by cube, fifth power, Hippol. Haer. 1.2.10 ; fifth power of unknown quantity (x⁵), Dioph. Def. 1 (pl.), al.
τό, the fraction 1/x⁵, Dioph. Def. 3, al.
τό, the fraction 1/x², Dioph. Def. 3, al.

strengthen, LXX Ec. 10.10, Thd. Da. 9.27, Polem. Call. 30, Porph. Sent. 35, Sall. 16, Procl. Inst. 70, al. ; — Pass., Ep. Col. 1.11, etc. in magic, put power into, σῶμα PMagLeid. W. 7.16 ; πρᾶγμα ib. V. 8.19 ; τινά PMagPar. 1.197 ; — Pass., PMagBerol. 2.121.
εως, ἡ, strengthening, fortifying, invigoration, ψυχῆς Plot. 4.6.3.
ή, όν, strengthening, ἡ δύναμις τῶν πάντων δυναμωτικώτατον (sc. αἴτιον) Dam. Pr. 61.
εως, ἡ, poet. for δύναμις, Pi. P. 4.238, B. 9.49, S. Ant. 604 (lyr.), 952 (lyr.), E. Ion 1012 ; ἐν (i.e. ἐς) δύνασιν pro virili parte, IG2². 1126.5 (Amphict. Delph.).

ἡ, power, lordship, domination, S. OT 593, D. 18.67 ; δ. ὀλίγων ἀνδρῶν Th. 3.62 ; πολιτικαὶ δ. the exercise of political power, Pl. Tht. 176c ; οἱ τὰς δ. ἔχοντες Isoc. 2.8, cf. 9.19, Plb. 3.18.1.
close oligarchy, opp. ἰσονομία, Th. 4.78, cf. And. 2.27, X. HG 5.44.46, etc. ; ὑπὸ τῶν ὀλίγων δ. Pl. Plt. 291d ; opp. πολιτεία, Arist. Pol. 1272b10 ; distd. fr. ὀλιγαρχία, ib. 1292b10, cf. 1293a31 ; in pl., of the Roman Senate, DC. 52.1. in pl., mighty deeds, LXX 4Ki. 13.12, al.
ἡ, fem. of δυνάστης, Tab. Defix. Aud. 38.11 (Alexandria, iii AD).
ατος, τό, in pl., natural resources, τὰ δ. τοῦ Λιβάνου LXX 3Ki. 2.46c.

ή, όν, arbitrary, ὀλιγαρχία Arist. Pol. 1298a32 ; oligarchical, αἵρεσις ib. 1306a18 ; ἰατρεία (opp. πολιτική) ib. 1272b3 ; πόλεις καὶ χῶραι Phld. Rh. 2.145 S. ; λόγος Plu. 2.818a ; tyrannical, δούλωσις Porph. Abst. 1.8.

hold power or lordship, be powerful or influential, Hdt. 9.2, Isoc. 12.82, OGI 56.12, etc. ; τὸ δυναστεῦον, opp. δῆμος, Th. 6.89 ; ἡ πόλις τῶν λοιπέων ἐδυνάστευε μέγιστον Hdt. 5.97 ; c. gen., to be lord over, Οἰχαλίας DS. 4.31 ; metaph, αἱ ἄλογοι ἡδοναὶ δ. ψυχῆς Ph. 1.19 ; c. dat., Ath. 14.624d ; generally, prevail, be prevalent, of a wind, of climate, Hp. Aph. 3.5, Aër. 12 ; to be influential, potent, ἐν τῷ σώματι Id. VM 16, cf. Herophil. ap. Gal. 12.619 ; — Pass., to be ruled, πρὸς μυρίων Ph. 2.503. Math., in Pass., to be concerned with powers of numbers, Pl. R. 546b.

ου, ὁ, lord, master, ruler, of Zeus, S. Ant. 608 (lyr.) ; ἄνδρες δ. the chief men in a state, Hdt. 2.32, cf. Pl. R. 473d, etc. ; petty chief, princelet, Th. 7.33, etc. ; ἡγεμόσι καὶ δ. καὶ βασιλεῦσιν Plb. 9.23.5, cf. 10.34.2, Posidon. 50 J., Str. 17.3.25 ; λαμπροὶ δυνάσται, of the stars, A. Ag. 6.
ή, όν, of or for a δυνάστης, arbitrary, Arist. Pol. 1320b31 (Sup.) ; Comp., more potent, Gal. 6.396.
ιδος, ἡ, fem. of δυνάστης, Demetr. Eloc. 292 ; τύχη ἡ πάντων δ. ἀνθρώπων dub. in Phld. Mort. 24.
ορος, ὁ, = δυνάστης, E. IA 280 (lyr.).

= δύναμαι, δυνατήσει τὸ συμβαῖνον ἴσχειν Phld. Sign. 11.
to be mighty, 2 Ep. Cor. 13.3.
ου, ὁ, poet. for δυνάστης, ὦ δυνάτα A. Pers. 674 (lyr., cod. Med.).

ή, όν, also ός, όν Pi. N. 2.14, Apollon.Cit. 2 : — strong, mighty, in body or mind, ὅ τι ἦν αὐτῶν δυνατώτατον the ablest-bodied men, Hdt. 9.31 ; sound in limb, opp. ἀδύνατος, Lys. 24.12 ; σῶμα δ. πρός τι X. Oec. 7.23 ; χερσὶ καὶ ψυχᾷ δ. Pi. N. 9.39 ; τοῖς σώμασι καὶ ταῖς ψυχαῖς X. Mem. 2.1.19 ; εἴς τι Pl. Hp. Mi. 366a ; κατά τι ib. 366d (Sup.) ; c. acc., ibid. (Sup.) ; of ships, fit for service, Th. 7.60 ; of things, δυνατώτερον ἀδικία δικαιοσύνης Pl. R. 351a ; λόγος a powerful argument, Epicur. Ep. 1 p. 31U. ; δ. προτείχισμα Plb. 10.31.8. c. inf., able to do, Hdt. 1.97, etc. ; δ. λῦσαι mighty to loose, Pi. O. 10 (11).9 ; λέγειν τε καὶ πράσσεινώτατος Th. 1.139, Pl. Prt. 319a ; δυνατώτατοι καὶ τοῖς σώμασιν καὶ τοῖς χρήμασιν λῃτουργεῖν Decr. ap. Arist. Ath. 29.5 ; ἐᾶν τοὺς δ. ἄρχειν X. Ath. 1.3 ; ὅσονπερ δ. εἰμι, with inf. omitted, E. Or. 523. of outward power, powerful, influential, S. El. 219 ; τῶν Ἑλλήνων δυνατώτατοι Hdt. 1.53 ; οἱ δ. the chief men of rank and influence, Th. 2.65 ; χρήμασι δ. Id. 1.13, etc., cf. OGI 669.13 (i AD).
able to produce, productive, χώρα δυνατωτέρα εἰς τὴν καρπῶν ἔκφυσιν Gp. 2.21.5.
potential, Arist. Metaph. 1048a27.
Pass., of things, possible, οὐ δύνατον γένεσθαι Sappho Supp. 5.21, cf. Hdt. 9.111, A. Ag. 97 (lyr.), etc. ; ὁδὸς δυνατὴ καὶ τοῖς ὑποζυγίοις πορεύεσθαι practicable, X. An. 4.1.24 ; λόγου δ. κατανοῆσαι Pl. Phd. 90c ; βίον τοῖς πλείστοις κοινωνῆσαι δ. Arist. Pol. 1295a30 ; κατὰ τὸ δυνατόν, quantum fieri possit, Pl. Cra. 422d, D. 3.6, etc. ; ἐς τὸ δ. Hdt. 3.24 ; εἰς ὅσον ἀνθρώπῳ δ. μάλιστα Pl. Phdr. 277a ; ἐκ τῶν δυνατῶν X. An. 4.2.23 ; ἐπὶ τὸ δ. Id. Cyn. 5.8 ; ἐν δυνατῷ εἶναι BCH 29.172 (Delos, ii BC) ; also ὅσον δυνατόν E. IA 997 ; ὅσον καθ’ ἡμᾶς δ. Id. Ba. 183 ; esp. with Sup., ὡς δ. πλεῖστον Isoc. 12.278 ; ὡς δ. κακίστους X. Mem. 4.5.5 ; γνώμη ὡς δ. δικαιοτάτη D. 24.13 ; τὰ δ. things which are practicable, Th. 5.89, cf. Arist. Rh. 1359b1. Adv. -τῶς strongly, powerfully, εἰπεῖν δ. Aeschin. 2.48 ; Sup. -ώτατα most ably, Pl. R. 516d. δ. ἔχει it is possible, Hdt. 7.11.
(sic), to be more capable of financial burdens, τινός PFlor. 296.37 (vi AD).
ἡμέρᾳ δωδεκάτῃ, Hsch.
ή, όν, potential, of the particle ἄν, κεν, ADysc. Synt. 205.5, 265.15, cf. Sch. E. Or. 379.

also δύω in Ep., Eleg. and late, SIG 1231 (Nicomedia, iii/iv AD), not in Ion. Inscrr. nor in Trag. (δύο ῥοπάς shd. be read in E. Hel. 1090), nor in Att. Prose or Inscrr. ; Lacon. acc. δύε IG 5(1).1 ; Thess. fem. δύας ib. 9 (2).517 ; gen. and dat. δυοῖν Hp. Vict. 1.3, but f.l. in Hdt. 1.11, 91 [used as monos. in S. OT 640, cf. δώδεκα for δυώδ -] ; later Att. also δυεῖν (esp. in fem. gen.) found in codd. of E. El. 536, cited fr. Th. by Ael. Dion. (?) Fr. 372, cf. 1.20 (cod. Laur.) ; Boeot. δουῖν Corinna Supp. 2.54 ; later δυσί, δυσὶν ἡμέραις Th. 8.101 codd., δυσὶν ἡμέρῃσι v.l. in Hp. Acut. (Sp.) 67 ; δυοῖν ὄμμασι καὶ δυσὶν ἀκοαῖς Arist. Pol. 1287b27, cf. Men. 699, SIG 344.26 (Teos, iv BC), etc. ; early Att. Inscrr. have δυοῖν IG1². 3.10, al., later δυεῖν SIG 2587.286, IG2². 463.78, al., from cent. iii on δυσί ib. 1028.27, al. ; Ion. gen. δυῶν GDI 5653d9 (Chios), Hdt. 1.94, 130, etc., dat. δυοῖσι ib. 32, 7.104 ; δυῶν also Dor., Leg. Gort. 1.40, Tab.Heracl. 1.139 ; δυοῖς Leg. Gort. 7.46. — Used indecl., like ἄμφω, by Hom. (who has no gen. or dat. δυοῖν), τῶν δύο μοιράων Il. 10.253 ; δύω κανόνεσσι 13.407, etc. ; so in Hdt. and Att., δύο νεῶν Hdt. 8.82 ; δύο ζεύγεσι Id. 3.130 ; δύο νεῶν Th. 3.89 ; δύο πλέθρων X. An. 3.4.9 ; with dual, δύο μναῖν dub.l. Id. Mem. 2.5.2 ; but not in Trag. and rare in Com., ἔτεσιν δύο Alex. 105 ; δὔ ἔτεσιν Damox. 2.3 ; not in Att. Inscrr. before the Roman period, IG 3.1443, al.
two, Il. 1.16, etc. ; in Hom., δύο and δύω are sts. joined with plural Nouns, δύο δ’ ἄνδρες 18.498, al. ; also in Trag., δύο κριούς S. Aj. 237 (lyr.) ; in Att. Prose, δύο τέχνας Pl. Grg. 464b ; but δυοῖν is rare with plural Nouns, ὀρθοστάταις δυοῖν IG 2.1054.64 ; ἕνα καὶ δύο one or two, a few, Il. 2.346 ; δὔ ἢ τρεῖς Ar. Pax 829, cf. X. HG 3.5.20 ; εἰς δύο two and two, Id. Cyr. 7.5.17 ; σὺν δύο two together, Il. 10.224, Hdt. 4.66 ; δύο ποιεῖν τὴν πόλιν to split the state into two, divide it, Arist. Pol. 1310a4.
coined as etym. of ζυγόν, Pl. Cra. 418d.
v. δυωδεκαδικός.
= δωδεκαπλάσιος, Bito 59.8.
v. δυωδεκάς.
τό, = δωδεκατημόριον, Paul.Al. K. 1.
v. δυώδεκα.
ές, of two forms, double, dual, λόγος Porph. VP 50 ; τὸ δ. τῆς ψυχῆς Herm. in Phdr. p. 167 A. Adv. -δῶς Dam. Pr. 55.
ὁ, or δυοκαιδεκάδελτον, τό, the Laws of the Twelve Tables, Lyd. Mag. 1.26, 42.
κύκλος zodiac, Vett.Val. 172.32.
ον, = δωδεκάμηνος, χρόνοι S. Tr. 648 (lyr.).
οἱ, αἱ, τά, twelve, Il. 2.557, etc.
ον, twelfth, Hp. Morb. 3.16, Epid. 7.5.
ή, όν, seventy-second, SIG 1011.21 (Chalcedon, iii/ii BC).
υ, of two and twenty cubits, Eust. 644.39.
ή, όν, twenty-second, IG1². 212, Archim. Aren. 4.
Dor. for δυοκαιπεντηκοστός.
ή, όν, Dor. δυοκαιπεντακοστός, fifty-second, Archim. Aren. 14.
(< δύο, ἥμισυ) two and a half, Supp.Epigr. 2.705 (Perga).
όν, making two, Arist. Metaph. 1083b36, Procl. in Prm. p. 548S.
ή, όν, second, τὸ δ. (sc. μόριον) answering the question ποστημόριον, i.e. half, Sch. E. Hec. 32.
= πωματίζει, Democr. 136.
πωμάσαι, Hsch.
ου, ὁ, diver, Call. Fr. 167, Oppian. H. 2.436 ; as Adj., κηρύλος Lyc. 387 ; of persons, Id. 73.

(lengthd. from δύω), duck, dive, ἠΰτε τις καύηξ δύπτῃσιν ἐς ἁλμυρὸν ὕδωρ Antim. Eleg. 6 (nisi leg. δύπτης); πρὸς κῦμα δυπτούσας Lyc. 715 ; without a Prep., ἔδυψε Νηρέως τάφους Id. 164 ; νειόθι δύψας ARh. 1.1326 ; c. acc., δύπτοντες κεφαλάς ib. 1008.
poet. for ὀδύρομαι.
ον, messenger of ill, Nonn. D. 20.184.
to be impious, IG 14.432 (Tauromenium).
ές, (< ἅγος) impious, opp. εὐαγής, Man. 5.180, Poll. 1.33.
poet. for δυσανακόμιστος.
poet. for δυσανάκριτος.
ον, unchaste, A. Supp. 751 (lyr.), Orac. ap. Luc. Alex. 54.
have bad sport in fishing, Plu. Ant. 29.
ές, unluckily caught, of fish, Oppian. H. 3.272.
ἡ, bad sport, Poll. 5.13.
ον, hard to guide, DH. 2.28, Luc. Abd. 3, 17 ; ἐπὶ τὸ καλόν DH. 9.8 ; of horses, Hippiatr. Praef.
ον, impregnable, Poll. 3.141, 5.79, 105.
ωνος, ὁ, ἡ, having seen hard service, Plu. Tim. 36.
ον, unhappy in one΄s brothers, A. Th. 871 (lyr., Sup.), Vett.Val. 18.5.
ον, laborious, Eust. 740.54.
ἡ, badness of air, Str. 5.1.7, Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.161 ; pl., fogs, Str. 4.1.8.
ον, having bad air, δεσμωτήριον (sc. ὁ κόσμος) D.Chr. 30.11 ; unwholesome, of the atmosphere, Procl. Par. Ptol. 122, cf. Sabin. ap. Orib. 9.20.8.

ές, (< ἄημι) ill-blowing, stormy, ἀνέμοιο δυσαέος Il. 5.865 ; Ζεφύροιο δ. 23.200, al. ; poet. gen. pl. δυσαήων for δυσαέων, Od. 13.99. generally, excessive, δ. κρυμός Call. Dian. 115 ; καῦμα QS. 13.134 ; κῦμα AP 7.739 (Phaedim.).
ill-smelling, of a seal, Opp. C. 3.114 ; φάρμακα Id. H. 4.662.
ον, most miserable, τροφαί S. OC 330, LXX 3 Ma. 4.4.
ον, most mournful, miserable, ib. 6.31.
ές, most melancholy, βοά A. Pers. 281 (lyr.).
ον, not clear, murky, ὄρφνη E. Heracl. 857.
ον, bleeding with difficulty, Aët. 8.44.
ον, of ill fame, Orph. A. 1340.
ατος, τό, riddle of woe, Sch. E. Ph. 45.
ον, hard to take, impregnable, Poll. 1.170.
ἡ, low degree of sensibility, Ti.Locr. 102e, Gal. 7.55 (pl.), prob. in Phld. Piet. 67.
to be hardly sensible, Alex.Trall. 1.13.
ον, insensible, σώματα Alex.Aphr. Pr. 1.72, cf. Adam. 1.7 ; τὸ δυσαίσθητον, = ἀναισθησία, Gal. 4.784. Pass., scarcely perceptible, Alex.Aphr. in Sens. 85.24 ; hard to trace, Poll. 5.12.
ον, hard to account for, Ph. 2.644, Gal. 13.605.
ωνος, ὁ, ἡ, most miserable, Trag. only lyr., A. Th. 926 (prob.), S. OC 151 ; αἰὼν δ. a life that is no life, E. Hel. 213 ; δ. ὁ βίος Id. Supp. 960.
ον, hard to heal, ἐκτρίμματα Hp. Fract. 29.
ές, = δυσάκεστος, Hsch. s.v. δυσηκῆ.
ατος, τό, severe pain, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.82.
ές, very painful, A. Ag. 1165, Plu. 2.106d, QS. 14.68.

ον, hard to be borne, most painful, Eup. 410.
unfeeling, hard-hearted, S. OT 12 ; δειλὸς ἢ δ. φρένας Id. Fr. 952.

ές, = δυσάλθητος, Hp. Art. 41, Cass. Pr. 1 (Comp.) ; τὸ τῆς φύσεως δ. Pl. Ax. 367b. Adv. -θῶς Philum. ap. Orib. 45.29.36.
deadly, Nic. Al. 12, 157, Luc. Dem. Enc. 13 ; neut. pl. as Adv., QS. 12.408.
ον, hard to cure, inveterate, QS. 9.388 (-άλθετος Hsch.).
ον, Dor. for δυσήλιος.
ον, hard to alter, Gal. Protr. 11 ; hard to digest, Hp. Alim. 49 ; χυμός Alex.Aphr. Pr. 1.83.
ον, hard to escape, Nic. Al. 251, 537, LXX Wi. 17.17, Man. 3.247.

ον, hard to catch or take, ἄγρα Pl. Ly. 206a (Comp.) ; of birds and fish, Arist. HA 615a17, 599b25 ; ἐρύματα Ph. 2.133.
hard to conquer, ἀρχά A. Pr. 167 (lyr.) ; πάθος Luc. Abd. 18 (Sup.) ; immune, τοῖς ἔξωθεν αἰτίοις δ. σῶμα Gal. 4.742 ; πρὸς νόσους Sor. 1.32 (Comp.) ; c. gen., δ. κακῶν beyond reach of ills, S. OC 1723 (lyr.).
hard to comprehend, Pl. Ti. 51a (Sup.).
ον, making unfortunate mistakes, Vett.Val. 11.16.
ον, poet. for δυσανάβατος, πέτραι Simon. 58.2.
Dor. for δυσημερία.
ον, most miserable, Il. 19.315, 22.428, 485, ARh. 2.218.
ον, hard to climb, Corn. ND 14.
prob. f.l. for δυσαναβλυστέω, well up with difficulty, Plu. 2.688e.
ον, hard to read, prob. <ανά> for δύσγνωστος, Plb. 3.32.1.
ον, hard to throw up, ὑγρά Dsc. 1.1, cf. Androm. ap. Gal. 13.28.
ον, hard to assimilate, Diph. Siph. ap. Ath. 3.91e, Gal. 19.364, Hippiatr. 1.
ον, hard to evaporate, Artem. 1.1.
ον, hard to cleanse, ἕλκωσις Gal. ap. Orib. Syn. 9.3.8.

ον, hard to call back, Plu. 2.74e ; J. BJ 2.18.8 (but simply, hard to summon, call together, Plu. Thes. 24), etc.
hard to restore, of hysterics, Sor. 2.29 (Comp.), cf. Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.74 ; or to good spirits, Max.Tyr. 33.6. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν to be hard to restore to one΄s senses, Dsc. Alex. 16.
ον, hard to carry upwards, ψυχή Plu. Rom. 28 ; — poet. δυσαγκόμιστος, hard to recall, αἷμα A. Eu. 262 (lyr.).
ον, hard to mix or temper, κοινωνία Plu. 2.1024d.
ον, hard to determine ; poet. δυσάγκριτος, πόνοι A. Supp. 126 (lyr.).

ον, hard to recover, μνήμη Alcid. Soph. 19.
hard to recover from, ἀρρωστία Jul. Or. 6.181a. Adv. -λήπτως, ἔχειν to be in a bad way for recovery, Ruf. ap. Orib. 8.47.4. of an athlete, unable to return to ordinary habits, Ath.Med. ap. Orib. inc. 1.6.
ἡ, difficult convalescence, Vett.Val. 236.17.
ον, hard to analyse, Porph. in Cat. 132.9. Adv. -τως Simp. in Cat. 212.16.
ον, hard to destroy, consume, στοιχεῖον Ph. 2.505.
ον, restless, Eust. 1296.58.
ον, hard to convince, Pl. Prm. 135a.
ουν, hard to sail up, ὁ Ῥοδανός Str. 4.1.14.
ον, = δυσανάπλους, Str. 5.2.5.

ον, offensive to inhalation, Arist. Sens. 443b12.
transpiring with difficulty, Gal. 7.287.
ον, hard to pass, Ph. 1.672, 2.118.
ον, hard to restore, Alex.Trall. Febr. 7.
ον, hardly recovering from an illness, Hp. Alim. 28.
bear ill, Th. 7.71 ; to be greatly vexed, ἐπί τινι, πρός τι, Plu. Cam. 35, Plb. 16.12.5 ; περί τινος Phalar. Ep. 37 ; τοῖς γενομένοις J. AJ 13.16.2 ; abs., Eus. Mynd. 59, Aët. 8.44.

ον, hard to bear, intolerable, ὕβρεις Ph. 2.92 ; κήδη Phleg. Macr. 4, cf. Dsc. Eup. 1.235, Porph. Abst. 3.20 ; poet. δυσάνσχετος ARh. 2 272. Act., bearing hardly, in Adv. -τως, ἔχειν ADysc. Synt. 218.9, cf. Poll. 3.130.
ον, hard to overthrow, δύναμις Plu. Caes. 4, cf. Gal. 18(1).604.
δυσκόλως ἀναφερόμενος, Hsch.
ἡ, (< ἀνήρ) want of men, App. BC 1.7.
ον, = δυσανάσχετος 1, interpol. in X. Mem. 2.2.8, cf. Gal. 7.181. Adv. -τως Poll. 3.130.
ον, Dor. for δυσήνεμος, S. Ant. 591 (lyr.).
ές, shy of flowering, Poll. 1.231.

ον, (< ἀνία) soon vexed, ill to please, Antipho Soph. 89, Critias Fr. 42 D., Men. 803 (but better -ήνιον) ; opp. εὔθυμος, Arist. Phgn. 805b6 ; vexed, annoyed, in Comp. -ιώτερος Phld. Acad. Ind. p. 50 M.
ῶσα, ῶν, (< ἀνιάω) much vexing, Plu. 2.106d.
ον, hard to open, πυξίδες Diog. Ep. 50.
ον, strengthd. for ἄνολβος, Emp. 124.
ον, poet. for δυσανάσχετος.
ον, hard to struggle against, Paus. 1.17.6, DL. 2.134, Jul. Or. 1.34b.

or δυσαντής, ές, = δυσάντητος Ι, φῦλα Opp. C. 3.262 ; μῆνις Nonn. D. 42.380. = δυσάντητος ΙΙ, κύματα ib. 6.310, cf. Musae. 324.
hard to climb, ὁδός Ph. 1.255 ; κολῶναι Opp. C. 4.432.

ον,
I. disagreeable to meet, boding of ill, opp. εὐάντητος, Luc. Tim. 5, etc.
IΙ. hard to withstand, πάθη Plu. 2.118c ; ὀδύναι Procl. H. 3.5 ; κακά Max.Tyr. 5.3.

ον, hard to look in the face, Plu. Marc.. 23 ; -βλεπτον στίλβειν ἀπὸ τῶν ὀμμάτων Corn. ND 20 ; hard to face, ἀπορία χαλεπωτάτη καὶ δ. Syrian. in Metaph. 178.30 ; hard to vie with, Philostr.Jun. Im. Praef. ; ὠφέλεια Agathin. ap. Orib. 10.7.6.
ον, hard to gainsay, DH. 5.18 ; metaph, ἐπιθυμία J. AJ 18.9.5.
ον, = δυσαντίλεκτος, gloss on ἐχυρόν, Hsch., EM 406.7. Adv. δυσαντιρρήτως Plb. 9.31.7.
ον, hard to resist, Plb. 22.8.13.
γάμος marriage with a bad husband, A. Supp. 1064.
ον, inexorable, Sch. S. OT 334.
ον, hard to wipe out, Sch. S. Tr. 682.
ἡ, the quality of being difficult to get rid of, persistency, Pl. Phlb. 46c.

ον, hard to get rid of, νοῦσος Hp. Nat. Mul. 40 ; ὀδύναι S. Tr. 959 (lyr.) ; πρόσταγμα Isoc. 10.28 ; ἀρρώστημα Arist. PA 671b9, cf. Cat. 10a4 ; c. gen., δυσαπαλλακτότεραι τῶν ἐμβρύων having difficulty in bringing forth, Id. HA 587b1 ; δ. ἀπὸ λόγου a person hard to draw away from…, Pl. Tht. 195c. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν τινός Eust. 1389.46, cf. Eustr. in EN 140.18.
ον, = δυσάντητος, Eust. 1054.30, Suid.
v. δυσάπιστος.
ον, very disobedient, AP 12.179 (Strato) ; — hence δυσαπαπιστέω, AB 1285.
v.l. for δυσυποβίβαστος, Gal. 6.535.
ον, hard to get rid of, πυρετός Alex.Aphr. Febr. 19 ; hard to cast away, Olymp. in Alc. p. 51 C. ; hard to lose, Id. in Cat. 116.25, cf. Ammon. in Cat. 82.8, Simp. in Cat. 228.23.
ον, hard to demonstrate, Pl. R. 488a.
ον, hard to unlearn, J. AJ 16.2.4.
ον, hard to drive away, Sch. Theoc. 10.11.
ον, hard to render or define, S.E. M. 7.242, Bacch. Harm. 95.
ον, hard to put aside, πάθος Olymp. in Alc. p. 101 C.
εως, ἡ, difficulty of recovering, mortal sickness, Erot. s.v. δυσθεσίην.

ον, hard to restore, M.Ant 11.8, Gal. 14.792.
hard to recover from, ὀργαί Phld. Ir. p. 63 W.
Adv. with difficulty in bending, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.90.
ον, hard to answer, Luc. Vit. Auct. 22. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν, of a letter, Mithr. Ep. 1. Act., hardly answering, Paul.Aeg. 3.9.
ον, hard to catch, Alex.Aphr. in Sens. 26.18 ; irreparable, Gloss.
ον, hard to defend or excuse, Plb. 1.10.4, cf. Ph. 1.562, J. AJ 16.4.2 ; hard to answer, Aristeas 213 ; hard to explain, Str. 4.1.7. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν Eust. 147.23.
ον, hard to get free of, δ. πάθος τὸ φιλότιμον Olymp. in Alc. p. 51 C. Adv. -τως Erot. s.v. βλακεύειν, Gal. 8.284.
ον, hard to wash off or out, Zen. 1.47, Sch. E. Ph. 63 ; Comp., Theol.Ar. 22.
ον, not apt to fall off, καρπός Thphr. CP 1.11.8.

ον, hard to tear away, Posidon. 15 J., Secund. Sent. 10, Dsc. 3.14. Adv. δυσαποσπάστως, ἔχειν Pl. Ax. 365b, Aristeas 123, DS. 20.51.
from which it is hard to tear oneself away, Ph. 2.11, 14 ; κάλλος Charito 5.8.
ον, hard to abstain from, S.E. M. 9.152.
ον, hard to accomplish, Eust. 1956.18.
ον, hard to dissuade, refractory, X. Mem. 4.1.4, Aristaenet. 1.28.
ον, hard to rub off and so get rid of, ὀνείδη Macar. 8.47, cf. Ph. 1.459, 615 (Sup.), Thessal. ap. Gal. 10.252 ; of persons, Plu. 2.55e.
ον, difficult to avert, ἄτη IG 2.1660.22.
ον, hard to cicatrize, Dsc. 4.41, Aët. 1.243, Hippiatr. 26 ; Comp., Phlp. in APo. 182.13.
δυσφροντίστῳ, Hsch.
incorrect form for δυσαρεστούμενος, Hsch.

suffer annoyance, Arist. HA 560b24 ; to be displeased, τινί at a thing, Plb. 4.22.9, DS. 5.9, J. AJ 8.5.3, Aq., Sm., Thd. Ps. 94 (95).10 ; δ. ὅτι DH. Comp. 11 ; Medic., suffer malaise, Gal. 10.551, Aët. 5.5 ; — also Med., τινί Plb. 5.94.2 ; ἐπί τινι Il. 28.11. c. dat. pers., to be displeasing to, Id. 7.5.6, DS. 18.62 ; τῷ θεῷ Ph. 2.6 ; — also Med. δυσαρεστουμένη φιλία Plu. 2.94d, cf. Iamb. VP 35.255.
ατος, τό, Medic., malaise, distress, Antyll. ap. Stob. 4.37.15, Sor. 1.26.

εως, ἡ, distress, Pl. Ax. 366d ; dissatisfaction, τινί or ἐπί τινι, Plb. 4.21.7, 23.7.5.
Medic., malaise, Cael.Aur. TP 3.6, Sor. 1.56.
ἡ, distress, malaise, Herod.Med. in Hermes 40.584, prob. in Aët. 16.18 (for -ησίαι), Hierocl. in CA 11 p. 442M.
ή, όν, distressing, σύμπτωμα Herod.Med. ap. Orib. 6.20.21.

ον, hard to appease, implacable, δαίμονες A. Eu. 928 ; ill-pleased, τι at a thing, Luc. Nav. 46 ; ill to please, fastidious, peevish, δυσάρεστον οἱ νοσοῦντες E. Or. 232, cf. Isoc. 1.31, 12.8, X. Mem. 3.13.3 (Comp.), Diph. 63, Nicostr. 31 (Comp.), Plu. 2.128d ; ἀνοίας νόσημα δυσάρεστον Polystr. Herc. 1520.1 ; τὸ δ. displeasure, Plu. Sol. 25. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν πρός τι Id. 2.476b.
ον, hard to count up, App. BC 2.73.
ἡ, unhappy mother of the noblest son, as Thetis calls herself, Il. 18.54.
ον, hard to govern, φρένες A. Ch. 1024 ; στρατόπεδα J. AJ 4.2.1 ; οὐδὲν ἀνθρώπου δυσαρκτότερον Plu. Luc. 2 ; ἔθνος δυσαρκτότατον App. BC 2.149.
ἡ, disharmony, ἠθῶν Plu. Aem. 5.
ον, ill-united, Plu. Eum. 13 ; insecure, πύργος App. Mith. 34.
ἡ, ill discipline, App. BC 5.17.
ές, blinding, Poet. de herb. 65.
δυσεγκλήμων, Hsch.
ἡ, ill or hard lodging, A. Ag. 555 (pl.), Ph. 1.195 (pl.).
ἡ, dub.sens., St.Byz. s.v. αὐλή (expld. as compd. of Αὖλις).
gloss on δύσαυλος¹, Hsch.
ἔρις an unhappy contest with the flute (< αὐλός), AP 9.266 (Antip.).
ον, (αὐλή) bad for lodging, inhospitable, of frost, S. Ant. 356 (lyr.).
ές, hardly or slowly growing, Arist. Aud. 802a25, Thphr. CP 1.8.4, J. AJ 3.1.3 ; — also δυσαύξητος, ον, Thphr. CP 1.8.2.
= δυσαυξής.
ἡ, stormy wind, Ar.Byz. Epit. 24.18 (s.v.l.).
ές, idly boasting, vain-glorious, ARh. 3.976.
ον, hard to take away, Arist. EN 1095b26 ; hard to remove, of an application, Gal. 12.356.
ές, hard to the touch, σάρξ Gal. 6.100.
[ῠσᾰ] ές, (< ἄχος) most painful, πάθος A. Eu. 145 (lyr.).
[ῠσᾱ] ές, Dor. for δυσηχής, πόλεμος Anacr. 107.
ές, very grievous, Tryph. 42, Max. 308.
δυσκατανόητος, βάρνακα γὰρ ἄγρια λάχανα δύσπλυτα EM 291.45.
gloss on ἀβασανίστως, Hsch.
ον, intolerable, grievous to be borne, LXX Pr. 27.3, Ev. Matt. 23.4, Plu. 2.915f, etc. ; of persons, Antisth. ap. Ph. 2.449.
make impassable, dub.l. in X. Eq. Mag. 8.9 (prob. for δύσβατα ποιούμενον).

ον, hard to traverse, impassable, ἀμαχανίαι Pi. N. 7.97 ; τόπος Pl. R. 432c ; τὰ δ., = δυσχωρίαι, X. Cyr. 2.4.27 ; metaph, δ. καὶ μακρὰ διερμήνευσις Iamb. Myst. 5.5.
trodden in sorrow, Περσὶς αἶα A. Pers. 1069 (lyr.).
or δυσβηρής, ές, = δύσβατος, Hsch., EM 291.43.
ον, = δυσβίοτος, AB 323.
ον, making life wretched, πενίη AP 7.648 (Leon.).
see badly, Hsch. s.v. κικυμώττειν.
ον, hard to help or cure, Hp. Coac. 491, DS. 3.47, 11.15, Paul.Aeg. 5.29 ; Comp., Dsc. Eup. 2.159. Adv. -τως Gal. 5.122.
ον, throwing badly, esp. with dice, Poll. 9.94.
ον, ill-advised, EM 3.51.
ἡ, ill counsel, A. Th. 802, Ag. 1609, S. Ant. 95 ; pl., ib. 1269 (lyr.).
ον, hard to deal with, Cratin. 404 ; cf. βρακεῖν.
ον, of ill soil, unfruitful, γῆ Hom. Epigr. 7 ; χθών AP 7.401 (Crin.).
to be unhappily married, Heph.Astr. 1.1.
ἡ, an ill marriage, Man. 1.19.
ον, ill-wedded, γάμοι δ. E. Ph. 1047 (lyr.) ; ῥυστάγματα Lyc. 1089, cf. Paul.Al. N. 2 ; δύσγαμον αἶσχος ἑλών, of Menelaus, E. Tr. 1114 ; χελιδών Luc. Trag. 49.
ι, very ticklish, skittish, ἵππος X. Eq. 3.10, cf. Ar. Fr. 43, Ael. NA 16.9 ; — also δυσγαργάλιστος, ον, prob. l. in Gp. 16.2.1, cf. Tim.Gaz. 148.3.
ον, = δυσγάργαλις.
ον, Lib. Ep. 234.1 codd., Phryn. PS p. 65 B.

ἡ, low birth, S. OT 1079, E. IA 446, Pl. R. 618d (pl.), Cerc. 17.36, Plu. 2.1b, etc.
meanness, E. HF 663 (lyr.), Plu. Alex. 62.

ές, low-born, E. Ion 1477, Ar. Ra. 1219, etc. ; Comp., Men. 533.10.
low-minded, mean, E. El. 363, etc. ; δ. ὢν τῷ τρόπῳ Com. ap. Stob. 4.30.6a.
ον, hard to make a bridge over, Str. 4.3.3.
ον, hard to till or cultivate, Str. 17.3.25.
ἡ, ignorance, doubt, E. HF 1107.
gloss on δυσέκτων (sic), Suid.
ον, hard to recognize, Gal. 7.804, al., Poll. 5.150. Adv. -τως ib. 160.
ἡ, difficulty of knowing, δυσγνωσίαν εἶχον προσώπου I did not know thy face, E. El. 767.

ον, hard to understand, Pl. Alc. 2.147c.
hard to recognize, τισί Plb. 3.78.4 ; Sup., Aen.Tact. 25.2.
ον, hard to seduce by enchantments, Pl. R. 413e.
ον, conceiving with difficulty, Vett.Val. 18.24, Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.207.

ον, hard to write, Aristid. 2.360 J.
unlearned, Philostr. VS 2.1.10.
ον, very grasping, Lib. Bas. Ep. 13.
ἀποδύω, Hsch.
to be wretched, Longin. 9.7.
ἡ, misery, E. IT 1120 (lyr.), And. 2.7.

ον, gen. ονος, ill-starred, unhappy, πότμος Emp. 9.4, A. Th. 827, S. Ant. 274 ; μοῖρα Id. OT 1302 (anap.) ; τύχη Pl. Lg. 905c ; νέρτεροι Ti.Locr. 104d ; of a person, BGU 1024 vii 24 (iv AD) ; Comp. -έστερος And. 2.9. Adv. -νως Eust. 1064.44.

ον, sorely wept, A. Ag. 442 (lyr.).
IΙ. Act., sorely weeping, AP 12.80 (Mel.) ; δάκρυα δ. tears of anguish, ib. 7.476 (Id.).
αρτος, ὁ, ἡ, ill-wedded, A. Ag. 1319.
ον, hard to subdue ; hence, hard to work, σίδηρος Sch. Hes. Sc. 122.
ον, hard to prove, θεωρήματα Gal. 15.139.
ον, = δυσδερκής, Opp. C. 2.607.

ές, ill to look upon, grim, ugly, Opp. C. 3.263, H. 1.47.
hard to see, faint, ἴχνη Id. C. 1.102, cf. 451.
ιδος, ὁ, ἡ, (< δηλέομαι) baneful, Hsch.
δύσνους, κακὰ βουλευομένους, Hsch.
ι, gen. ιος, hard to fight with, Nic. Th. 738.
ον, hard to get through, ποταμός Aen.Tact. 8.1, cf. X. An. 6.5.19 ; τόποι Plb. 1.39.13 ; ῥεῦμα DS. 17.93.
δυσδιαγνω<σ>τικός, ή, όν, τὸ δ. the difficulty in diagnosis, Alex.Trall. 8.2.
ον, hard to distinguish, Cic. Att. 5.44.1, DH. 2.71, Gal. 9.433, etc.
ον, unpleasant to live in, πόλις Str. 16.2.23 ; Comp., Ptol. Tetr. 168.

ον, hard to dispose of (in marriage), χαλεπόν γε θυγάτηρ κτῆμα καὶ δυσδιάθετον Men. 18.
hard to manage or settle, Plu. Caes. 11, DC. 73.15, Hierocl. in CA 11 p. 438M.
ον, hard to divide or split, Arist. Pr. 928a29, Thphr. HP 7.11.3, Sor. 1.118, Theol.Ar. 5.
ον, hard to decide, Plu. Comp. Cim. Luc. 3 ; λόγος Porph. Abst. 2.1.
ον, hard to carry through, Hsch.
ον, hard to pierce, Ael. NA 17.44.

ον, hard to distinguish, Str. 13.4.12, Clytus 1 ; ἀξίαι Plu. 2.617 d ; δ. ἀπό… Corn. ND 31. of litigants, whose case is hard to decide, DS. 33.28a.
hard to digest, Xenocr. 9.
ον, hard to reconcile, Suid. Adv. -τως Ammon. 63.

ον, hard to dissolve, Arist. Pr. 870b31 (Comp.) ; σχῆμα τῆς τάξεως Plb. 1.26.16.
hard to digest, Philotim. ap. Ath. 2.53f, Gal. 16.760.
hard to reconcile, Arist. EN 1126a20.
ον, hard to understand, Sch. E. Ph. 30.
ον, hard to open, ὀφθαλμός Hippiatr. 1.

ον, slow to evaporate, Thphr. CP 1.2.4, Dsc. 5.6.
slow to perspire, Herod.Med. ap. Orib. 5.27.3.
ον, hard to break, τάξις Plb. 15.15.7 ; hard to pull up, of a palisade, Ph.Mech. Bel. 82.35.
to be unstable, dub. in Plu. 2.993e.
ον, hard to separate, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.90.
ον, hard to soften, prob. l., Thphr. CP 2.15.2.
or δυσδιάφυκτος, ον, hard to escape, Suid., Hsch. (-διαφύ[λα]κτον cod.).
ον, hard to break up, τὰ δ. βραδυπεψίας ἐργάζεται Gal. 7.209.
ἡ, difficulty of dissipation, Cass. Pr. 66.

ον, hard to disperse or dissipate, Gal. 11.119.
hardly evaporating, Id. 10.657 ; not excreting readily, Id. 17(1).188 ; διάθεσις Alex.Trall. 8.2 ; cf. δυσδιαχώρητος.
= δυσδιάφευκτος.
v. δυσδιάφευκτος.
ον, indigestible, Arist. Pr. 927b21 (Comp.) ; hard to pass, prob. for -φόρητος, Xenocr. 34. Act., costive, Alex.Aphr. Pr. 1.90, Sever. p. 6 D.
ον, hard to instruct, Hp. Ep. 17.
ον, hard to be roused from, καταφορά Gal. 19.413, cf. Herod. (?) Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.77.
ον, hard to pass, βίος Porph. Abst. 4.18.
ον, hard to get through, v.l. in DS. 3.44.
ον, = δυσδιέξοδος ΙΙ, Hippiatr. 69.

ον,
I. hard to get through, traverse, DS. 5.34, DC. 60.20.
IΙ. hard to pass, Gal. 6.535.
ον, hard to search thoroughly, Pl. R. 432c, DC. 51.26, Them. Or. 21.254d.
ον, hard to narrate, LXX Wi. 17.1.
ον, = δυσδιήλυτος, Hsch. ; of a child΄s tissues, Sor. 1.95.
ον, hard to pass through, Plb. 3.61.3, etc.

ον, hard to manage, J. BJ 2.16.4, Poll. 5.105 (vulg. -ητικός).
hard to digest, Xenocr. 31, Sor. 1.93.
ον, hard to see one΄s way in, τόπος διὰ τὸ σκοτεινόν Alcin. Intr. 35.
ον, hard to set right, Hsch.
ον, hard to delimit, ἀπ’ ἀλλήλων S.E. M. 5.74 ; hard to distinguish, φαντασία ib. 7.416.
ον, gloss on δύσσοα, Sch. Theoc. 4.45.
ον, hard to test, τῇ γεύσει Dsc. 3.82.
ον, = ἄδωρος, Oppian. H. 3.303.
τοῦ τοίχου τὰ πέριξ (Cypr.), Hsch.
ον, hard to wake, Gal. 16.645, Paul.Aeg. 3.9.
ον, hard to sustain, S.E. M. 9.152.
v. δυσαύλητος.
ον, hard to take in hand, J. AJ 15.11.2.
ον, hard to dam up, prob. in Str. 16.1.10.

ον, bringing evil in one΄s abode, A. Ag. 746 (lyr.).
fitting ill, awry, DH. Comp. 6.
ἡ, ugliness, DL. 2.33.

ές, unshapely, ugly, Hdt. 6.61, S. Fr. 88.9, Pl. Sph. 228a, Agatharch. 74 ; of sounds, ἧττον δ. τοῦ ε τὸ ο DH. Comp. 14.
difficult to discern, τὸ δ. τῆς οὐσίας Procl. Theol.Plat. 5.23.
ον, hard to make out, of Thucydides’ style, DH. Lys. 4, cf. Luc. Icar. 4.
ον, unyielding, stiff, Paul.Aeg. 2.11.21.
to wear mean clothes, Plu. 2.299e.
ον, meanly clad, E. El. 1107.
ἡ, mean clothing, Sch. E. Hec. 240.
ον, gen. ονος, ill-clad, Ps.-Hes. ap. Ath. 3.116a.
ἡ, difficulty in rowing, Suid.
ον, hard to enter or invade, of Laconia, E. Fr. 1083, cf. Aen.Tact. 16.17 ; of a river, Str. 4.1.8 ; Sup. -ώτατος, ον, least accessible, of Locris, Th. 3.101.
ον, difficult to enter, σπήλαιον TAM 2 (1).174 C 13 (Sidyma).
ουν, gen. ου, hard to sail into, Str. 4.1.8.
ον, = δυσείσπλους, prob. l. for δυσεκπλωτος, Sch. Th. 3.2.
ον, hard to get out of, DC. 56.19, Nonn. D. 45.269 (but f.l. for δυσέμβατος, φλόξ 2.487).
ον, hard to overpower, ἐπιθυμίαι Plu. 2.127a, cf. Cor. 2, Eun. VS p. 500 B.
ον, hard to endure, intolerable, Gal. 19.2.
ον, hard to escape, Nic. Al. 14.
ον, hard to shake off, Hsch. s.v. νήδυμον.
ον, hard to warm, Plu. 2.625a, Gal. 6.608, Antyll. ap. Orib. 10.13.9. Adv. -τως Id. ib. 10.29.3, Gal. 10.674.
ον, hard to avert by sacrifice, σημεῖα Plu. Crass. 18.
ον, hard to wash away, DH. 4.24.
ον, hard to evacuate, Gal. 8.192.
ον, hard to carry out, Hsch. and Suid. s.v. δυσέξοιστον.
ον, hard to digest and pass, Diph. Siph. ap. Ath. 2.69e, Xenocr. 38. Adv. -τως, ἀθροίζεσθαι Gal. UP 10.10. Act., excreting with difficulty, γαστέρες Id. 6.462.
ον, hard to disturb, shake, φυλακή S.E. M. 7.23.
ον, hard to express, Cic. Att. 5.10.3 (prob.), DH. Lys. 11.
ον, hard to escape from, Plu. 2.829b.
Adv. dub. in Gal. Anim. Pass. 1.5 (leg. δυσεξάλειπτον).
ον, hard to calculate, Suid.
ον, hard to undo, τέχνημα A. Fr. 375 (Dind. δυσέκδυτον hard to escape from) ; δόξα Ph. 1.192, cf. Vett.Val. 71.23, al. Adv. -τως indissolubly, A. Pr. 60.
ον, hard to dislodge, of disease, Antyll. ap. Orib. 10.29.3.
ον, hard to suck out, Sor. 1.87.
ον, hard to swim out of, Max.Tyr. 17.10.

ον, hard to wash out, Pl. R. 378d, Trag.Adesp. in Gött.Nachr. 1922.26, Cerc. 3, Ach.Tat. 6.11, Porph. Abst. 4.20 ; μῖσος Them. Or. 21.249c. Adv. δυσέκτως Gal. 8.36, al.
hard to cleanse, ὀδόντες Ael. NA 1.48.
ον, hard to pass out from, hard to escape, E. Hipp. 678 (lyr.), 883 (lyr., v.l. δυσεκπέραντος).
ον, hard to terrify, ὑπὸ φόβων Arist. VV 1250a7.
ον, hardly realizable, Phld. D. 1.12.
ον, tangled, inextricable, Gloss.
ουν, hard to sail out of, Plb. 34.2.5, Str. 1.2.15.

ον, hard to wash out, Ph. 2.182, 487, Plu. 2.488b.
hard to cleanse, ὀδόντες Ael. NA 1.48 ; metaph, ψυχαί Ph. 1.558.
ον, hard to breathe out, Sch. E. Ph. 1438.
ον, τιμωρίας καὶ πόνους δυσ[εκπο]νήτους hard to endure, Phld. Herc. 1251.12 (dub. rest.).
ον, hard to get out of, πύλαι Ph.Mech. Bel. 79.25 ; τέλμα J. AJ 13.2.4.
ον, not easily dislocated, Paul.Aeg. 6.114.
ον, hard to bring to suppuration, Gal. 11.119, Paul.Aeg. 4.18.
ον, hard to extirpate, πλάνη Ph. Fr. 105 H.
ον, not easily displaced. Adv. -τως Orib. 49.22.17.
ον, hard to wash out, Xenocr. 58.
ον, hard to melt, dub. in Hp. Alim. 51.
ον, hard to escape from, Tim. Pers. 130, Theodect. 10, Plb. 1.77.7, Man. 4.477 ; hardly escaping, Tim. Pers. 140. Adv. δυσεκφύκτως APl. 4.198 (Maec.).
ον, = δυσέκφορος, DH. Comp. 22.
ον, hard to pronounce or utter, Phld. Po. 994 Fr. 22, 1676.8, DH. Comp. 12, 16 (Sup.) ; λαλιά Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.167. Adv. -ρως, δ. καὶ τραχέως λαλεῖν Str. 14.2.28.
ον, hard to pronounce, Eust. 76.33.
ον, hard to refute, of persons or arguments, Str. 1.2.1 (Comp.), 11.6.4, Luc. Pisc. 17.
ἡ, ill-starred Helen, E. Or. 1388 (lyr.) ; cf. Δύσπαρις.
ον, hard to undo, Eust. 229.38 ; hard to unroll and read, βίβλοι Jul. Or. 7.227b.
ές, unfavourable for the healing of sores, of a constitution, opp. εὐελκής, Hp. Acut. 46, cf. Morb. 2.52, Gal. 10.387.
ἡ, the constitution of a δυσελκής, Hp. Epid. 2.10 (pl.).
incorrect spelling for δυσελπιστέω, Plb. 16.33.1, 21.13.2.
ι, gen. ιδος, hardly hoping, despondent, A. Ch. 412 (lyr.), Hp. Nat. Mul. 41 (prob.), X. HG 5.44.31, Arist. Rh. 1390a4 ; δ. τι ἐρεῖν Luc. Herm. 69. Pass., hardly hoped for, νίκη Onos. 38.2.
to have scarce a hope, τοῖς ὅλοις, ἐπὶ ταῖς βοηθείαις, Plb. 2.10.8, 4.60.4 ; — Pass., to be despaired of, Epicur. Sent.Vat. 17.
ἡ, despondency, Arist. VV 1251b25, Plb. 1.39.14, Teles p. 35 H., Ph. 1.119, App. BC 4.12.

ον, = δύσελπις, Lyr.Adesp. 138, Epicur. Fr. 470, Plu. Fab. 17. Adv. δυσελπίστως, ἔχειν Plb. 1.87.1.
unhoped for, ἐκ δυσελπίστων unexpectedly, X. Cyr. 6.1.47, cf. Vett.Val. 124.25.
ον, hard to walk on, rugged, τοῦ χωρίου τὸ δ. Th. 4.10 ; inaccessible, οἰωνοῖσι DP. 1150.
ον, hard to set, of dislocations, Hp. Art. 71.

ον, = δυσέμβλητος, Hp. Fract. 38 (Comp.).
hard to enter, δυσεμβολωτάτη ἡ Λακωνική X. HG 6.5.24 ; δ. τοῖς πολεμίοις [χώρα] Arist. Pol. 1326b41 ; ὄρη Plb. 3.49.7, cf. J. AJ 17.2.1.
not to vomit easily, Philum. ap. Aët. 9.23.
ές, hard to make to vomit, Gal. 17 (2).329, prob. l. in Dsc. 4.153 ; cf. δυσημής.
ον, hard to burn, Ph.Mech. Bel. 82.23.
ον, not easily falling into a thing, Nicom. Harm. 11, Gal. 5.433. Adv. -τως Nicom. Harm. 4.
ον, hard to way-lay, App. Hisp. 88.
ἡ, lassitude, Dsc. 5.49.
ον, sluggish, Sch. Ar. Pl. 313. of food, badly digested, Sor. 1.34.
ἡ, dysentery, Hp. Aph. 3.12 (pl.), al., Hdt. 8.115, Pl. Ti. 86a (pl.), Arist. Pr. 861b16, etc.
suffer from dysentery, Hippiatr. 39, Alex.Trall. 9.3.
ή, όν, afflicted with dysentery, Hp. Coac. 451, Arr. Epict. 2.21.22, Mnesith. ap. Orib. 4.4.4 ; liable to it, Plu. 2.101c ; δ. πάθη Epicur. Fr. 138 ; τὰ δ. Dsc. 1.51.
τό, late form of δυσεντερία, Act. Ap. 28.8, Moeris 129.
ες, ill with dysentery, Hp. Epid. 1.5, 3.8 ; symptomatic of or belonging to it, ib. 3.17. θ’ ; τρόπος Aret. SD 2.9.
ον, suffering from dysentery, Nic. Al. 382.

ον, unpleasant to meet, physically repulsive, δ. καὶ ἀηδής Thphr. Char. 19 ; but more usu.
unpleasant to deal with, Plb. 5.34.4, Plu. 2.27e ; τὸ δ. Ph. 2.520, J. AJ 13.2.1.
ἡ, repulsive demeanour, DS. 19.9, Cass. Pr. 80 (pl.).
ον, (< ἑνόω) hard to unite, M.Ant 11.8.
ον, difficult to carry off or get rid of, Hp. Insomn. 89, Arist. Pr. 871a19 (Comp.).
ον, difficult to hear, τὰ διὰ φωνῆς (sc. παραγγέλματα) Ael. Tact. 35.3.
ον, hard to wipe out, εὔνοια Plb. 39.3.1 ; συνήθεια DS. 3.6 ; μνήμη Longin. 7.3 ; ψυχῆς διάθεσις Corn. Rh. p. 353 H.
ον, hard to avoid, Hsch.
ον, = δυσανάλωτος, Hp. Alim. 49.
ον, hard to deceive, Pl. R. 413c, X. Ages. 11.12.

ον, hard to unbind, ψυχὴ δ. hard to loose from the bonds of the body, Plu. Rom. 28.
hard to kindle, χυμός Gal. 7.341, cf. Steph. in Hp. 1.284 D.
ον, hard to count, Plb. 3.58.6, Plu. 2.667e.
ον, hard to evaporate, Gal. 14.776.
v. δυσεξίλλητος.

ον, hard to refute, Pl. Phd. 85c (Sup.), Ptol. Tetr. 164.
hard to discover, φάρμακα DH. 3.5.
ον, hard to get out of, Tz. H. 11.556.
ον, hard to unfold, involved, πλοκή DH. Th. 29, cf. Amm. 2.2, Plu. Brut. 13 ; δυσεξέλικτα κυματούμενος κλύδων Luc. Trag. 25 ; twisted, contorted, ὀδόντες Ael. NA 14.8.
ον, hard to work out, Eust. 1394.7.
ον, hard to explore, Arist. Pol. 1330b26.
ον, hard to find out, Arist. HA 611a26, Plu. 2.407f.
ον, hard to explain, Darius ap. DL. 9.13, Gal. 17 (2).71.
ον, hard to tame, Plu. Art. 25.
ον, indissoluble, δεσμός E. Hipp. 1237.
ον, hard to appease, πένθη Plu. 2.609f.
ον, hard to unravel, Cic. Att. 5.10.3 (s.v.l.). Adv., in form δυσεξειλήτως, v.l. in Sch. Theoc. 14.51.
ον, not easily perishing, ἄνθος φαρμάκων Str. 11.8.7, cf. Plu. 2.696d, Philum. Ven. 4.3.
ον, = δυσέξιτος, Hsch., EM 238.42.
ον, hard to get out of, DS. 3.44 (v.l. δυσδιεξίτητος).
ον, = δυσδιέξοδος, Procl. Par. Ptol. 153.

ον, hard to get out of, Arist. Pol. 1330b26, Lyc. 1099, Paus. 2.31.1 ; metaph, ἐρώτησις Luc. Fug. 10.
hard to remedy, Hp. Epid. 4.30.
ον, hard to explain ; τὸ δ. Porph. VP 48, cf. Hsch. = δυσεκκόμιστος, Id.
ον, craggy, rugged, Eust. ad D.P. 389.
ον, not easily displaced outwards, Sor. 1.102.
ον, hard to dislodge, Simp. in Ph. 677.29.
ον, hard to draw back, of overwound strands of gut, Ph.Mech. Bel. 58.23.
ον, hard to correct or reform, Vett.Val. 77.6 ; πολιτεία Theo Prog. 12.
ον, hard to extend or distend, Gal. 8.288, al.
ον, hard to master, Suid. s.v. Ἀγάπιος.
ον, hard to get at, DS. 1.69.
ον, hard to attain to, παράδειγμα OGI 764.17 (Pergam.).
ον, hard to assail, χώρα Aen.Tact. 8.1 codd. ; risky to undertake, πλοῦς Peripl. M.Rubr. 39 ; unsuccessful, Paul.Al. N. 4.

ον, hard to attack secretly, X. Eq. Mag. 4.11 (Comp.), Ages. 6.7 (Sup.).
hard to damage, Apollod. Poliorc. 139.7.
ον, hard to identify or find out, SIG 1023.9 (Cos, iii/ii BC), App. BC 1.18.
ον, hard to attack, Aen.Tact. Praef. 2.
ον, hard to meet, ἀπορία Alcid. Soph. 21.
ον, hard to decide, Ap. Ty. Ep. 19, Gal. 13.789.
ον, hard to conceive, Diog.Oen. 38.
ον, disinclined for intercourse, τινί Str. 11.2.2 ; abs., unsociable, Id. 3.3.8 ; τὸ ἄστοργον καὶ δ. Plu. 2.917c, Porph. Abst. 4.6.
ον, hard to understand, M.Ant 6.17 ; hard to devise or plan out, Jul. Or. 1.12b.
ον, hard to turn or guide, ἅρματα App. Mith. 42.
ον, hard to check, of bleeding, Gal. 19.457, Aret. CA 2.6. Adv. -τως Gal. 7.725, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.99.

ον, hard to accomplish, στρατεία DS. 17.93 ; ineffective, Vett.Val. 43.12, al., Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.164. Adv. -τως Vett.Val. 194.27.
hard to treat, Hippiatr. 26.
ον, hard to criticize, Alex.Aphr. in Top. 543.5.

ον, hard to prove, πρόβλημα Arist. APr. 42b31.
hard to attack, θέσις Id. Top. 159a3 ; πρόβλημα ib. 158b16 ; Sup. δυσεπιχειρητότατοι τῶν ὅρων ib. 158b8 ; of a person, J. BJ 4.3.10, Plu. 2.281a, App. Pun. 118.
ον, hard to cicatrize, Gal. 6.751, v.l. in Dsc. 4.41.

ον, unhappy in love, Max.Tyr. 3.5 (Comp., wrongly spelt δυσερασίστερος).
unfavourable to love, ὄρθρος AP 5.171 (Mel.), 172 (Id.).
ἡ, difficulty of performing, Artem. 1.67.
ον, difficult to construct, χώματα J. BJ 5.9.2.
ἡ, difficulty, Sor. 2.53, Orib. 45.18.14 ; functional defect, Paul.Aeg. 6.42, al.
to be sluggish, καταμήνια γοῦντα, of dysmenorrhoea, Hp. Ep. 21.
ατος, τό, difficulty, hindrance, Dsc. Ther. Praef.
ές, difficult, App. Hisp. 73, al. ; τὸ δ. OGI 502.6 (Aezani) ; Comp., of an operation, Antyll. (?) ap. Orib. 44.23.23 ; making it hard to work, βαρύτητες Plu. 2.1129d.

ἡ, difficulty in working or construction, δυσεργίαν παρέχειν Ph.Mech. Bel. 56.42, cf. Hero Aut. 23.8 (in form -έργεια), Plu. Aem. 16 ; difficulty in pronouncing, ἡ ἐν τῇ προφορᾷ δ. Phld. Po. 2.42 ; inability to exert oneself, Hp. VM 10 (v.l. δυσοργίη) ; inability to act, App. Syr. 19.

ον, hard to work, ὕλη Thphr. HP 5.1.1 ; λίθοι Paus. 3.21.4 ; unfit to be worked, σίδηρος Plu. Lyc. 9 ; hard to manage, ὁπλισμός Id. Flam. 8 ; δ. χρῆσθαι Id. Tim. 28 ; πόλις δυσεργοτέρα harder to besiege, Id. Nic. 17.
hard to effect, difficult, Plb. 28.8.3, Ph. 1.272 (Sup.) ; πόλεμος App. Hisp. 63 (Sup.) ; τὸ παραφυλάττειν τὰς ἐξόδους δυσεργότερον J. BJ 5.12.1. Adv. -γως, κινηθῆναι Plu. Demetr. 43. Act., incapable of work, useless, πρός τι App. Syr. 16 ; χεῖμα δ., hiems ignava, Bion Fr. 15.5 ; idle, νωθρὸς καὶ δ. Plu. Alex. 33.
ον, hard to search, χωρία J. BJ 1.16.5.
ον, very lonely, desolate, πάγος AP 9.561 (Phil.).
ι, gen. ιδος, quarrelsome, contentious, Isoc. 1.31, Arist. Rh. 1381a32, EN 1108a30, al. ; δ. λόγος Pl. Lg. 864a. Act., producing unhappy strife, φθόνος Plu. Pel. 4 ; τὸ δανείζειν δ. App. BC 1.54.
ἡ, contentious disposition, Procl. in Prm. p. 539 S. ; irreconcilability, Iamb. Myst. 1.2.
ον, pertaining to unholy strife, αἷμα S. El. 1385 (lyr.) ; σπουδή Cleanth. Stoic. 1.122.
ον, hard to interpret, Ep. Hebr. 5.11, Gal. 11.454, Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.114.26 ; hard to describe, χρόαι DS. 2.52 ; θέα Ph. 1.649.
ἡ, v. δύσερμος.
ον, not favoured by Hermes, unlucky, Suid. ; — hence δυσερμία, ἡ, ill luck, Hsch., EM 291.49.
ές, hardly shooting or sprouting, Poll. 1.231.

ωτος, ὁ, ἡ, madly or disastrously loving, τινός E. Hipp. 193 ; τῶν ἀπόντων Th. 6.13 ; τῶν ἀφροδισίων X. Oec. 11.13 ; mali cupidus, Max.Tyr. 36.4 ; εἰς χρήματα Jul. Or. 2.85c ; abs., Lys. 4.8 (s.v.l.), Call. Epigr. 42.6, AP 5.244 (Maced.), al. ; of bees, Lyr.Alex.Adesp. 7.16 ; δ. ἔρως Plu. Per. 20.
laggard in love, Theoc. 1.85, 6.7.
to be desperately in love, Ach.Tat. 5.1, Plu. Fr. 21.2.
ἡ, (< ἔτος) bad season, Poll. 1.52.
ον, hard to derive, ὄνομα Corn. ND 20.
Dor. for δυσευνήτωρ.
Dor. δυσευνάτωρ, ορος, ὁ, ill bedfellow, A. Th. 293 (lyr.) ; — expld. by δυσεύνητος, ill-bedded, in Sch. ad loc.
ον, hard to procure, Alex.Trall. 1.15.

ον, hard to find out, A. Pr. 816 ; λόγος Porph. ap. Eus. PE 3.11 ; δ. τό τινων γένος Ph. 1.234.
hard to find or get, X. Mem. 3.14.7, Secund. Sent. 11 ; σπάνιον καὶ δ. Plu. 2.97b.
hard to find one΄s way through, impenetrable, ὕλη E. Ba. 1221.
ον, hard to come at, Plb. 31.25.3, Plu. 2.65e, Phld. Rh. 2.119 S. ; ἀνθρώπῳ Ecphant. ap. Stob. 4.7.64 ; hard to understand, Vett.Val. 272.8, al.
ον, hard to get at, inaccessible, DS. 1.57 (Sup.) ; τὸ δ. Phld. Rh. 1.325 S. (nisi leg. δυσέφικτον).
ον, hard to digest, Suid. s. vv. ἕψανον, τέραμνον.
ον, = δυσέψανος, Phryn. PS p. 33 B. ; hard to cook, Gal. 6.541 (Comp.).
ἡ, jealousy, Ath. 13.589a.

ον, exceeding jealous, Od. 7.307 ; ἐπί τινι ARh. 4.1089 ; γυνή Plu. Alex. 9 ; τὸ δ. Id. 2.471a. Adv. -λως, ἔχειν πρός τινα Id. Alex. 77.
eager, ὁρμή Emp. 114.3.
rivalling in hardship, αἰθυίῃσι βίον δύσζηλον ἔχοντες Hom. Epigr. 8.
ον, hard to seek or track, X. Cyn. 8.1, Poll. 5.50.
v.l. for δυσοδία, Ps.-Callisth. 3.9.
ον, wretched, βίοτος δ. AP 9.574.
δυσάντητον, Hsch.
ον, hard to heal or cure, Hp. Fract. 29, AP 3.19 (Cyzicus).
ές, = δυσήκεστος, Hsch.
to be hard of hearing, Antyll. ap. Orib. 10.13.5.
ἡ, hardness of hearing, Dsc. 5.17, Plu. 2.1073d, Vett.Val. 109.31 ; disobedience, Plu. 2.794d.

ον, hard of hearing, ὦτα Ph. 2.35 ; δυσήκοος ὦ Στρατονίκη, epitaph in Inscr. Mus. Alex. 299 (iii BC) ; disobedient, Plu. 2.13f.
ill-sounding, terrible to hear, prob. in S. Fr. 220 ; unpleasant to the ear, Demetr. Eloc. 48, Poll. 2.117, Philostr. VS 1.12 ; of an orator, Eun. VS p. 456 B.
ον, spinner of ill, Μοῖρα Nonn. D. 1.367 ; Φιλομήλη ib. 4.321.
ον, hard to drive through or over, Poll. 1.186.

ές, (< ἄλγος, ἀλεγεινός) Homeric epith. of death and war, bringing bitter grief, cruel, ruthless, θάνατος, πόλεμος, Od. 22.325, Il. 20.154 ; πηγάδες… δυσηλεγέες cruel frosts, Hes. Op. 506 ; δυσηλεγέος ἀπὸ δεσμοῦ Id. Th. 652 ; also of men, πολῖται Thgn. 795 ; γείτονες Max. 87.

Dor. δυσάλιος, ον, ill-sunned, sunless, κνέφας A. Eu. 396 (lyr.), cf. E. Rh. 247 (lyr.), Plu. Mar. 11, etc.
too much sunned, parched, θέρος Trag.Adesp. 340.
have an unlucky day, be unlucky, Pherecr. 98 ; κατὰ τὰς μάχας DH. 1.57.
ατος, τό, ill luck, Sch. Il. 6.336.
Dor. δυσαμερία, ἡ, unlucky day ; mishap, misery, δυσαμεριᾶν πρύτανιν A. Fr. 236 ; μοῖρα δυσαμερίας S. Fr. 591, cf. Plu. Eum. 9.
ον, (< ἥμερος) hard to tame, restive, Str. 3.3.8, Ptol. Tetr. 56.
ον, = δυσημής, Hp. Epid. 6.8.26.
ές, = δυσεμής, Hp. Aph. 4.7.
δυστάραχον, τὸ κακοὺς ἀνέμους ἔχον, Hsch.
ον, hard to bridle, Tim.Gaz. 124.11.
ον, (< ἀνία) = δυσάνιος, ill at ease, uneasy, Hp. Epid. 3.17. ιαʹ codd.
ον, (< ἡνία) = δυσηνίαστος, refractory, Epict. Gnom. 63 ; γυνὴ δυσήνιόν ἐστι (v.l. -άνιόν) Men. 803. Β.
ον, hard to hold in, ungovernable, Luc. Abd. 17.
= δυσήνυτος.
ον, (< ἀνύω) hard to accomplish, J. BJ 5.12.1 ; also δυσήνυκτος, Hsch.
ες, difficult, opp. εὐήρης, Suid.
ιδος, ὁ, ἡ, = δύσερις 1, Pi. O. 6.19, Axiop. 1.4 ; Att. form of δύσερις acc. to Moer. 126.
ον, = δύσηρις, Hsch. ; also, = ἀμφίβολος, Id.
ον, (< ἀρόω) hard to plough, Call. Del. 268, Poll. 1.227.
ον, hard to conquer, Poll. 1.157.
ορος, ὁ, ἡ, heavy at heart, Hsch.

Dor. δυσαχής¹, ές, (< ἠχέω) ill-sounding, Phld. Po. 2.16, v.l. in DH. Comp. 14 ; giving a dull sound, of metals, Plu. 2.721c ; ἰσθμοῖο δ. Emp. 100.19 ; — in Hom., epith. of πόλεμος, Il. 2.686 (cf. Anacr. 107), al. ; and of θάνατος, Il. 16.442, al. (where it should perh. be taken, = bringer of great woe (< ἄχος), cf. Apollon.Soph. Lex.), of φόνος Emp. 136.1 ; of ill-repute, δ. ἀνδράσιν h.Ap. 64.
ἡ, unpleasantness of sound, Phld. Po. 2.24, Po. Herc. 994.23.
ον, ill-sounding, ῥυθμός Hermog. Id. 1.7 ; συνθήκη ibid.
ον, subject to sea-sickness, Sor. 1.109.
ές, hardly growing, Cratin. 405, Alex.Mynd. ap. Ath. 9.393a.
ας, ἡ, a misfortune, Sophr. 83 (pl.).

ές, hardtowarm ; chilly, χειμών Il. 17.549.
over-warm, burning hot, QS. 11.156 codd.

strengthd. for θανατάω, long for death, J. BJ 5.9.3, 6.6.2, Agath. 3.22, cf. EM 442.48 ; but freq. confused with δυσθανατέω, as in Ph. 2.390. δυσθανατῶσα γραῦς ΄with one foot in the grave΄, Chrysipp. Stoic. 3.50.

to be loath to die, Hdt. 9.72 ; struggle against death, die hard, Pl. R. 406b, Thphr. HP 3.11.3, Plu. Ant. 77, etc. ; also, to be sick to death with desire, περί τι Ph. 2.167 ; to be deadly obstinate, περί τι ib. 100 ; abs., to be in deadly terror, ib. 173.
ον, bringing a hard death, Hp. Prorrh. 1.55 ; κρατῆρες E. Ion 1051 (lyr.).
ές, unhappy in death, AP 9.81 (Crin.).

ον, ill to look on, A. Pr. 69 (lyr.), S. Aj. 1004.
hard to see, ἀμαυρὸν αἴθυγμα καὶ δ. Plu. 2.966b, cf. Ael. NA 9.61.
(< σθένος) to be weak and powerless, Hp. Morb. 2.54, al.

ον, godless, ungodly, A. Ag. 1590, Ch. 46 (lyr.) ; ὦ δ. μίσημα S. El. 289.
miserable, wretched, μισθὸς εὐσεβίης AJA 17.170 (Cyrene, written δύσθιον).
ἡ, difficulty of treatment, Cass. Pr. 1.
ον, hard to cure, Hp. Medic. 10, S. Aj. 609 (lyr.) ; εὐήθεια Ph. 1.334.
δυσαλθήτους, Hsch.
ον, cold, Sch. Il. 17.549.
ον, over-hot, parched, Poll. 5.110.
ἡ, bad condition ; fretfulness, peevishness, Hp. Fract. 33 (v.l. δυσαισθησίη).
to be dissatisfied, ταῖς συνθήκαις Plb. Fr. 128 ; to be in distress, DS. 14.113. mostly in Med., abs., to be vexed, X. Cyr. 2.2.5 ; τινί Plb. 33.17.1 ; to be in straits, Id. 8.5.4.

ον, (< τίθημι) in bad case, κακόν Ph. 1.97 ; τὸ δ. bad condition, J. AJ 15.9.6.
hard to set right, Hp. Fract. 38 (Comp.).

ον, hard to observe, Arist. HA 511b13 ; scarcely visible, τρύπημα Hero Spir. 1.31, cf. Philum. Ven. 15.6.
hard to understand or reduce to theory, τέχνη Ph.Mech. Bel. 49.19, cf. Plb. 3.31.7, Phld. Rh. 1.141 S., Ph. 2.84.
ον, hard to catch, Arist. HA 615a22, Plu. Pomp. 38 ; metaph, τὸ δ. [τῆς φιλοσοφίας] Ph. 1.234 ; δ. τἀληθές Plu. Per. 13, cf. Ph. 2.217, al.
ον, = δυσθήρατος, Pl. Sph. 218d, 261a.
ἡ, bad hunting, Poll. 5.13.
ον, having bad sport, Oppian. H. 3.431, Poll. 5.13.
ον, hard to store, καρπός Pl. Criti. 115b, cf. Arist. Mu. 401a5.
v. δύσθεος.
ον, hard to crush, tough, Thphr. HP 8.4.1 (Comp.), Gal. UP 11.17.
= δυσθανατέω, only in part., E. El. 843, Rh. 791.
= δυσθνῄσκω, Nic.Dam. p. 36 D.
ον, hard to break, Dsc. 4.154, Gal. UP 11.17.
ον, loud-wailing, most mournful, ἔπος S. Ant. 1211 ; θρῆνοι E. IT 144 (anap.) ; — also δύσθρηνος, gloss on δυσηχής, Apollon.Soph. Lex.
= δυσθρήνητος.
ον, ill-sounding, φωνά Pi. P. 4.63 ; βάγματα, αὐδά, γόοι, A. Pers. 637 (lyr.), 942 (anap.), 1076 (lyr.).
ον, hard to break in pieces, στερρότης Plu. ap. EM 104.1 (dub.l.).
to be dispirited, despond, h.Cer. 362.
= δυσθυμαίνω, Hdt. 8.100, Onos. 10.26 ; δ. ταῖς ἐλπίσιν Plu. Tim. 34 ; — Med., to be melancholy, angry, Democr. 286, E. Med. 91.

ἡ, despondency, despair, Hp. VM 10, Pl. Lg. 666b, etc. ; πρὶν ἐλθεῖν ξυμμάχοις δυσθυμίαν E. Supp. 696 ; pl., Id. Med. 691, S. Fr. 663, Arist. Pr. 954b35, Ph. 2.99.
ill-temper, Them. Or. 13.172c.
ή, όν, melancholy, Arist. Phgn. 813a33.

ον, desponding, melancholy, S. El. 218 (lyr.), X. Cyr. 5.2.34, Arist. Pr. 955a17 (Comp.), Phld. Herc. 1251.10 ; τοῖς πεπραγμένοις S. El. 550 ; τὸ δ., = δυσθυμία, Plu. Per. 15. Adv. -μως, ἔχειν Plb. 1.87.1, Phld. Mort. 27 ; Comp. -ότερον Pl. Phd. 85b.
to be hard to heal, Paul.Aeg. 3.18.

Ion. δυσίητος [ι], ον, hard to heal, κληΐς Hp. Art. 14 (Comp.), cf. Cass. Pr. 1 (Comp.) ; κακὸν δ. an ill that none can cure, A. Ag. 1103 (lyr.) ; ὀργή E. Med. 520 ; νόσημα Pl. Lg. 916a, cf. Ph. 1.40, al. ; of persons, implacable, Them. Or. 15.192c. Adv. -τως, μόριον πεπονθὸς δ. Gal. 18(2).273.
ωτος, ὁ, ἡ, hardly perspiring, Thphr. Sud. 18.
to have bad omens in a sacrifice, Plu. Caes. 63, 2.587c.
Att. δυσιθάλαττος, ον, (< δύω) dipped in the sea, AP 6.38 (Phil.).
ον, (< ἰκμάς) with scanty secretions, Hp. Mul. 1.34 ; δ. πάθος Orib. Fr. 78.
ή, όν, = δυτικός, PLond. 1.98.51.

ον, κάματος, ph = ma, of the torments of love, ARh. 3.961, 4.4.
tormented by love, Nonn. D. 42.202, al.
ον, = δύσιππος, τόπος Anon. Hist. in Rev.Ét.Gr. 5.320, Sch. Pl. Mx. 240c, cf. Poll. 1.186 (v.l.).
ον, hard to ride in ; τὰ δ. parts unfit for cavalry-service, X. HG 3.4.12 ; δ. χώρα Plu. Phil. 14.

εως, ἡ, (< δύω) setting of the sun or stars, opp. ἀνατολή, Heraclit. 120, A. Pr. 458 ; ἀμφὶ Πλειάδων δύσιν (cf. Πλειάδες) Id. Ag. 826 ; περὶ δύσιν Πλειάδος Damox. 2.19 ; δ. χειμερινή, θερινή, ἰσημερινή, Cleom. 1.9 ; δ. τροπική Str. 2.4.7 ; ἄχρι ἡλίου δύσεως IG 4.597 (Argos) ; ἁλίου ἄχρι δ. ib. 606 (ibid.) ; Κυνὸς ψυχρὰν δ. S. Fr. 432.11 ; personified, PMagBerol. 2.94 ; pl., δύσιες, opp. ἀντολαί, ARh. 1.85 ; metaph, δ. τοῦ λογισμοῦ Ph. 1.511.
quarter in which the sun sets, west, πρὸς ἡλίου δύσιν Th. 2.96 ; πρὸς δύσεις Arist. Mu. 393a18 ; ἀπὸ δύσεως CIG 1755 (Opus) ; πρὸς δύσει Plb. 1.42.5 ; πρὸς τὰς δύσεις βλέπειν Id. 5.104.7.
hiding-place, Oppian. H. 1.330.
ον, hard to track, Sch. S. Aj. 32.
ον, not easily rusted in Comp., Orib. 49.3.5.
ές, hard to burn, burning badly, Plu. 2.952c.
ον, hard to overthrow, Ph. 1.61 ; στάσις J. BJ 2.17.4.

ον, hard to purify, Ph. 1.239, al. ; hard to purge, πνεύματα Plu. 2.991b, cf. Dsc. 5.69.
hard to satisfy by purification or atonement, δ. ᾍδου λιμήν, of the house of the Labdacidae in which murders never ceased, S. Ant. 1284 (lyr.) ; δαίμων Ar. Pax 1250.
ον, hard to hold in, ἵπποι X. Mem. 4.1.3 (Sup.) ; πλήθη Plu. Num. 4 ; metaph, Corn. ND 30 ; πλοῦτος Luc. Tim. 29 (s.v.l., al. δυσκάτοχος) ; hard to keep in mind, retain, Plu. 2.408b.
ον, hard to go down into, σπήλαιον Conon 35.1.
ές, hard to bend, Plu. 2.650d, Aret. SD 2.3 ; Comp., Sabin. ap. Orib. 9.19.2.
ον, = δυσκαμπής, Cass. Pr. 61, Sch. Ar. Th. 74. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν Aët. 16.8.

ον, noisome from smoke, δώματα A. Ag. 774 (lyr.).
producing an unpleasant smoke, Thphr. Ign. 72 ; φοῖνιξ Chaerem. 39 (Sup.).
ον, hard to endure, κακόν Phld. D. 1.12, Ph. 2.73, Plu. Phoc. 4, etc. Adv. -τως Porph. Marc. 8, Herod.Med. ap. Aët. 9.2.
όν, making a landing difficult, βράχη Stad. 114.
ον, hard to overcome, Plb. 15.15.8, DH. 3.7 ; hard to refute, Id. Rh. 8.3 ; τὸ δ. impregnability, Corn. ND 20.
ον, hard to bring, πρὸς φιλίαν, f.l. for δυσσυγκάθετος, Iamb. VP 31.194.
ον, hard to break, Thphr. HP 3.7.4, Dsc. 3.22, Apollod. Poliorc. 139.8.
ον, hard to comprehend, DS. 1.3, Ph. 2.216, M.Ant 5.10.
ον, hard to reconcile, Plu. 2.13d, Ath. 14.625b.
ον, hard to bring to an end, πόλεμοι Str. 14.1.28 ; hard to overthrow, δυναστεία J. BJ 4.5.5.
ον, hard to learn or understand, Isoc. 10.11, Pl. Plt. 303d (Comp.), DH. Th. 9. Adv. -μαθήτως, ἔχειν Isoc. 2.33.
ον, hard to overcome, DS. 3.35 ; νόσος (sc. πενία) Lib. Decl. 34.4.
ον, hard to understand, διάλεκτος DS. 5.14, cf. Plu. 2.47c.
ον, hard to check, ἄλγος A. Ch. 470 (lyr.) ; βοή LXX 3 Ma. 5.7 ; of persons, Plu. Alex. 31 ; restless, ψυχή E. Med. 109 (anap.) ; τὸ δυσκαταπαυστότερον Thphr. Vent. 35.
ον, hard to digest, Thphr. CP 1.14.4.
ον, hard to keep in awe, Plb. 1.67.4.
ον, hard to conquer, DS. 2.48.
ον, hard to execute, M.Ant 6.19, Arr. Epict. 3.12.8 ; hard to digest, Sor. 2.32.
ἡ, difficulty of swallowing, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.86, Philum. ap. Aët. 8.48.
have difficulty in swallowing, Herod.Med. ap. Orib. 5.30.12.
ον, hard to swallow, Arist. Sens. 443b12, Archig. ap. Gal. 12.976.
ον, hard to effect, X. Cyr. 8.7.12 (Comp.).
ον, hard to place rightly, ἐν τῇ ἐπιβάσει, of stallions, Hippiatr. 14.
ον, hard to extinguish, DS. 4.54, Plu. 2.417b.
ον, hard to restore or rally, X. Cyr. 5.3.43 (Comp.).
ον, not to be despised, ib. 8.1.42 (Comp.).
ἡ, indigestion, Anon. Lond. 6.10.

ον, hard to work, λίθος Str. 17.1.33 ; καρποὶ δυσκατεργαστότεροι slower to mature, Thphr. CP 1.14.4 ; hard of digestion, Dsc. 2.93, Ph. 2.244. = δυσκατάπρακτος, X. Mem. 4.2.7 (Comp.).
hard to tame, γένος ταύρων Agatharch. 76 (Sup.) ; hard to overcome, Luc. Tyr. 15.
δυσθεώρητος, Hsch.

ον, hard to succeed in, ἔργον Demetr. Eloc. 127, Ph. 2.83, Gal. UP 15.7 ; τυραννίς Chio Ep. 15 (Comp.).
hard to set right, remedy, σπάνις τῶν ἀναγκαίων J. AJ 2.5.6.
ον, hard to cicatrize, Dsc. 5.81 ; ἕλκη Apollon. Mir. 42.
v. δυσκάθεκτος.
ον, hard to burn, Apollod. Poliorc. 139.8.
v. δύω.
ον, ill-sounding, shrieking, φόβος Il. 16.357 ; ζῆλος δ. envy with its tongue of malice, Hes. Op. 196 ; δ. ὕμνος Ἐρινύος A. Th. 867 (anap.), cf. Fr. 451 I ; μοῦσα E. Ion 1098 (lyr.).
ον, hard to excrete, Gal. 18(1).580 (Sup.).
ον, hard to temper, φύσις πρὸς τὸ πιθανὸν δ. Plu. Dio 52 ; δύσμικτα καὶ δ. Id. 2.754c.
ές, with ill gains, ill-gotten, Oppian. H. 2.417.

ές, (< κῆδος) full of misery, δυσκηδέα νύκτα φυλάσσω Od. 5.466.
ΙΙ. (< κήδομαι) δυσκηδέα· δυσφύλακτον, χαλεπόν, Hsch.
ον, (< κηλέω) past remedy, A. Eu. 825 (cf. Sch. ad loc.) ; but perh. rather formed by analogy from εὔκηλος ; hence, spiteful.
ἄφρονα, δυσολώνιστον, Hsch.
Ion. -ίη, ἡ, difficulty of moving, Hp. Aph. 3.17, Arist. GA 780a25, PA 685a8.
move with difficulty, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus. 58.104.

[ῑ] ον, hard to move, Pl. Ti. 56a, Ph. 2.227 (Comp.), Thphr. Vent. 35 (Sup.) ; πλοῖα Plb. 1.22.3. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν πρὸς τοὺς ἀνέμους Arist. Cael. 294b17. in mental relations, δ. πρὸς τοὺς φόβους Pl. R. 503d ; δ. ὑπὸ ὀργῆς Arist. VV 1250a5 ; δ. ποιεῖν τὴν διάνοιαν Id. PA 686a30 ; ἕξις δυσκινητοτέρα διαθέσεως Id. Cat. 9a10 ; τὸ δυσκίνητον obstinacy, Phld. Lib. p. 55 O. ; of language, clumsiness, τὸ ἄσχημον καὶ δ. Id. Po. 994.35. Adv. -τως καὶ δυσμαθῶς ἔχειν Pl. R. 503d.
firm, resolute, Plu. Thes. 36 ; inexorable, ᾍδης AP 7.221.
impervious to motion, of the soul, Plot. 1.4.8.

ές, inglorious, Il. 9.22 (poet. acc. δυσκλέα for δυσκλεέα) ; infamous, shameful, of persons and things, δ. θέα A. Pr. 243 ; δυσκλεεστάτῳ μόρῳ Id. Pers. 444 ; πρῶτον μὲν οὐκ οὖσ’ ἄδικός εἰμι δυσκλεής E. Hel. 270. cf. X. Cyr. 3.3.53, LXX 3 Ma. 3.23 (Sup.). Adv. -εῶς S. El. 1006, E. Hel. 993 codd., Plu. 2.169a.

ἡ, ill-fame, infamy, S. Fr. 188, E. Med. 218, Th. 3.58, Pl. Lg. 663a, etc. ; ἐπὶ δυσκλείᾳ tending to disgrace them, S. Aj. 143 (anap.).
ingloriousness, D. 60.24.
ον, of ill name, boding ill, Luc. Am. 39.
to be unlucky in one΄s lot, esp. in standing for an office, opp. λαγχάνω, Pl. Lg. 690c.
ατος, τό, piece of ill luck, Plb. 30.20.9 (pl.) ; τῆς πατρίδος DS. 32.22 (pl.).
ον, unlucky, Phryn. PS p. 61 B.
poet. for δυσκλεής, Simm. Secur. 6.
ον, in bad repute, Heraclid. Tar. ap. Ath. 3.120d.
ον, hard to inflect, irregular, δ. ῥήματα, title of work by Eulogius, EM 809.33.
δυσέκβατον, Suid.
ον, ill-famed, Hsch.

ον, bad for the bowels, Dsc. 1.105, Plu. 2.137a.
costive, Paul.Aeg. 1.44.
ον, unsocial, Pl. R. 486b ; ἀρχή Plu. Demetr. 3.
to have bad nights, Hp. VM 10, Acut. 30.
ον, making bed unpleasant, Aristaenet. 2.7.

impf. ἐδυσκόλαινον Pl. Phlb. 26d ; fut. -κολανῶ Isoc. 15.149 : — to be peevish, Ar. Nu. 36 ; of a baby, Lys. 1.11, cf. X. Mem. 2.2.8 ; τινί D. 37.15 ; feel a difficulty, δ. ὡς… Pl. l.c. ; in argument, to be captious, Arist. Top. 160b3, al.
cause trouble or annoyance, οὔρησις δυσκολαίνουσα Hp. Prorrh. 1.109.
ἡ, discontent, peevishness, Ar. V. 106, Pl. R. 411c. of things, difficulty, δ. ἔχειν D. 5.1, Arist. Pol. 1281a14, etc. ; πλείους παρέχειν δυσκολίας ib. 1263a11 ; δ. ὀνομάτων J. AJ 2.7.4.
ον, hard to glue together, Gal. 11.124, 133 ; illglued or fastened, loose, Luc. Hist. Conscr. 11.
ον, hard to bend ; δ. καμπή an intricate flourish in singing, Ar. Nu. 971.
ον, making bed uneasy, μέριμνα ib. 420.

ον, (< κόλον) ; of persons, prop. hard to satisfy with food (cf. Ath. 6.262a) ; but, generally, hard to please, discontented, fretful, peevish, Ar. V. 942 ; γῆρας E. Ba. 1251 ; δ. ψυχὴ καὶ ἀγρία Pl. Lg. 649e, cf. Arist. EN 1108a30, etc. ; τὸ δ. Pl. Lg. 791c ; of animals, intractable, Id. Tht. 174d (Comp.) ; so in Adv. δυσκόλως, ἔχειν, διακεῖσθαι πρός τινα, D. 19.132, Isoc. 3.33 ; δυσκολώτερον διακεῖσθαι Pl. Phd. 84e. of things, troublesome, harassing, δ. ἡ ἡνιόχησις Id. Phdr. 246b ; πυρετοί Hp. Coac. 38 ; generally, unpleasant, ἄν τι δ. συμβῇ D. 18.189, cf. Men. 89 ; εἴ τι δ. πέπρακται Θηβαίοις πρὸς ἡμᾶς D. 18.176 ; καιροὶ δ. difficult times, IG2². 682.33. Adv. -λως, ὑπακούειν Hp. Epid. 3.8.
difficult to explain, Arist. SE 180b5, Metaph. 1001b1 ; δ. ἐστι it is difficult, Ev. Marc. 10.24, cf. Onos. 1.15 (Comp.) ; τὰ μὲν ῥάδια… τὰ δὲ δ. Phld. Po. 994.24. Adv. -λως hardly, with difficulty, Ev. Marc. 10.23, al.
ον, with luckless womb, γαστήρ, of a woman whose child was dead before birth, AP 7.583 (Agath.).
ον, hard to bear, intolerable, πότμος S. Ant. 1346 (lyr.) ; τέκνα E. HF 1422.
ον, hard to bake, ἄρτος EM 150.35.
ον, (< κόπτω) hard to bruise, Damocr. ap. Gal. 13.636.
ές, intemperate, Oppian. H. 2.517.
αὐχμηρόν, Hsch. ; cf. δυσχρανής.
ἡ, bad temperament, of the air, Str. 6.4.1, Plu. Alex. 58 (pl.) ; σώματος Stoic. 3.216 ; τῶν ἐν ἡμῖν δυνάμεων Ph. 1.29. (δυσκρασίη Man. 4.543.)
ές, = δυσκράτητος, δυσκρατέστατον πάντων ὁ λόγος Stob. 3.33.10.
ον, hard to control, τὸ δ. τῆς ἐπιβολῆς DS. 3.3 ; ungovernable, ill-disciplined, J. AJ 19.4.1 ; γηρῶντι ἤδη δ. εἶναι (sc. τὴν ἀρχήν) App. Syr. 61.
ον, of bad temperament, ἀήρ Str. 2.3.1, cf. Gal. 9.912. Adv. -τως Id. 10.518 ; διακεῖσθαι Ps.-Plu. Vit. Hom. 202.
ές, hard to distinguish, Plu. 2.922a ; = δύσκριτος, Aët. 5.10.
ον, = δύσκριτος, Sch. Hp. 2.272 D.

ον, hard to discern or interpret, ἄστρων δύσεις A. Pr. 458 ; κληδόνες ib. 486 ; ὀνείρατα Id. Ag. 981 (lyr.), cf. S. Tr. 949 (lyr.) ; δ. νοῦσοι hard to determine, doubtful, Hp. Aph. 3.8 ; but δύσκριτα ἐγένετο there was an obscure crisis, Id. Epid. 3.12 ; δ. ἐστι πότερον… ἢ… difficult of solution, Id. Aph. 1.12, Pl. R. 433c. Adv. -τως doubtfully, darkly, A. Pr. 662 ; δ. ἔχειν to be in doubt, Ar. Ra. 1433.
ον, badly put together ; Adv. -τως, διακεῖσθαι to be in bad condition, Meno Iatr. 13.20, cf. 9.16.
ον, hard to come by, πραγματεία Plb. 3.32.1 ; τἀγαθόν Phld. Herc. 1251.4 (dub.).
to be unlucky at dice, Ath. 15.666d, Poll. 9.94.
Adv. rolling with difficulty, δ. ἔχειν Philostr.Jun. Im. 10.
ον, in A. Ag. 653 δυσκύμαντα κακά evils from the stormy sea.
to be hard of hearing, Gal. 12.653, AP 7.731 (Leon.), Dsc. 4.162.
ἡ, deafness, Dsc. Eup. 1.61.
ον, hard of hearing, Hp. Coac. 193, Arist. Insomn. 459b21, LXX Ex. 4.11, Str. 14.2.21 ; τὸ τοῦ γήρως δ. Plu. 2.13e.
(< λεαίνω) hard to pound or bray, Archig. ap. Aët. 3.184.
ον, = δυσλέαντος, opp. εὐλείωτος, Asclep. ap. Gal. 13.677.
ον, hard to tell, A. Pers. 702 (anap.).
ον, ill-wedded, Sch. S. El. 492.
ές, rough-husked, κάρυον Nic. Al. 271.
gloss on δυσηλεγής, Hsch.
ον, hard to take hold of, Sor. 1.88 ; hard to catch, μοχθηρία Ph. 2.366, cf. Luc. Anach. 27 ; hard to comprehend, Str. 13.4.12, ADysc. Synt. 225.28, Plu. 2.17d.
ον, gloss on δύσορμος, Sch. rec. A. Pers. 448.
ον, hard to compute, Anaximen. ap. Stob. 2.8.17, Plu. 2.981e, Gal. 18(2).631, DC. 73.15. Act., ill-calculating, misguided, χείρ S. Aj. 40.

ον, hard for the neck, hard to bear, ζεύγλη, ζυγόν, Thgn. 848, 1024 ; χείρ B. 12.46 ; δ. φρενί prob. l. in S. Ichn. 4 ; δυσλοφωτέρους πόνους A. Pr. 931.
impatient of the yoke, ἡμίονοι Ael. NA 16.9. Adv. -φως, φέρειν E. Tr. 303.

ον, indissoluble, δυσλύτοις χαλκεύμασι A. Pr. 19 ; ἄκος τῶν δ. πόνων E. Andr. 121 (lyr.) ; ὦμοι stiff, Arist. Phgn. 811a4. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν X. Oec. 8.13.
insoluble, of a problem, Luc. JTr. 12, Alex.Aphr. in Metaph. 223.2 ; αἴνιγμα Plu. Fr. 25.3 ; hard to refute, Alex.Aphr. in Top. 558.25.
δυσχερῶν, Hsch.
to be slow at recognizing, A. Ch. 225.

ές, hard to learn, A. Ag. 1255 ; δ. ἰδεῖν hard to know at sight, E. Med. 1196 ; τὸ δ. difficulty of knowing, Id. IT 478. Act., slow at learning, dull, Pl. R. 358a, etc. ; Comp., Plu. 2.992d ; Sup., Ph. 2.175, Jul. Or. 7.225b. Adv. δυσμαθῶς, ἔχειν Pl. R. 503d.
ἡ, slowness at learning, ib. 618d (pl.), Lg. 812e, etc. ; — written δυσμαθμάθεια, Id. Ep. 315c, Iamb. VP 20.95.
(perh. f.l. for Δύμ-), = βάκχαι, at Sparta, Hsch. ; title of play by Pratinas, Ath. 9.392f.
ον, hard to soften, Ruf. ap. Orib. 8.24.22.
ές, thick, ὕδατα Thphr. HP 7.5.2.
ον, unfading, Trag.Adesp. 339.
ές, difficult, opp. εὐμαρής, ἀποτέλεσμα Phld. Rh. 2.119 S.
ον, hard to chew, Gal. 16.760.
Dor. for δυσμήτωρ.
fight in vain against or fight an unholy fight with, θεοῖσι δυσμαχοῦντες S. Tr. 492 ; πρὸς τὴν βελτίονα [δύναμιν] Plu. 2.371a ; abs., fight desperately, ib. 661c.
one must fight a losing battle with, ἀνάγκῃ δ’ οὐχὶ δ. S. Ant. 1106.
ον, keenly contested, δῶρα Μοισᾶν Lyr.Adesp. 86 B (cf. B. Fr. 32).

ον, hard to fightwith, unconquerable, X. HG 4.2.10 (Comp.), E. Hec. 1055 (Sup.) ; πάντων δυσμαχώτατον γυνή Id. Fr. 544 ; of things, A. Pr. 921, Pl. Lg. 863b, D. 1.4, etc. generally, difficult, δ. κρῖναι A. Ag. 1561 (lyr.).

or δύσμικτος, ον, hard to mix ; without affinity, Pl. Ti. 35a, etc.
unsocial ; Adv. -τως, ἔχειν Plu. 2.640d.
ον, hard to appease, Plu. Art. 19 ; πικρία Id. 2.553a.
ον, hard to employ in melody, of enharmonic intervals, Theo Sm. p. 56 H. (Sup.).
bear ill-will, τινί against another, E. Med. 874 ; δ. τοῖς κοινοῖς ἀγαθοῖς D. 18.217 ; δ. τῆς ποτὲ βίας App. Pun. 60 ; abs., Ph. 1.145.

Ion. -ίη, ἡ, ill-will, enmity, ἡ ἐκ σοῦ δ. S. El. 619 ; ἐν δ. εἶναι ib. 1124 ; δ. ἄρασθαί τινι E. Heracl. 991 ; in Prose, Democr. 191, Antipho 4.1.3, etc. ; φθόνος καὶ δ. Isoc. 5.68, Pl. R. 500c ; φθόνοι καὶ ἄλλαι δ. Id. Prt. 316d.
participial form, only masc., bearing ill-will, hostile, Od. 2.72 ; δυσμενέοντες ib. 73, 20.314.

ές, (< μένος) hostile, ἄνδρες δ. Il. 5.488 ; δυσμενέες enemies, 16.521, cf. Schwyzer 84.12 ; δυσμενέων ὄχλος A. Th. 234 (lyr.), cf. 366 (lyr.), Hdt. 3.82, S. Aj. 662 (Sup.), etc. ; οἱ ὑμέτεροι δ. X. HG 5.2.33 ; c. dat., τῷ πατοῦντι δυσμενεῖς A. Ag. 1193, cf. S. Ph. 585 ; οὐδὲν τυράννου δυσμενέστερον πόλει E. Supp. 429 ; less freq. c. gen., ἄνδρα δ. χθονός an enemy of the land, S. Ant. 187, cf. Ph. 2.136. Adv. -νῶς Pl. Tht. 168b ; δ. ἔχειν τινί Isoc. 3.5 ; πρὸς τὴν πόλιν Id. 14.6 ; — poet. δυσμενέως, Nonn. D. 21.85 (v.l.). rarely of things, δ. χοαί S. El. 440 ; δυσμενὲς ὁ τοῦ πλεονεκτεῖν ἔρως X. Mem. 2.6.21, cf. E. Alc. 617 (v.l.).
ου, ὁ, = δυσμενής, Ael. VH 3.7.
ή, όν, like an enemy, hostile, Plb. 6.7.8, etc. Adv. -κῶς Id. 8.8.1.
ον, hard to chew up, τραγήματα Philum. ap. Aët. 9.23.
ἡ, difficulty of alteration, Sor. 1.91.
ον, hard to alter, Hp. Alim. 51, Plu. 2.952c.
ον, = δυσμετάβλητος, Damocr. ap. Gal. 13.1003. Adv. -λως ib. 1004.
ον, not imparting freely, Str. 17.1.29 ; c. gen., reluctant to part with, τῶν ἀναγκαίων Phld. Herc. 1251.20.
