ον, hard to alter, of persons, opinionated, Plb. 12.26d. 5 ; προαίρεσις Plu. 2.799b ; hard to remove, Gal. 11.215.
ον, hard to shift, ψυχὴ δ. ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων J. AJ 16.11.8 ; γυνή Plu. 2.288d, Eust. 1733.32. Adv. -τως, ἔχειν Alex.Trall. 1.16.
ον, hard to break or move, Sch. S. OT 12.
ον, hard to cure of a habit, Gp. 19.2.13.
ον, hard to divert, Gal. 19.489. Adv. -τως, gloss on ἀσκελέως, Apollon.Soph. Lex.
ον, = δυσμετάστρεπτος, Eust. 1461.43.

ον, hard to manage, παῖς Pl. Lg. 808d (Sup.), cf. Plu. Mar. 37, al., Aen.Tact. 39.7 ; ζῷα Ael. NA 4.44 ; δίκτυα X. Cyn. 2.6.
hard to attack, στρατός Hdt. 7.236, J. BJ 1.7.1 ; of the tortoise΄s shell, Hierocl. p. 13 A.

ον, hard to measure, Antipho Soph. 106.
hard to traverse, πέλαγος Philostr. VA 4.15.

ἡ, (δύω) = δύσις, setting, mostly in pl., ἀελίου δ. S. OC 1245, cf. A. Fr. 69, Hp. Epid. 7.5, Pl. Phd. 61e ; ἐπὶ δυσμῇσιν ἐών at the point of setting, Hdt. 3.104 ; περὶ ἡλίου δυσμάς Lys. 1.39 ; ἥλιος ἦν ἤδη περὶ δυσμάς Hell. Oxy. 15.5 ; metaph, τὸ γῆρας δυσμαὶ βίου Arist. Po. 1457b25, cf. DH. 4.79, Ph. 1.678, S.E. M. 9.90, Diog.Oen. 2, etc.
the quarter of sunset, west, ἀπὸ ἑσπέρης τε καὶ [ἡλίου] δυσμέων Hdt. 2.31 ; πρὸς ἡλίου δυσμέων Id. 7.115, cf. 2.33 ; πρὸς δυσμαῖς A. Pers. 232 ; opp. ἀνατολαί, BGU 1049.8 (iv AD) ; — also δυθμή, Call. Cer. 10 (pl.), Fr. 539 (sg.).
ι, wrathful, θεός Poll. 1.39 ; χόλος AP 9.69 (Parmenion).
ον, = δύσμηνις, δένδρεα AP 7.141 (Antiphil.) ; ψυχαί Ptol. Tetr. 159 (-ίτας).
ερος, ἡ, in Od. 23.97 μῆτερ ἐμὴ δύσμητερ my mother yet no mother, cf. Lyc. 1174, Nonn. D. 46.194.
ι, contriving ill, Suid., Hsch. (cod. -ήτης).
Dor. δυσμάτωρ, ορος, ὁ, ἡ, in A. Supp. 67 (lyr.) δ. κότος an ill mother΄s wrath.
to be at loss how to do, c. inf., A. Ag. 1360.

ον, hard to effect, Epimen. ap. DL. 1.113 ; difficult, Ἀρχύτεω δυσμήχανα ἔργα κυλίνδρων Eratosth. Fr. 35.7 ; prob. f.l. for δύσμαχον, J. BJ 4.1.2. Act., at a loss, πρός τι Them. Or. 10.137b.
devising ill, Nonn. D. 44.210 ; δόλος ib. 35.273 ; also, ill-devised, wicked, ἔργον Oppian. H. 3.404.
ή, όν, (δυσμή) = δυτικός, western, Str. 2.5.11, Hld. 8.15 ; Comp., Str. 2.1.34, Ptol. Alm. 2.13, Theo Sm. p. 137 H. ; Sup., Str. 2.1.32, Ptol. Geog. 2.3.18.
v. δύσμεικτος.
ον, hard to imitate, DS. 1.61, Luc. Alex. 20, CIG 3187 (Smyrna) ; τὸ δ. Plu. Cat. Mi. 8 ; Sup., Anon. Oxy. 1012ii34.
ον, much hated, Lyc. 841.
ον, hard to remember, Arist. Rh. 1416b22, Aen.Tact. 24.2, Epicur. Ep. 2 p. 35U., DS. 1.3. Act., remembering ill, unmindful, Pl. Ti. 74e (Comp.).
ον, (μοῖρα) = δύσμορος, S. OC 327.
ἡ, a hard fate, AP 9.351 (Leon.).

ον, ill-fated, Il. 22.60, etc. ; δυσμόρου γε δύσμορα (sc. σκῆπτρα) S. OC 1109, cf. Men. Sam. 40, Lyc. 897, Opp. C. 3.217 ; in Prose, Antipho 3.2.11. Adv. -ρως with ill fortune, prob. in A. Th. 837 (lyr., cod. M -φόρως).
ἡ, misshapenness, ugliness, Hdt. 6.61, Phld. Mort. 29, etc.
ον, misshapen, ill-favoured, ἐσθής E. Hel. 1204, Lyc. 692, Plu. 2.670a.
ον, = ἄμουσος, unmusical, αὐλός AP 9.216 (Honestus).
ον, hard to dislodge, Aët. 3.34, Simp. in Cat. 236.27.
ον, hard to conquer, ἔρως J. AJ 18.1.6, cf. Plu. Comp. Pel. Marc. 2, DC. 43.28.
ον, hard to wash out, δ. ἐκ δέλτου γραφή S. Tr. 683.

ον, (< νίψ) snowed upon, Nonn. D. 2.685.
chilly, wintry, ὕδωρ ib. 3.210 ; οἶδμα ib. 13.533.
to be ill-affected, τινί LXX 3 Ma. 3.24, Plu. Cic. 38.
ον, hard to be understood, Darius ap. DL. 9.13, 2 Ep. Pet. 3.16 ; χρησμοί Luc. Alex. 54. Act., slow of understanding, Vett.Val. 345.26.
ἡ, disaffection, ill-will, malevolence, S. El. 654, E. Hec. 973, Pl. Tht. 151d, Plu. Demetr. 3, Phld. Lib. p. 29 O., etc.
Ep. and Ion. -ίη, ἡ, lawlessness, bad constitution, Sol. 4.32 ; personified in Hes. Th. 230.
ον, lawless, unrighteous, AP 6.316 (Nicodem.).
ον, contr. δύσνους, ουν, ill-affected, disaffected, τινί S. Ant. 212 ; τῇ πόλει Th. 2.60 ; πρὸς τὰ πράγματα X. HG 2.1.2 ; abs., E. IT 350, Plu. 2.176b. Adv. δύσνως Poll. 2.230.

νόστος a return that is no return, E. Tr. 75.
from which no traveller returns, ῥόος App.Anth. 4.54.
ον, hard to be corrected, θηρίον (sc. πενία) Men. Georg. 78.
ουν, contr. for δύσνοος.
ον, ill-wedded, AP 7.401 (Crin.).
ον, ill-wedded or ill-betrothed, E. IT 216 (lyr.), Tr. 144 (lyr.).
ον, inhospitable, Poll. 9.22.
ον, hard to dry, Thphr. CP 1.4.3, Plu. 2.627d, etc.
ον, hard to understand, Corn. ND 28, DC. 56.29.

ον, hard to deal with, driving a hard bargain, Pl. R. 486b, X. Mem. 2.6.3, Plu. Phoc. 5. = δυσξύμβλητος, Poll. 5.150.
ill to meet, ζῷα Artem. 4.56 (v.l. δυσσυμβούλευτα).
ον, hard to understand, δυσξύνετον ξυνετὸς μέλος ἔγνω E. Ph. 1506 (lyr.) ; διαγράμματα X. Mem. 4.7.3 ; τὸ δ., τὰ δ., Plu. 2.975f (δυσξύνθετον codd.), Iamb. VP 35.252.
ον, overheavy, burdensome, πλοῦτος Plu. Aem. 12.
ον, hardly passable, App. Syr. 21.
make bad way, get on slowly, Plu. Pyrrh. 32 ; of difficult breathing or childbirth, Ph. 2.563, Sor. 2.59 ; metaph, Arr. Epict. 3.19.3.

ἡ, badness of roads, App. Syr. 21 ; pl., in concrete sense, Ptol. Tetr. 197 ; metaph, difficulty, δυσοδίαν παρέχειν τῷ λόγῳ Plu. 2.448a, cf. Ph. 2.67 ; δυσοδία ἐντροχάζειν δοκεῖ Demetr.Lac. 1012.50 F. ; δ. σκυβάλων Sor. 2.20.
v. sub δυσοσμία.
v. sub δύσοσμος.
ον, difficult and rugged, prop. of a mountain road ; metaph, A. Eu. 387 (lyr.).
ον, hard to pass, scarce passable, Th. 1.107, Poll. 3.96.
(aor. ἐδύσοιξα Hsch.), to be distressed, E. Rh. 724 (lyr.) ; fear, tremble at, οὔτοι δυσοίζω θάμνον ὡς ὄρνις φόβῳ A. Ag. 1316 ; — Med., fear, E. Rh. 805. (Lacon. acc. to Hsch.)
ον, bad to dwell in, Hp. Aër. 19, X. Cyr. 8.6.21.

ον, hard to digest, Diph. Siph. ap. Ath. 2.70a, Xenocr. 73.
difficult to manage, τὸ δ. Artem. 2.58.
ον, gloss on ἄοικος, Sch. S. Ph. 534.
δυσθρήνητος, Hsch.
ον, acc. to Sch. and Hsch., = δύσοδος, τύχα δ. A. Ch. 945 (lyr.) ; or perh. (< οἴμη), a sad theme, cf. δύσοιμος· ἐπὶ κακῷ ἥκουσα, Hsch.
ον, yielding bad wine, Poll. 6.21.

ον, (< οἴσω) hard to bear, insufferable, ὀδμή Hp. Mul. 2.181 ; πήματα, ἄλγη, πόνοι, A. Pr. 690 (lyr.), Ch. 745, S. Ph. 508 (lyr.) ; βίου δύσοιστον ἕξομεν τροφάν Id. OC 1688 (lyr.) ; δ. ἀήρ Str. 12.3.40 ; ὀργή Jul. Gal. 161b.
(< οἰωνός) augurill of a thing, Phryn. PS p. 62 B.
ὁ, an ill omen, Hsch. s.v. ἀπήχεια.
ή, όν, ill-omened, Suid. s.v. ἐς κόρακας.
ον, = δυσοιωνιστικός, Ph. 2.542, Hermog. Stat. 3, Luc. Eun. 6, DC. 41.49.
ον, very lazy ; Adv. -κνως, ἐξεγείρεσθαι M.Ant 5.1 ; unwillingly, καταλείπειν τέκνα Hdn. 6.7.1.
ον, not slipping easily, Paul.Aeg. 3.76.
v. δύω.
ον, stormy ; metaph, βέλη S. Ant. 358 (lyr.).
ον, hard to live with, σκαιὸς καὶ δ. Hierocl. p. 59 A. ; δ. παροικοῦσα πόλις ἐχθρά D.Chr. 40.27.
ἡ, unsociableness, Satyr. Vit. Eur. Fr. 39x5.

ον, hard to live with, Plu. Demetr. 42.
bringing evil in one΄s company, Ἐρινύς A. Ag. 746 (lyr.).
ον, scarce-seeing, purblind, A. Eu. 388 (lyr.).
ον, unlike, Stratt. 75, Hsch.
infaustus, Gloss.

ον, full of ill dreams, ὕπνος Plu. 2.15b.
bringing ill dreams, βρώματα ib. 734f, cf. Dsc. 2.105.
δυστυχοῦντα, Hsch.
δύσφωνον, Hsch.
ον, (< ὄψομαι) hard to detect, Gal. Anim. Pass. 2.3 ; τὸ δ. τῆς ἡμέρας gloominess, Plb. 18.21.2.
ἡ, dim sight, Ruf. ap. Orib. 7.26.15 (pl.).

ον, hard to see, X. Cyr. 1.6.40, Ph. 1.570 ; δι’ ὑπερβολὰν λαμπρότατος δ. Ecphant. ap. Stob. 4.7.64 ; τὰ δυσόρατα dark corners, X. Eq. Mag. 4.18.
ill to look on, horrible, App. Hisp. 97.
ἡ, = passionateness, Hp. Hum. 9 (pl.).
ον, = δύσοργος, Arist. Phgn. 811a31, [Babr.] 11.12 ; θεός Poll. 1.39. Adv. -τως DH. 6.47.
ἡ, = δυσοργησία, v.l. in Hp. VM 10.
ον, quick to anger, S. Aj. 1017, Ph. 377, Tr. 1118 (wrongly expld. by κακοεργός, Hsch.).
ἡ, lack of appetite, Gal. 7.128.

ον, difficult to adapt to a limit, Arist. Mete. 378b24, GC 329b32.
difficult to define, χαρακτήρ DH. Din. 5.
(< ὅρκος) swear falsely, Phryn. PS p. 65 B.
ον, (< ὁρμίζω) = δύσορμος, Poll. 1.101.

ον, with bad anchorage, νῆσος… δ. ναυσί A. Pers. 448 ; also τὰ δ. rough ground, where one can scarce get footing, X. Cyn. 10.7. Act., πνοαὶ δ. that detained the fleet in harbour or that kept it from reaching harbour, foul winds, A. Ag. 193 (lyr.).
ιθος, ὁ, ἡ, = δυσοιώνιστος, boding ill, A. Th. 838 (lyr.), E. Hipp. 757 (lyr.) ; with ill auspices, Plu. Marc.. 4.
α, ον, dusky, τρύχη E. Ph. 325 (lyr.).
ἡ, an ill smell, S. Ph. 876, Fr. 538, Luc. Tox. 29 ; -ίη Man. 4.270.

Ion. δύσοδμος, ον, (< ὀσμή) ill-smelling, ἐν δυσοδμοτάτῳ [τόπῳ] γινόμενον εὐωδέστατόν ἐστι Hdt. 3.112 ; ὀσμή Arist. Pr. 908b29 (Comp.).
bad for scent, in hunting, οἱ ὄμβροι τὴν γῆν ποιοῦσι δύσοσμον X. Cyn. 5.3. Act., having a bad nose, Arist. Insomn. 459b22.
δύσοσμον, τό, = σκόρδιον, Ps.-Dsc. 3.111.
ον, hard to scar over, Alex.Trall. 4.1, Poll. 4.196.
to have difficulty in micturition, Diocl. Fr. 141, Ruf. ap. Orib. 8.24.6, Dsc. 1.6, POxy. 468.1, Aret. SD 2.4 ; — Med., Hp. Vict. 2.54.
ή, όν, suffering from δυσουρία, Gloss.
Ion. -ίη, ἡ, difficult micturition, Hp. Aph. 3.31 (pl.), Arist. Fr. 486 ; ἐν δυσουρίᾳ γενέσθαι Plu. 2.733c.
εως, ἡ, = δυσουρία, Ar.Byz. Epit. 146.5, Suid. s.v. τέτανος.
= δυσουρέω, Dsc. 1.33, Hippiatr. 31.
ή, όν ; πάθος δ., = δυσουρία, f.l. in Cic. Fam. 7.26.
ον, (< οὐρίζω¹) driven by a too favourable wind, fatally favourable, S. OT 1315 (lyr.).
δυσφύλακτον, Hsch.
ον, offensive to the sight, αἶσχος Telest. 1.3.

or δυσπαθία (Hsch.), ἡ, deep affliction, Plu. 2.112b.
firmness in resisting, Plu. Demetr. 21 ; in pl., capabilities of endurance, Id. 2.666b ; insensitivity, Alex.Aphr. Pr. 1.39.

suffer a hard fate, Mosch. 4.84 ; of sickness, suffer severely, ῥινῷ δ. Nic. Th. 381 ; to be in a bad way, Plb. 29.7.4.
to be impatient, ἐπί τινι, πρός τι, Plu. Aem. 36, Per. 33 ; ἔν τινι Id. 2.77e.

ές, (< παθεῖν) feeling to excess, opp. ἀπαθής, ib. 102d.
not easily affected, τὸ ὅμοιον ὑπὸ τοῦ ὁμοίου δυσπαθέστερον ib. 651c ; abs., impassive, ib. 454c, Luc. Anach. 24, Plot. 1.4.8.
ον, rough and steep, βῆσσαι Archil. 115 ; κύματα B. 5.26 ; Ὄθρυς Nic. Th. 145 ; rough, λάχνη Oppian. H. 2.369, cf. C. 2.381, al.
unhappy child, Sch. rec. S. OT 1243.
[ᾰ], ον, hard to wrestle with, [Epich.] 254 ; ἀρά A. Ch. 692 ; πράγματα Id. Supp. 468 ; γῆρας E. Supp. 1108 ; δύναμις X. HG 5.2.18 ; cf. δυσπέλαστος, unskilled at wrestling, Philostr. Gym. 40.

[ᾰᾰ], ον, hard to struggle with, δόλοι θεῶν A. Eu. 847 (lyr.) ; hard to beat, περὶ τὴν τέχνην Tz. ap. Suid. s.v. Λυκόφρων. helpless ; Adv. δυσπαλάμως, ὀλέσθαι to perish helplessly, A. Supp. 867 (lyr.).

ές, hard to wrestle with, δίνα A. Eu. 559 (lyr.) ; difficult, c. inf., διακρίνειν… δυσπαλές [ἐστι] Pi. O. 8.25, cf. P. 4.273, Cerc. Fr. Oxy. 26.
dangerous, noxious, ῥίζαι ARh. 4.52.
stubborn, Nicom. Harm. 3.
δυστάραχος, δυσκίνητος, Hsch. ; cf. δυσπέμφελος.
gloss on δυσοδοπαίπαλος, Sch. A. Eu. 387.
ον, incomparable, Plu. Ant. 27.
ον, hard to assist, Plb. 5.22.7.
ον, hard to persuade, A. Supp. 108 (lyr.).
ον, hardly to be reduced to rule or formulated, Plb. 12.25i. 7.
ον, hard to define, ποσότης Plb. 16.12.10 ; hard to state precisely, Id. 18.15.1 ; hard to terminate, of life, Phld. Herc. 1251.16.
ον, hard to mislead, Poll. 8.10.
ον, hard to admit or believe, S.E. M. 9.42, Alex.Aphr. in Sens. 18.18. Act., hardly admitting, Sor. 2.62. Adv., metaph, δυσπαραδέκτως ἔχειν to be sceptical, Plb. 12.4.7.
ον, hard to assuage, A. Supp. 386 (lyr.).

ον, hard to move by prayer, inexorable, φρένες A. Pr. 34 ; ὀργή Plb. 30.31.13 ; of a person, Plu. Cat. Mi. 1.
difficult to refuse, Id. 2.531d, 602f.
ον, inexorable, Sch. S. OT 334 ; τὸ δ. τοῦ τρόπου J. AJ 16.5.4 (v.l. δυσπαραιτ-).
ον, hard to follow, i.e. hard to understand, Men. 490, DH. Pomp. 5, Corn. ND 7, J. AJ 11.3.10, Arr. Epict. 2.12.10. Act., hard of understanding, dull, M.Ant 5.5 (Comp.).
ον, hard to carry along, Plu. Demetr. 19 ; πλοῦς δ. a difficult voyage, Plb. 3.61.2.

[ῡ], ον, hard to appease, Pl. Ti. 69d, Plu. Mar. 45.
admitting no consolation, συμφορά, πάθος, J. AJ 2.9.2, Poll. 3.101.
ον, hard to dissuade, prob. in Arist. Phgn. 809a35 (Comp.).
ον, hard to sail along, Str. 16.4.18.
ουν, = δυσπαράπλευστος, DS. 3.44.
ον, hard to alter or forge, Gal. 14.52, Ammon. Diff. 74.
ον, hard to observe, Antig. Mir. 126, Porph. Abst. 3.4.
ον, hard to seduce or bribe, Poll. 8.10.
ον, ill-mated, λέκτρον S. Tr. 791.

ον, = δυσπαρήγορος, ἐπιθυμία J. AJ 16.7.4.
inconsolable, Plu. 2.74e ; admitting no consolation, συμφορά Phalar. Ep. 144.1 ; hard to soothe, ἄλγημα Herod.Med. ap. Aët. 9.2.
ον, hard to appease, A. Eu. 384 (lyr.).
ον, a virgin to her cost, Ἠχώ Nonn. D. 16.324 ; Αὔρη ib. 48.421.
ιδος, ὁ, unhappy Paris, Paris of ill omen, Il. 3.39, 13.769, Luc. DMort. 19.1.
ον, hard to pass, X. An. 4.1.25.
ον, hard to enter, Apollod. Hist. ap. Ath. 15.682d.
Pass., have a severe attack, of fever, Alex.Trall. Febr. 2.
ον, hard to the feet, ὁδός Luc. Trag. 227.
ον, hard to stop or appease, Gal. 1.334.
ἡ, indiscipline, disobedience, App. BC 1.48.
to be refractory, POxy. 44.6 (i AD).

ές, hard to persuade, not easily talked over, Pl. Phdr. 271d.
self-willed, disobedient, Id. Lg. 880a, Hierocl. p. 63A. ; κύνες X. Mem. 4.1.3 (Sup.).
hard to believe, Phld. D. 3.12. Adv. -θῶς, ἔχειν πρός τι Plu. Galb. 25 ; δ. φέρειν Id. Lys. 15 ; with difficulty, κάμπτεσθαι Hero Bel. 75.9.
Ion. -ίη, ἡ, difficulty of learning by experiment, Hp. Hum. 1.
disbelieve, Tz. H. 7.34.

ον, hard to persuade, opinionated, Arist. EN 1151b6 ; ὄμματα ἀκοῆς D.Chr. 12.71 (Comp.). Adv. -τως, ἔχειν to be incredulous, Isoc. 4.18.
disobedient, X. Eq. Mag. 1.23.
ον, dangerous to come near, δ. ἀμαθία κακόν (Nauck δυσπάλαιστον) S. Fr. 924.
ον, hard to banish, A. Ag. 1190.

ον, rough and stormy, εἰ καὶ δυσπέμφελος εἴη (sc. πόντος) Il. 16.748 ; as a general epith. of the sea, οἳγλαυκὴν δυσπέμφελον ἐργάζονται Hes. Th. 440 ; ναυτιλίη δ. stormy passage, Id. Op. 618 ; αὔρη Nonn. D. 2.550 ; metaph, rude, uncourteous, Hes. Op. 722 ; δ. εὐνή, of a wife, Max. 88.
ον, of an evil father-in-law, θεσμά Nonn. D. 3.309.
to be sore afflicted, Plu. 2.106a (v.l.).

ές, bringing sore affliction, direful, κάματος Pi. P. 12.10 ; δόλος ib. 11.18 ; θαλάμοιο… δυσπενθέα κόσμον Epigr.Gr. 431 (Antioch) ; Ἀΐδας IPE 2.286.5 (Panticapaeum).
bitterly lamented, of the dead, Oppian. H. 4.261.
ον, hard to soften, Sch. S. Aj. 205.
digest with difficulty, Dsc. 5.6 ; — Pass., Id. 4.82.

ον, hard to digest, Arist. GA 776a12, al., Nicom.Com. 1.31, Dsc. 1.125 ; refusing to be assimilated, Pl. Ti. 83a.
unripe, v.l. ap. Sch. in Nic. Al. 297.
ον, = δυσπέρατος, ποταμός Ps.-Callisth. 3.10.
ον, hard to pass or cross, ὑπερβολαὶ ὄρους Str. 4.6.6, cf. 15.1.26 (Comp.) ; metaph, ἀμηχανίας δ. αἰών E. Med. 646 (lyr.).
ον, hard to wheel about, Arr. Tact. 16.8.
ον, hard to strip off, peel, φλοιός prob. in Thphr. HP 5.1.1.
ον, hard to overcome, Ph. 1.621.
ον, hard to treat comprehensively, πραγματεία Sor. 1.78.
ον, hard to peel, clean off, φλοιός Thphr. HP 5.1.1 codd. (leg. -αίρετος).
ον, not successful in acquiring property, Paul.Al. N. 3.

ον, hard to encompass, γαστήρ Posidon. 6 J. ; πόλις τοῖς ἐναντίοις δ. Arist. Pol. 1330b3 ; στελέχη δ. πέντε ἀνθρώποις Str. 15.1.21.
hard to embrace in one view, treat synoptically, DS. 1.3.
hard to get, φιλήματα AP 12.200 (Strat.).
ον, hard to conceive, Ph. 1.570.
ον, hard to overturn, ἕδρα Gal. UP 3.9. Adv. -τως Id. 18(1).591.
ον, hard to chill, Dsc. 1.30, Sor. 1.100.
fall out ill, Suid.
ατος, τό, misfortune, LXX 2 Ma. 5.20.
ές, falling out ill, most difficult, μαθεῖν δ. S. Aj. 1046. Adv. -τῶς, Ion. -έως Hdt. 3.107 ; δ. φέρειν Hp. Prog. 15, A. Pr. 752 ; Comp. -εστέρως Hp. Morb. 1.22.
ἡ, indigestion, Macho ap. Ath. 8.341b, Ph. 2.352, Dsc. 5.45, Gal. 7.66.
ον, full of grievous evil, disastrous, A. Eu. 481 (as Scaliger for δυσπήματ’ ; cf. δυσκύμαντος).
ές, squalid, στολαί S. OC 1597, cf. Ar. Ach. 426.
mistrust, τινί Plu. 2.593a.
ἡ, disbelief, Aët. 7.118.

ον, hard of belief, distrustful ; Adv. -τως, ἔχειν πρός τι to be incredulous about a thing, Pl. Erx. 405b. Pass., hard to be believed, Vett.Val. 108.13, Palaeph. 30 ; Comp., D.Chr. 32.64.
superstitious, Hsch.
ον, wandering in misery, A. Pr. 608 (lyr.) ; δ. ἀλατείαις ib. 900 (lyr.).

ον, not easily terrified, ὑπὸ φόβων Ph. 2.665, cf. Andronic. Rhod. p. 575 M.
hard to hit, Simp. in Cat. 247.7.
ον, hard to fill or fulfil, Poll. 9.21.
f.l. for δασπλῆτις, Lyc. 1452, Suid.
Ion. δυσπλοΐη, ἡ, difficulty of sailing, AP 7.630 (Antiphil.), Str. 1.2.31 ; pl., Ph. 1.601 ; — written δυσπλωΐα, Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.178.
ον, contr. δύσπλους, ουν, dangerous for ships, Κρήτα AP 7.275 (Gaet.).
ουν, contr. for δύσπλοος.
ον, hard to wash clean, Hp. Mul. 2.122.
= δυσπλοΐα.
ον, = δύσπλοος, AP 7.699.
ον, gloss on δυσαής, Hsch.
Ion. δυσπνοιέω, breathe with difficulty, Aret. SD 1.11, Gal. 19.423.
ον, dub. in Hp. Judic. 35.

ἡ, difficulty of breathing, shortness of breath, Hp. Aph. 3.31, X. Cyn. 9.20, Nymphis 16, Aret. SA 1.9, etc.
contrary winds, Sch. ARh. 4.1.
ή, όν, short of breath, Dsc. 4.134 (v.l.), Asclep. ap. Gal. 13.108, Hippiatr. 27.

ον, contr. δύσπνους, ουν, scant of breath, Hp. Prog. 17 (Comp.), S. Ant. 224.
unfit to breathe, ἀήρ Thphr. Ign. 24. δ. πνοαί contrary winds, S. Ant. 588 (lyr.).
ουν, contr. for δύσπνοος.
ον, hard to war with, A. Supp. 648 (lyr., s.v.l.), Isoc. 4.138 ; εἰ δέ τις… δ. οἴεται τὸν φίλιππον εἶναι D. 4.4 ; δ. ὅπλον, offriendship, Luc. Tox. 36.
ον, unlucky in war, A. Pers. 1013 (lyr.). = δυσπολέμητος, Γαλάται IG 11(4).1105 (Delos, iii BC), LXX 2 Ma. 12.21.
ον, hard to take by siege, X. HG 4.8.5 (Comp.), Plb. 5.3.4, J. AJ 2.10.2 ; τὸ δ. Corn. ND 20.
ον, unfit for public business, τὸ δ. Plu. Dio 32.
ές, toilsome, δυσπονέος καμάτοιο Od. 5.493. Adv. -έως Max. 194.
ον, bringing toil and trouble, δαίμων A. Pers. 515 ; δυσπόνητον ἕξετ’ ἀμφ’ ἐμοὶ τροφήν laborious, S. OC 1614.
ἡ, toil and trouble, Man. 4.260.
ον, toilsome, S. Ant. 1276 (lyr.).
ον, hard to pass, πηλὸς ταῖς ἁμάξαις δ. X. An. 1.5.7 ; ἀνοδίαι Ph. 2.14 ; ὁδοί DC. 53.22.
have a toilsome march, J. BJ 3.6.2.
ον, hard to sack, Sch. rec. A. Pr. 166.
ἡ, difficulty of passing, τοῦ ποταμοῦ X. An. 4.3.7.

ον, hard to come by or procure, opp. εὐπ., Epicur. Ep. 3 p. 63U., cf. Phld. Herc. 1251.12, DH. 1.37, D.Chr. 7.152, Muson. Fr. 18A p. 94 H., Plu. 2.156f ; σχήματα Alex. Fig. 1.1 ; δ. ἡ ἀρετὴ τοῦ σωφρονεῖν J. AJ 19.2.5 ; τὸ δ. difficulty of getting, τῶν ἀναγκαίων Ph. 1.19, cf. Plu. Sol. 23.

ον, scarcely passable, Pl. Cra. 420e, X. An. 6.5.12.
difficult to get, τροφή Corn. ND 28, Poll. 5.105.
despair of oneself, ἐν ἀρρωστίαις Plb. 33.17.1.
ἡ, ill luck, ill success, DH. 9.28, Them. Or. 13.170a.

ον, unlucky, ill-starred, of persons and things, δ. θεός, of Prometheus, A. Pr. 119 ; δ. βοῦς, of Io, Id. Supp. 306 ; δ. εὐχαί, i.e. curses, Id. Th. 820 ; χλιδά S. OT 888 (lyr.) ; θήρα E. Ba. 1144, cf. Ar. Ach. 419 ; τύχαι DH. 1.17 ; Comp. -ώτερος E. Ph. 1348 ; Sup. -ότατος Plu. Comp. Per. Fab. 1. Adv. -μως A. Pers. 272 (lyr.) ; Sup. -ότατα Plu. Fab. 18.
ον, unpalatable, πῶμα A. Eu. 266.
ποδος, ὁ, ἡ, slow of foot, Call. Fr. 1.63 P.
to be unlucky, A. Ag. 790 (anap.), Plu. Ant. 63, Al. Jb. 5.24.
ές, faring ill, Vett.Val. 16.21.
ill luck, ill success, Gorg. Hel. 9 (pl.), Antipho 2.49, Ph. 2.75, Jul. ad Them. 257b.
ον, hard to manage, λαός Plu. 2.348f.
ον, hard to do, Poll. 3.131, 5.105.
ἡ, ill success, ill luck, A. Pr. 966, S. OC 1399, And. 2.5, Men. 707 ; pl., A. Eu. 769, S. Aj. 759, Isoc. 6.102.
ον, hard to sell ; name of a play by Antiphanes, Ath. 6.262c.
ον, hard to tame, Hsch. s.v. δυσγάργαλις.
ἡ, indecency, J. AJ 3.7.4.
ές, base, undignified, E. Hel. 300.
ον, hard to saw through, Thphr. HP 5.6.3.
ον, making progress with difficulty, Vett.Val. 76.24.
ον, hard to approach, Th. 4.129, DC. 56.12.
ον, hardly admitted, disagreeable, Plu. 2.39d. Act., disinclined to entertain, διαβολῆς M.Ant 1.5.
ον, hard to speak with, repulsive, DC. Fr. 11.6, Poll. 1.42. Adv. -ρως Id. 5.139.
ον, difficult of access or attack, πόλις DH. 4.54, cf. DS. 15.42, Onos. 11.6 ; λιμὴν δ. ναυσί J. BJ 4.10.5 ; τεῖχος DC. 40.34 ; of a man, E. IA 345.
ον, hard to attack, Plu. Tim. 21.
ον, hard to get into, λιμήν Poll. 1.101.

ον, difficult of access, χωρίον Th. 5.65, cf. Aen.Tact. 28.1 (Sup.) ; δ. τοῖς ἐναντίοις πόλις Arist. Pol. 1330b3 ; hard to assault, τάξις, παρεμβολή, Plb. 1.26.10, 2.65.12. of men, unsocial, δ. αὑτὸν παρέχειν Th. 1.130, cf. X. Ages. 9.2, Luc. Scyth. 6, Plu. Demetr. 42, DC. Fr. 11.6.
ον, hard to approach, στόμα S. OC 1277.
ον, hard to look on, horrid to behold, κάρα τὸ δ. ib. 286 ; ὀνείρατα Id. El. 460 ; ὄψις καὶ κίνησις Plu. Aem. 12. Adv. -τως Agatharch. 26.
ον, hard to land on, having few ports, Plb. 1.37.4 ; δ. ἀπόβασις a difficult landing, DS. 1.31.
ον, = δυσπροσόρμιστος, Scymn. 726.
ον, hard to get at, Plu. Pomp. 28 ; gloss on δασπλῆτις, Sch. Od. 15.234.
ον, bad for foraging in, χώρα Aen.Tact. 8.1.
ον, hard to apply, of stiff ointment, Gal. 11.134 (ap. Orib. 44.15.21).
ον, hard to speak with, condemned by Poll. 5.138.
ον, of ill aspect, sour looks, Artem. 3.47, f.l. in Plu. Mar. 15, cf. Men. Rh. p. 416S.
ον, hard to pronounce, Mart.Cap. 5.514.
ές, hard to break, Luc. Anach. 24 (Comp.).
ιδος, ἡ, name of a plaster, Crito ap. Gal. 13.797.
ον, hardly flowing, of thick water, S.E. M. 5.75 (Comp.).
ον, hard to break through, Gal. UP 15.5, DC. 62.8.

ον, that should not be spoken, Demetr. Eloc. 302.
hard to give a name to, Gal. 12.501.

ον, impatient of cold, sensitive to cold, ζῷα Hdt. 5.10, cf. Arist. HA 605a20 (Sup.), Men. 1007, J. AJ 7.14.3, Plu. 2.916a ; of plants, Thphr. HP 6.7.3. Adv. -γως Ruf. ap. Orib. 8.24.61, Agathin. ib. 10.7.17 ; Comp. -οτέρως, διάγειν Arist. Pr. 863a2.
flow ill, i.e. to be unlucky, Arr. Epict. 1.28.30, al.
ή, όν, leading to ill luck, ib. 4.1.58.
ἡ, bad circulation, Anon. Lond. 4.17 ; metaph, ill luck, misfortune, Arr. Epict. 2.17.18.
ον, contr. δύσρους, ρουν, sluggish, γαστήρ Orib. 8.35.6, cf. Gal. 8.358.
ρουν, contr. for δύσροος,
ον, healing with difficulty, of ulcers, Gal. 12.188, Aët. 2.187.

ἡ, impiety, ungodliness, πρὸς δυσσεβείας ἦν it verged on impiety, A. Ch. 704 ; παντὸς ἔργου δ. S. Ant. 301 ; a charge of impiety, τὴν δ. εὐσεβοῦσ’ ἐκτησάμην ib. 924. — In Lyrics also δυσσεβία, A. Eu. 533 ; -ίη Nonn. D. 20.404.
to be ungodly, S. Tr. 1245 ; οἱ δυσσεβοῦντες A. Eu. 910, E. Med. 755.
ατος, τό, impious act, LXX 2 Ma. 12.3, DH. 7.44, Scymn. 684, etc.

ές, ungodly, impious, profane, of persons, A. Th. 598 (Comp. or Sup.), and their acts, δ. χάρις S. Ant. 514 ; τὰ τῶν κακίστων δυσσεβέστατα Id. OC 1190 ; δ. μέλαθρα E. IT 694. Adv. -βῶς Id. Fr. 825. — This family of words is chiefly found in Trag. (δυσσεβής occurs in Men. 540, Diph. 105, and later Prose as Jul. Or. 5.174b (Sup.)) ; εὐσεβής, etc., are freq. also in Prose.
ἡ, v. δυσσέβεια.
ον, hard to shake, Hsch.
ον, not easily rotting, κρέα Plu. 2.725b ; δένδρα Id. in Hes. 7, cf. Gal. 10.942, al.
ον, hard to save, ruined, Theoc. 3.24 ; τὰ δ. the rogues, Id. 4.45, cf. Riv. Indogr. 8.266 (Camarina, v BC).
ον, ill-suited for encamping, Aen.Tact. 8.1.
ον, condescending with difficulty, πρὸς τὰς ἐξωτερικὰς φιλίας prob. cj. in Iamb. VP 31.194.
ον, hard to conceive, σπέρματα Sor. 1.41.
ον, hard to reason out, Gal. 8.882.
ον, ill-agreeing, πρὸς τὸ ἀλλόφυλον Plu. 2.661c.
v. δυσξύμβλητος.
v. δυσξύμβολος.
v. δυσξύμβολος.
ἡ, difficulty in coalescing, Gal. 19.401.
ον, not coalescing easily, Gal. 8.873.
ον, hardly growing together, Gal. 10.336 ; τραύματα Sor. 1.38.
ον, hard to grasp as a whole, of an argument, Simp. in Ph. 1272.13.
ον, hard to bring together, πλῆθος J. BJ 4.4.6.
ον, hard to deal with, Vett.Val. 115.9.
ον, with a bad conscience, Vett.Val. 37.29, al.
ἡ, lack of understanding, Simp. in Ph. 1147.9.
ον, hard to get a view of, Plb. 3.84.2, etc. ; metaph, Iamb. VP 30.182.
δύσμαχον, Hsch.
Adv. with small chance of survival, ἔχειν Hippiatr. 71.
ον, ill-regulated, disordered, Pl. Lg. 781a. (for δύσστακτον) = κακοδάκρυτον, Hsch.
αινα, αν, most miserable, S. Aj. 410, etc. ; freq. in E. in fem., Med. 1028, al., masc. twice in E., δ. σὺ τῆσδε συμφορᾶς Hipp. 1407, cf. Supp. 1034.
ον, (< στέλλω) hard to check, Hippiatr. 9.
ον, hard to manage, πνεῦμα Arist. Aud. 800b31.
Dor. for δύστηνος.
ον, very stormy, Hsch. s.v. δυσήνεμον.
to be unstable, αἰσθήσεις Plu. 2.1124b.

ον, hard to make out from signs, hard to trace, ἴχνος S. OT 109 ; δ. τέχνη, of the art of interpreting auspices, A. Pr. 497 ; ποικίλον τι καὶ δ. E. Hel. 712 ; τέλος DH. 4.29 ; γνώμη Plu. Cat. Mi. 72 ; δ. πατὴρ τῶν ὅλων Ph. 1.467 ; hard to estimate, Aret. CA 1.4.
ἡ, ill luck in the matter of children, Man. 2.179.
ον, unfortunate in one΄s children, S. OT 1248, Vett.Val. 18.5, Cat.Cod.Astr. 1.149.
δυσχερὲς τέλος ἔχον, ἢ μὴ ἔχον τέλος, Hsch.
ές, ill-pleasing, A. Ch. 277.
ον, unsuccessful, Doroth. in Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.174.
ἡ, difficulty in securing, πραγμάτων Heph.Astr. 2.28.
ον, (< τήκω) hard to melt, Hp. Alim. 51, Plu. 2.701b.
ἡ, = μοχθηρία, Hsch.

Dor. δύστανος, ον, wretched, unhappy, unfortunate, disastrous, poet. Adj. ; mostly of persons, as always in Hom. and mostly Trag., A. Pers. 909 (anap.), etc. ; δυστήνων δέ τε παῖδες ἐμῷ μένει ἀντιόωσιν unhappy are they whose sons…, Il. 6.127. of sufferings and the like, μόχθος δ. Pi. P. 4.268 ; θέρος A. Ag. 1655 ; αἰκίαι S. El. 511 (lyr.) ; ὄνειδος Id. Aj. 1191 (lyr.) ; ὄνειρος Ar. Ra. 1333 (lyr.) ; πάθος DH. 6.20. Adv., Sup. δυστανοτάτως γηράσκω E. Supp. 967 (lyr.). after Hom., in moral sense, wretched, S. El. 121 (Sup., lyr.), Ph. 1016 ; λόγοι E. HF 1346. — Rare in Prose, though D. 19.255 has δ. λογάρια, in latter sense ; Sup. (v. supr. 1) ; no Comp. is found. (Cf. ἄστηνος.)
ον, hard to keep, κάλλος Ps.-Phoc. 217 ; θηρίον Plu. Cleom. 36.
ον, bad for scent, Plu. 2.917e, 918a.
ον, hard to tame, Str. 15.1.42, Plu. 2.529b ; τὸ δ. Artem. 3.12.
ον, gen. ονος, suffering hard things, h.Ap. 532, Orph. Fr. 49vi95.
ον, hard to bear, Ἀνάγκη Emp. 116, A. Ag. 1571 (anap.) ; δύστλητα τολυπεύειν IG 14.2123.
ἡ, one who has borne a child to misery, dub. in Hsch.
έως, ὁ, ἡ, suffering in child-birth, δυστοκέες ἀλετρίδες Call. Del. 242 ; unhappy parent, δ. τοκέες IG 14.2125.
suffer in childbirth, Hp. Aph. 5.35, Pl. Tht. 149d, Arist. HA 587a4 ; metaph, ἡ πόλις δυστοκεῖ Ar. Ra. 1423, cf. Aristid. Or. 31 (11).11.
ἡ, painful delivery, Arist. HA 587a10 (pl.), Thphr. HP 9.16.1 (pl.). = δυστεκνία, Man. 1.46.
ον, born for mischief, δάκος E. Fr. 863.
(< στόμα) speak evil of, τινά τι S. OC 986.
ἡ, (< στόμα) difficulty in pronunciation, Phld. Po. 2.24.

ον, (< στόμα) hard-mouthed, of a horse, ἱππείη APl. 4.361, Hippiatr. Praef.
hard to pronounce, συλλαβή Phld. Po. 2.15.
ον, (< τέμνω) hard to cut, Thphr. HP 3.14.1.
ον, (< στένω) lamentable, grievous, A. Th. 989 (lyr., codd.), Ch. 469 (lyr.).
δυσχερῶς ὑπονοήσαντες, Hsch.
ον, hard to guess, ὅστις ποτ’ εἶ σύ, δυστόπαστος εἰδέναι E. Tr. 885 ; Φοίβου δυστόπαστ’ αἰνίγματα Id. Supp. 138, cf. Phld. Mort. 37 ; αἰτία Plu. Rom. 21 ; κοσμοποιός Ph. 1.570.
= δύστηνος, Hdn. Gr. 1.217.
ον, hard to hit upon, καιρός Plu. Ant. 28, cf. Dsc. Ther. Praef.
ον, fed on horrid food, E. HF 385 (lyr.).
= δυστραπελία.
or δυστραπέλεια, ἡ, difficulty of managing, DS. 4.11, 5.15 ; ἐν τοῖς καταγείοις Id. 17.82 ; unhealthiness, τόπου Iamb. VP 19.92.

ον, difficult to deal with, φλέψ Hp. Oss. 16 ; πρᾶγμα Henioch. 4.4, cf. Plu. 2.419a ; ὀφθαλμία Sor. 2.15. of persons, intractable, stubborn, S. Aj. 914 (lyr.), Arist. EE 1234a5. Adv. -λως awkwardly, clumsily, X. Oec. 8.16 ; with difficulty, Gal. 14.114.
to be stiff-necked, stubborn, Tz. H. 1.427.
ον, hard to pierce or bore, of in ferior pearls, Suid.
ον, hard to bruise or grind, Artem. 1.70, Hippiatr. 1.
ἡ, peevishness, Poll. 5.119, Jul. Mis. 365b, Alex.Trall. 7.9.
ή, όν, peevish, Sch. Ar. Ra. 848.

ον, (< τρόπος) ill-conditioned, surly, peevish, δ. γυναικῶν ἁρμονία E. Hipp. 161 ; δύσκολος καὶ δ. D. 6.30, Ph. 1.621 ; δ. καὶ σκυθρωπαὶ φύσεις Plu. 2.361b. Adv. δυστρόπως, λογιστεύειν Philostr. VS 1.19.2.
μήν, ὁ, name of a Macedonian month, OGI 55 (iii BC), AP 11.243 (Nicarch.), etc.
ον, hard to rear, Thphr. CP 1.8.4.
ον, hard to bore through, Thphr. HP 5.6.3 (Comp.).
ον, hard to injure, σιδήρῳ καὶ λίθῳ Plu. 2.983d, cf. Apollod. Poliorc. 139.8 ; Comp., Gal. UP 1.2.
ον, not easily taking an impress, Gal. 1.322.

Ion. impf. ἐδυστύχεον Hdt. 8.105 ; aor. ἐδυστύχησα Pl. Mx. 243a ; pf. δεδυστύχηκα Id. La. 183c, Isoc. 4.55, Lyc.Trag. 5 ; — Pass., v. infr. : — to be unlucky, unfortunate, Hdt. l.c., etc. ; ἐπεύχομαι τῷδε μὲν εὐτυχεῖν… τοῖσι δὲ δ. A. Th. 482 (lyr.), cf. S. Ant. 1159 ; γάμοις E. Ph. 424 ; παίδων πέρι Id. Andr. 713 ; ἔν τινι Ar. Ra. 1449 ; εἴς τι Pl. La. 183c ; κατὰ γῆν καὶ κατὰ θάλατταν Id. Alc. 2.148d ; περί τι Plu. Cam. 11 ; c. acc., πάντα δυστυχῶ E. Hec. 429 ; δυστυχεῖν ἄμορφον γυναῖκα to be curst with…, AP 11.287 (Pall.) ; μανίαν Ach.Tat. 4.17 ; τῆς ἀλλοδαπῆς βαρυτέραν τὴν πατρίδα δυστυχήσασα Hld. 10.16 ; — Pass. in same sense, ὅταν τις δυστυχηθῇ is made unfortunate, Pl. Lg. 877e ; τὰ ὑφ’ ἑτέρων δυστυχηθέντα Lys. 2.70, cf. Plu. Pyrrh. 4.
ατος, τό, piece of ill luck, failure, misfortune, And. 2.9, Lys. 24.3 (pl.), Pl. Cra. 395d (pl.), Onos. 36.4 (pl.) ; esp. of defeat in war, X. HG 4.5.18, etc.

ές, unlucky, unfortunate, of persons and things, Th. 7.87, Pl. Lg. 832a, etc. ; freq. in Trag., δυστυχῆ πράσσειν A. Th. 339 (lyr.) ; δ. βίος S. El. 602 ; δ. εἴς τι E. Ph. 1642 ; τά τ’ ἔνδον τά τε θύραζε δ. Id. Or. 604 ; τὸ δυστυχές A. Ch. 913. Adv. -χῶς Id. Ag. 1660, Pl. Lg. 687e, etc. of the Erinyes, δ. κόραι ill-starred, harbingers of ill, A. Eu. 791 (lyr.).
ἡ, ill luck, ill fortune, E. Ba. 388 (lyr.), al. ; τοῦ πάθους ἡ δ. Th. 6.55, etc.
ον, scant of water, J. AJ 2.11.2, Ph. 2.516.
ον, hard to pass over, Ph.Mech. Bel. 82.35.
sleep ill, Pl. Lg. 790d.
Adv. ἔχειν suffer from insomnia, Agathin. ap. Orib. 10.7.27. [To be deleted (Suppl.)]
ον, sleeping badly, ib. 10.
ον, hard to carry off by purging, etc., Diph. Siph. ap. Ath. 3.74c, Gal. 6.535.
ον, hard to endure, AP 5.162 (Mel.), J. AJ 15.7.1 ; hard to carry, βάρος Archig. ap. Aët. 13.120.
ον, = δυσυπομόνητος, S.E. M. 9.154.
ον, hard to abide, Ph. 2.287, 432, Sor. 1.80.
ον, hard to detect the nature of, of a person, Ph. 2.268 ; μῖσος ib. 201.
ον, hard to withstand, βία DS. 17.11 ; of a person, Plu. Cor. 8.
gloss on δυσύποιστος, Suid.
ές, scarce visible, ἥλιος Plu. 2.431f.
Dor. for δύσφημος.
ές, dark, obscure, νύξ Plu. Luc. 9 ; metaph, σώματος ψυχὴ δυσφανέστερόν τι χρῆμα Them. Or. 1.2c.
ον, hard to imagine, Plu. 2.432c.

ον, hard to speak, unutterable, A. Ag. 1152 (lyr.).
hard to explain, Lyc. 10.
ές, shining ill, gloomy, Poll. 5.109.
ές, intolerable, Hsch.
ον, hard to be avoided, κακόν Men. Georg. 12, cf. Ph. 2.268.

use ill words, esp. words of ill omen, A. Ag. 1078, S. El. 905, Plu. Cic. 22.
trans., speak ill of, S. El. 1183, E. Heracl. 600, Hec. 181 (lyr.), Phld. Rh. 1.215 S., Them. Or. 13.178a ; — Pass., Phld. Mort. 36.
ατος, τό, word of ill omen, Plu. 2.1065e.

ἡ, ill language, esp. words of ill omen, κατεῖχε… πᾶν στρατόπεδον δυσφημίαις S. Ph. 10, dub. in J. AJ 16.4.1 ; pl., curses, Plu. 2.587f, cf. Pel. 8 ; but, unsavoury details, Demetr. Eloc. 302.
blasphemy, slander, DH. 6.48, etc.
ill fame, obloquy, S. Fr. 178 (pl.), Them. Or. 7.99c.
ον, = δύσφημος, Suid. s.v. δυσκληδόνιστος.

Dor. δύσφαμος, ον, of ill omen, boding, Hes. Op. 735 ; opp. εὔφημος, E. Andr. 1144, Pl. Hp. Ma. 293a. Adv. -μως, ἱερουργεῖν Zen. 4.95.
slanderous, shameful, ἔπη Thgn. 307 ; λόγος Men. 715 ; abusive, Plu. Luc. 18. Adv. -μως Phryn. PS p. 62 B.
of ill fame, evil, κλέος Pi. N. 8.37.
ἡ, evil talk, Phld. Sto. 339.20.
ον, hard to destroy, S.E. M. 9.19 ; not easily spoilt, Diph. Siph. ap. Ath. 3.121c, Hices. ib. 87d, Xenocr. 73 (Comp.), Dsc. 2.9.
ον, unfit to be uttered, Poll. 3.129, 5.123.
ον, hard-sounding, Demetr. Eloc. 246.
ές, hateful, δάκος A. Ag. 1232 ; γαμήλευμα Id. Ch. 624 ; γέρων S. OC 1258, etc.

impf. ἐδυσφόρουν Hp. Epid. 3.1. γ΄, X. Cyr. 2.2.8 : — to be impatient, angry, vexed, Hdt. 5.19, A. Supp. 513, S. El. 255, Pherecr. 22 D., Ar. Th. 73, Men 543.7, etc. ; κακοῖς E. Andr. 1234 ; ἐπί τινι A. Th. 780 (lyr.), J. AJ 1.10.4, Hdn. 3.9.7 ; περὶ τὰς ἀναστάσιας to feel ill on getting up, Hp. l.c. ; διά τι DS. 4.61 ; — Med., X. Cyr. 2.2.8, Procop. Arc. 10, 12 ; — Pass., S. Ichn. 329, v.l. in X. Cyr. 2.2.5.
ον, hard to be borne, Hsch. ; f.l. for διαφόρητος, E. Cyc. 344.

ἡ, malaise, discomfort, Hp. Acut. 54, Epid. 1.26. ηʹ, Coac. 260 ; classed as εἶδος λύπης, Stoic. 3.100.
vexation, distress, Epicur. Fr. 445 (pl.), Simp. in Epict. p. 117 D.
ή, όν, indicative of vexation, Eust. 1581.22.
ιγγος, ὁ, ἡ, unlike the lyre, mournful, E. IT 225 (lyr.).

ον, hard to bear, heavy, θώρακες X. Mem. 3.10.13. mostly of sufferings, hard to bear, grievous, θάμβος, μέριμνα, Pi. N. 1.55, Fr. 248 ; ἄτα, βίος, A. Eu. 372 (lyr., codd.), Ag. 859, etc. ; δ. γνῶμαι false, blinding fancies, S. Aj. 51 ; τὰ δ. our troubles, sorrows, Id. OT 87, cf. El. 144 (lyr.) ; δύσφορόν [ἐστι] X. Cyr. 1.6.17. Adv. δυσφόρως, διάγειν τὴν νύκτα Hp. Epid. 5.95 ; δ. φέρειν Id. Aph. 1.18 (Sup.), Hdn. 1.8.4 ; δ. ἔχειν S. OT 770 ; impatiently, τοὔνειδος ἦγον ib. 783. of food, oppressive, X. Cyr. 1.6.17.
bearing bad crops, χώρα Men. Rh. p. 345 S. (from Pass.) moving with difficulty, slow of motion, σώματα Pl. Ti. 74e ; ἵππος X. Eq. 1.12 (Comp.).
ον, hard to be borne or carried, CIG 3127 (Teos).
ἡ, difficulty of pronunciation, Eust. 852.58.
ον, cohesive, Steph. in Hp. 1.298 D.
ον, hard to tell or explain, mysterious, Pl. Ti. 50c ; generally, difficult, κέλευθα Oppian. H. 2.60. Act., speaking with difficulty, γλῶσσα Ezek. Exag. 114. Adv. -τως Lyc. 1466.
ἡ, = δυσφροσύνη, in pl., anxieties, troubles, δυσφρονέων ἐπιλήθεται Hes. Th. 102 ; in Pi. O. 2.52, παραλύει δυσφρονᾶν should be read (metri gr.) for δυσφροσύναν παραλύει, cf. ἀφρόνη, εὐφρόνη.
= δυσκηδής, Eust. 1546.41.
gloss on δυσαρεής, Hsch.
ἡ, anxiety, care, Hes. Th. 528, Simon. 86 (both times in Ep. gen. pl. δυσφροσυνάων) ; pl., E. Tr. 597 (lyr.), Ph. 2.75.

ον, gen. ονος, sad at heart, sorrowful, τὸ δ. στύγος A. Ag. 547 ; ἄτα S. OC 202 (lyr.) ; λῦπαι E. Andr. 1043 (lyr.).
ill-disposed, malignant, δράκοντες A. Supp. 511 ; ἰός Id. Ag. 834 ; οἱ δ. ib. 608 ; λόγοι E. Andr. 288 (lyr.). = ἄφρων, senseless, insensate, A. Th. 875 (lyr.) ; φρενῶν δυσφρόνων ἁμαρτήματα S. Ant. 1261 (lyr.). Adv. -όνως foolishly, rashly, A. Pers. 552 (lyr.).
ές, germinating tardily, Thphr. HP 7.1.3 ; Sup., ibid.
ἡ, tardy germination, opp. ταχυβλαστία, Thphr. CP 4.8.2.
= δυσωρέομαι, Eust. 797.28.

ον, hard to guard, δυσφύλακτον οὐδὲν ὡς γυνή Alex. 339 ; of a city, Plb. 2.55.2 ; πλοῦτος Str. 9.3.8 ; ἀρχή DC. 56.33.
hard to keep off or prevent, κακά E. Ph. 924, cf. Andr. 728 ; hard to guard against or avoid, τενάγη Str. 11.4.2 ; τὸ οἰδεῖν δυσφυλακτότατον Longin. 3.3.
κακὴ φύσις, Hsch.
ἡ, roughness of sound, Demetr. Eloc. 48, Poll. 2.112, Cat.Cod.Astr. 2.167.
ον, ill-sounding, harsh, Demetr. Eloc. 69 (Comp.), 105 ; κολοιοί Babr. 33.
ον, hard to detect, Plu. 2.51d.
βλάσφημοι, χαλεποί, Hsch.
ον, hard to rein, unbridled, Gal. 19.94 (s.v. δυσήνιος).
ον, thankless, τῶν πυκνῶν φιλημάτων A. Fr. 135.
ή, όν, = δυσχείμερος, τὰ δ. wintry climates, Thphr. HP 8.8.1.

ον, wintry or stormy, Hom. (only in Il.) epith. of Dodona, 2.750, al. ; χώρη Hdt. 4.28, cf. Arist. HA 606b5 ; φάραγξ A. Pr. 15 ; metaph, δ. πέλαγος δύης ib. 746 ; δ. ἆται Id. Ch. 271.
bearing winter ill, Arist. HA 596b5, Gp. 19.2.8.
ον, gen. ονος, = δυσχείμερος 1, ARh. 4.635.
ατος, τό, a hard conquest, incorrect formation in S. Ant. 126.
ον, hard to subdue, Hdt. 7.9. β’ (Sup.), D. 61.37, Plu. Alc. 4, DC. 53.25 (Comp.) ; Sup. δυσχειρότατον is prob. f.l. in DS. 5.34.
Adv. part. pres., with disgust, v.l. in Arist. Rh. 1408a17.

impf. ἐδυσχέραινον Pl. Tht. 169d ; aor. ἐδυσχέρανα S. OC 1282, Isoc. 12.201 ; aor. Pass. ἐδυσχεράνθην Plu. 2.820f ; (< δυσχερής) : — to be unable to endure or put up with, to be disgusted at, c. acc., Isoc. 14.46, Pl. Tht. 195c, D. 19.116, etc. ; θεούς Pl. Lg. 900a ; δ. τὸ γενέσθαι τι X. HG 7.4.2 ; τὸ ἀδικεῖν Pl. R. 362b ; c. acc. et part., to be annoyed at his doing, Aeschin. 1.158. mostly intr., feel dislike, disgust or annoyance, to be displeased, περί τινος And. 3.35 ; τινί at a thing, D. 55.11 ; ἐπί τινι Isoc. 1.26 ; πρός τι DH. Th. 34, Plu. Pyrrh. 21 ; κατά τινος Luc. Nav. 10 ; also δ. ἑαυτῷ to have misgivings, Arist. Metaph. 984a29 ; — Pass., to be hateful, ὄνομα δυσχεραινόμενον Plu. Publ. 1 ; δ. ὑπὸ πολλῶν Id. Cic. 24. c. inf., scorn to do a thing, Pl. R. 388a ; c. acc., δ. τι τῶν λεχθέντων feel qualms about, Id. Plt. 294a ; ταῦτ’ οὐκ ἐδυσχέραινεν felt no scruple about, Aeschin. 1.54 ; to be fastidious, περὶ τὰ μαθήματα Pl. R. 475b. causal, cause annoyance, ῥήματ’ ἢ τέρψαντά τι ἢ δυσχεράναντ’ S. OC 1282 ; δ. τὴν ὁδόν make it difficult, App. Ill. 18 ; — Pass., to be disagreeable, τοῖς ἀκούουσι Arist. Rh. Al. 1432b19 ; abs., ib. 1437a33. δ. ἐν τοῖς λόγοις to make difficulties in argument, to be captious, Pl. Grg. 450e.
εως, ἡ, disgust, Andronic. Rhod. p. 570 M., Plot. 1.9, Simp. in Epict. p. 45 D.
one must boggle at, θεόν Pl. Lg. 828d, al.
ή, όν, peevish, M.Ant 1.8, Hierocl. in CA 11 p. 444M. Adv. -κῶς, ζῆν Simp. in Epict. p. 35 D.
ατος, τό, in pl., harsh judgements, Pl. Phlb. 44d ; inconveniences, Dam. Isid. 66 ; — condemned by Poll. 3.133.

ἡ, opp. εὐχέρεια, of things, annoyance, disgust caused by a thing, τοῦ φορήματος, τοῦ νοσήματος, S. Ph. 473, 900, cf. Pl. Plt. 286b ; unpleasantness, of food, DC. 68.31 ; pl., Plu. 2.654b.
odium, unpopularity, Pl. Lg. 967c (pl.).
difficulty, troublesome question, Id. R. 502d, Isoc. 5.12 (pl.), etc. ; δ. παρέχειν Plb. 1.20.10 ; εἰς δ. ἐμπεσεῖν Id. 8.7.1 ; κατὰ τὴν προφοράν, opp. εὐχέρεια, Phld. Po. 994.8. in argument, difficulties, δ. λογικαί Arist. Metaph. 1005b22, cf. 995a 33. of persons, harshness, Pl. Phlb. 44c ; offensiveness, Thphr. Char. 19.
loathing, nausea, Pl. Prt. 334c.

ές, (< χείρ) hard to take in hand or manage, opp. εὐχερής ; of things, annoying, vexatious, θεωρία A. Pr. 802 ; πᾶσι θαῦμα δ. S. Ant. 254 ; Ἁρπάλου ἄφιξις Din. 2.5 ; of actions, odious, unpopular, Isoc. 12.63 (Sup.) ; disagreeable, Pl. Lg. 779e (Comp.) ; τὸ δ., = δυσχέρεια, E. Ph. 390 ; δυσχερὲς εἰπεῖν D. 18.3 ; δυσχερὲς ποιεῖσθαι to raise difficulties, Th. 4.85.
difficult, Pl. Hp. Mi. 369b (Sup.), etc. ; τύχη Lys. 24.6 (Sup.) ; βίος D. 60.24 ; τὰ δυσχερῆ difficulties, Id. 10.58, al. ; καιροὶ δ. difficult times, Inscr.Prien. 37.132. of arguments, contradictory, captious, Pl. Prt. 333d, D. 20.113 ; τὰ δυσχερῆ difficulties in an argument or discussion, Arist. EN 1145b6, Metaph. 1067b35. of persons, ill-tempered, unfriendly, τινί to one, S. El. 929 ; πρός τινα E. Ion 398 ; ἄτοποι καὶ δ. D. 19.308 ; δ. περὶ τὰ σιτία fastidious, Pl. R. 475c, cf. Arist. EE 1221b3.
unpleasant, offensive, Thphr. Char. 19.1 ; ὕδωρ DC. 68.31. Adv. δυσχερῶς, φέρειν, Lat. aegre ferre, Hp. Aph. 1.25 ; ἀποδέχεσθαι Pl. Euthphr. 6a ; δ. ἔχειν to be annoyed, πρός τι Id. Prt. 332a ; ἐπί τινι Amphis 34.
κακοτροπώτερον (Tarent.), Hsch.

ον, troublesome, dangerous, fearful, δράκων A. Th. 503 ; πλημμυρίς Id. Ch. 186 ; κέλευθοι Id. Pers. 567 (lyr.) ; ὄρη Id. Fr. 342 ; χθών, πνεύματα, E. Ba. 15, Supp. 962 (lyr.). (It is doubtful whether -χιμος (required by the metre in A.) is cognate with χεῖμα, hiems, cf. μελάγχιμος ; the form δύσχειμος is corrupt in A. Fr. 342, E. ll.cc.)
ον, hard to split, Thphr. CP 5.16.4.
ἡ, mean or shabby clothing, E. Hec. 240 ; in pl., τὰς ἐμὰς δυσχλαινίας Id. Hel. 416.
ον, difficult to stage, Plu. 2.712e.
ον, with little grass or food, δ. οἶκοι inhospitable dwellings, E. IT 219 (lyr.).
δυσχερής, Hsch.
ὐχμηρός, Hsch.

to be intractable, Plb. 27.7.10.
to be in difficulties or distress, Id. 4.60.8 ; ταῖς εἰρεσίαις Id. 16.4.10 ; διά τι Id. 1.51.6 ; περὶ τὴν ἔξοδον ib. 75.7 ; — also in Med., δ. ἐν τοῖς κινδύνοις ib. 87.7 ; πράγμασι, λόγοις, Id. 1.18.7, 3.11.4 ; of things, to be useless, Id. 16.3.5 ; — Pass., to be brought into distress, ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀπαντωμένοις ὑπ’ Ἀρχιμήδους Id. 8.6.5 ; to be annoyed, DS. 18.39 ; ἐπί τινι Id. 19.77.
ατος, τό, inconvenience, Stoic. 3.23.

ἡ, difficult position, awkward circumstances, εἰς δ. ἥκειν Plb. 11.25.1, cf. 5.26.2, al. ; distress, Phld. Ir. p. 52 W., Mort. 26 (pl.) ; of things, inconvenience, disadvantage, Plb. 5.46.5 ; pl., Id. 1.53.13 ; χρείας καὶ δ. Str. 2.5.17 ; opp. πλεονέκτημα, Corn. ND 18, cf. Plu. 2.600a. (< χράω) difficulty in obtaining loans, ΄tightness’ of money, Cic. Att. 16.7.6.

ον, (< χράομαι) hard to use, inconvenient, opp. εὔχρηστος, Hp. Aph. 2.54, cf. Sch. Il. Oxy. 221 vii 14 ; ἱππικὸν στράτευμα ἐν νυκτὶ… δ. X. Cyr. 3.3.26 ; intractable, κύνες Id. Cyn. 3.11 ; of troops, Plb. 4.11.8 (Sup.) ; δ. ἐξουσία hard to use well, Isoc. 8.103 ; δύσχρηστα inconveniences, Cic. Att. 7.5.3, cf. DS. 4.8. Adv. -τως, διακεῖσθαι to be in difficulties, unmanageable, of ships, Plb. 1.61.4 ; of troops, ἀπαλλάττειν Id. 4.64.7 ; δ. ἔχειν Plu. Aem. 19 ; — synon. for οὐ χρησίμως, Str. 17.2.4.
ἡ, bad colour, Dsc. Ther. 6, Gal. 17 (2).215, Asp. in EN 44.6.
ον, contr. δύσχρους, ουν, = δύσχρως, Hp. Aph. 5.42.
ουν, contr. for δύσχροος.
ωτος, ὁ, ἡ, of a bad colour, discoloured, Hp. Coac. 136.
ον, with bad juices, ill-savoured, Xenocr. 12.
ἡ, an ill taste, Thphr. CP 6.12.12.
ον, ill-savoured, Arist. GA 776a30, Thphr. CP 6.12.4.

ον, hard to traverse ; inextricable, ἀκρισία Plb. 23.1.13 (s.v.l.).
difficult to digest, τροφή Aët. 9.30.

ἡ, rough ground, X. Cyr. 1.6.35 ; τῶν Ἰταλῶν Jul. Or. 1.38c ; in pl., X. Cyr. 1.4.7, Isoc. 6.80, Onos. 11.3, Gal. UP 3.1, etc.
want of room, Ph. 2.563, Ath. 4.129c.
difficulty, Alex.Aphr. Fat. 200.23.
ον, hard to separate, Gal. 2.700 (Comp.) ; hard to distinguish, ἡ κολακεία τῆς φιλίας δ. Plu. 2.51a.
δυσχωρῇ, διακωλύεται, Hsch.
ον, not easily affected by cold, Gal. 1.346.
to be ill-smelling, Ph. 2.563.
ες, (< ὄζω) ill-smelling, stinking, foul, χωλός, δ. S. Ph. 1032 ; δ. πῦον Hp. Prog. 7 ; καρπός Hdt. 2.94 ; πνεῦμα Th. 2.49 ; ὀσμαί Arist. HA 626a27 ; Comp., κόπρος Plu. Fr. inc. 149.
ἡ, foul smell, Arist. Pol. 1311b34, HA 626b20, Ph. 2.96, Plu. 2.90b, Phld. Herc. 19.27, etc.
ον, causing grievous pangs, AP 6.272 (Pers.).
ον, hard to kill, tenacious of life, Thphr. HP 3.12.5.
ον, hardly, i.e. reluctantly, swearing, Poll. 1.39.
impf. ἐδυσώνουν AP 11.169 (Nicarch.) : — beat down the price, cheapen, Pl.Com. 224 ; — Med., Arist. Fr. 558.
ου, ὁ, one who beats down the price, hard bargainer, Lync. ap. Ath. 6.228c ; οὐδεὶς δ. χρηστὸν ὀψωνεῖ κρέας Com.Adesp. 277.
ον, hard to buy, Hdn. Epim. 213.
have a bad name, Hdn. Epim. 203.

ον, bearing an ill name, hateful, υἷες Ἀχαιῶν Il. 6.255 ; ἠώς Od. 19.571 ; μοῖρα Il. 12.116 ; λέκτρα S. OC 528 (lyr.) ; φθόνος E. Fr. 403 ; κήρ ARh. 2.258 ; esp. bearing a name of ill omen, such as Αἴας, S. Aj. 914 (lyr.) ; Comp., Ph. 1.680 ; — in S. Fr. 88.9 (lyr.) perh. δ. γλώσσῃ whose tongue earned him an ill name (of Thersites).

aor. ἐδυσώπησα Luc. Asin. 38 ; (< ὄψ) : — put out of countenance, abash, τινά Ph. 1.291, Plu. 2.418e, Luc. l.c., S.E. P. 3.66, etc. ; οὐδὲν αὐτὴν ἐδυσώπει X.Eph. 4.5 ; c. acc. inf., shame a person with doing a thing, J. BJ 1.6.5, al. ; esp. of importunate persons, δ. τινὰ δεήσει ib. 3.8.6 ; so, entreat, ἥκειν ὑμᾶς καὶ παρακαλῶ καὶ δ. Hld. 10.2 ; abs., to be importunate, αἰσχυνόμενοι ἀντιλέγειν τοῖς ἀγνωμόνως δυσωποῦσιν ὕστερον δυσωποῦνται τοὺς δικαίως ἐγκαλοῦντας Plu. 2.532d ; — Pass., θεὸν εἶναι τὴν ἠχὼ δυσωποῦμαι I am constrained to believe that, Jul. Ep. 189, cf. Marcellin. Puls. 23 ; to be susceptible to importunity, τὴν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀναισχύντως λιπαρούντων ἧτταν, ἣν ἔνιοι δυσωπεῖσθαι καλοῦσιν Plu. Brut. 6 ; δυσωπεῖν τὴν ὄψιν to disgust, Id. Lyc. 9 ; alarm, πάθος δ. τινά Procop. Arc. 2. in early writers only Pass., impf. ἐδυσωπούμην Pl. Phdr. 242c : — to be put out of countenance, abs., Id. Plt. 285b, etc. ; πρὸς ἀλλήλους Id. Lg. 933a ; δ. μή… Id. Phdr. l.c. ; τινί Plb. 20.12.6 ; ἐπί τινι Ph. 1.639 ; εἰ… Id. 2.423 ; περί τινος Phld. Rh. 1.297 S. ; of animals, to be shy, timid, X. Mem. 2.1.4. c. acc., to be put to shame by, τὴν ἀρετήν τινος Plu. Cor. 15 ; τὴν χάριν Lib. Decl. 37.19 ; but more freq.
fight shy of, ὄνομα DH. Comp. 12 (so in Act., look askance at, δ. καὶ ὑποπτεύω μήποτ’ οὐ Λυσίου ὁ λόγος Id. Lys. 11), cf. Phryn. 166 ; ὑφορᾶν καὶ δ. Them. Or. 26.330b ; διὰ τοὔνομα τὴν μοναρχίαν Plu. Sol. 14 ; regard with aversion, ὄψα Ael. Fr. 182 ; disapprove of, Phld. Hom. p. 55 O. ; c. inf., to be ashamed to do,… εἰπεῖν D.Chr. 32.7, cf. 36.54 ; also τὴν ἀντίδοσιν δ. feel ashamed to reply, Jul. Ep. 184.
intr. in Act., to see with difficulty, Luc. Lex. 4.
ατος, τό, a means of making one ashamed, and so, a corrective, τῶν ἡμαρτημένων J. BJ 1.25.5, cf. D.Chr. Fr. 8.
one must be shy of using, τὴν ταυτολογίαν Eust. 173.12.
ή, όν, importunate, Eust. 105.15 (Comp.), etc. Adv. -κῶς Sch. Ar. Pl. 21 (v.l. -ωπικῶς).

ἡ, confusion of face, shamefacedness, Phld. Lib. p. 24 O., Ph. 2.603 (pl.), Plu. 2.95b ; false modesty, ib. 528e, al. ; cause for shame, ib. 707e, Cic. Att. 13.33.2 ; δυσωπίαν habere, to have an ugly look, ib. 16.15.2 ; τὰς δ. (v.l. δυστροπίας) τὰς ἐν τοῖς διαπορηθεῖσι dub. in Ph. 1.330.
(< ὤρα) keep painful watch, ὡς δὲ κύνες περὶ μῆλα δυσωρήσονται ἐν αὐλῇ Il. 10.183 ; but Apollon.Soph. Lex. read δυσωρήσωσιν, cf. Hsch., EM 292.49.
ον, (ὥρα) unseasonable, Poll. 5.109.
δυσχεραίνειν, Hsch.

insepar. Prefix, opp. εὖ, un-, mis-, with notion of hard, bad, unlucky, etc., as δυσήλιος, δύσαγνος ; destroying the good sense of a word, or increasing its bad sense ; hence, joined even to words expressing negation, as δυσάμμορος, δυσανάσχετος ; poet. in strong contrasts, as Πάρις Δύσπαρις, γάμος δύσγαμος. Before στ, σθ, σπ, σφ, σχ, the final ς was omitted, v. δυστ-.
(Cf. Skt. duṣ-, dur-, e.g. durmanās, = δυσμενής ; ONorse tor-, e.g. torsóttligr (< δύσμαχος) ; OIr. du-, do-, e.g. dochruth ΄misshapen΄.)
Dor. δύτα, ἡ, shrine (?), IG 4.823.42 (Troezen), 7.2477 (Cabireum).
ου, ὁ, (< δύω) diver, Hdt. 8.8 ; δ. βύθιος Poll. 1.97.

ή, όν, able to dive, ζῷον Arist. Fr. 496 ; ἡ δυτική (sc. τέχνη) Poll. 7.139. (< δύσις) later form for δυσμικός, setting, Euc. Phaen. p. 10 M.
western, στοά J. AJ 20.8.11 ; opp. ἀνατολικός, Ptol. Alm. 2.11 ; Comp. -ώτερος fartherwest, ib. 2.13 ; δ. ὠκεανός Nonn. D. 12.1 ; δυτικόν, τό, closing at sunset, = κλύμενον, Ps.-Dsc. 4.13 ; = φοῖνιξ, ib. 43.
ὁ, unknown water-bird, Dionys. Av. 2.13, 3.24.

(v. infr.), δύνω ; causal Tenses, cause to sink, sink, plunge in ; pres. only in Thphr. HP 5.44.8 οὐκ ἐν ἴσῳ βάθει πάντα δύοντες τῆς θαλάσσης ; aor.1 ἔδυσα (ἐξ-) Od. 14.341 ; cf. the compds. ἀπο, ἐκ-, ἐν-, κατα-δύω. non-causal, get or go into, c. acc. ; pres. δύω (v. 1.4) ; more freq. δύνω Il. 17.202, Hes. Op. 616, S. Ph. 1331, etc. ; Ep. impf. δῦνον Il. 11.268 ; aor. ἔδυνα Batr. 245, part. δύνας Plb. 9.15.9, Paus. 2.11.7, Ael. VH 4.1, but ἔδυσα Ev. Marc. 1.32, etc. ; more freq.
Med. δύομαι Il. 5.140, E. Rh. 529 (lyr.), etc. (also in Att. Inscrr., as IG2². 1241) ; impf. ἐδυόμην Pl. Plt. 269a ; Ep. δύοντο Il. 15.345 ; fut. δύσομαι [υ] 7.298, E. El. 1271 ; aor. ἐδυσάμην ARh. 4.865, (< ἀπό) Nic. Al. 302 ; Ep. 3 pl. δύσαντο Il. 23.739, opt. δυσαίατο prob. in 18.376 (Prose and Com. in Compds.) ; Hom. mostly uses the Ep. forms ἐδύσεο, ἐδύσετο, imper. δύσεο 19.36, Hes. Sc. 108, part. δυσόμενος (in pres. sense) Od. 1.24, Hes. Op. 384 ; more freq. aor. ἔδυν (as if from Δῦμι) Il. 11.63, etc. ; 3 dual ἐδύτην [υ] 10.254 ; 1 pl. ἔδυμεν S. Fr. 367 ; ἔδυτε Od. 24.106 ; ἔδυσαν, Ep. ἔδυν Il. 11.263 ; Ion. 3 sg. δύσκεν 8.271 ; imper. δῦθι, δῦτε, 16.64, 18.140 ; subj. δύω [υ] 6.340, 22.99, but δύῃ [υ] Hes. Op. 728 ; Ep. opt. δύη [υ] (for δυίη) Od. 18.348 ; inf. δῦναι Il. 10.221, Att., Ep. δύμεναι [υ] 14.63, ἐκδῦμεν 16.99 ; part. δύς, δῦσα, Hdt. 8.8 ; pf. δέδυκα Il. 5.811, Sappho 52, Pl. Phd. 116e ; Dor. inf. δεδυκεῖν [υ] Theoc. 1.102 ; — Pass., fut. and aor. δυθήσομαι, ἐδύθην [υ], and a pf. δέδυμαι only in compds., v. ἀπο, ἐκ-, ἐν-δύω. [υ in δύω in pres. and impf. Act. and Med., Hom. ; but ARh. has δῡομαι, δῡετο 1.581, part. δῡόμενος ib. 925, Call. Epigr. 22 ; δύεται Nonn. D. 7.286 ; ἐκδέδυκας AP 5.72 (Rufin.).]
of Places or Countries, enter, make one΄s way into, in Hom. the most freq. use, εἰ… κε πύλας καὶ τείχεα δύω (aor.2) Il. 22.99 ; πόλιν δύσεσθαι Od. 7.18 ; ἔδυ νέφεα plunged into the clouds, of a star, Il. 11.63 ; δῦτε θαλάσσης εὐρέα κόλπον plunge into the lap of Ocean, 18.140 ; γαῖαν ἐδύτην went beneath the earth, i.e. died, 6.19, cf. 411, etc. ; πόλεμον δύμεναι plunge into…, 14.63 ; θεῖον δύσονται ἀγῶνα 7.298 ; ἐδύσετο οὐλαμὸν ἀνδρῶν 20.379 ; δύσεο δὲ μνηστῆρας go in to them, Od. 17.276 ; rarely in Trag., αἰθέρα δ. S. Aj. 1192 (lyr.), cf. E. El. 1271. in Ep. less freq. with Preps., ἔδυν δόμον Ἄϊδος εἴσω Il. 11.263 ; δύσομαι εἰς Ἀΐδαο Od. 12.383 ; ἐς πόντον ἐδύσετο 5.352 ; δέρτρον ἔσω δύνοντες 11.579 ; δύσεθ’ ἁλὸς κατὰ κῦμα Il. 6.136 ; ὑπὸ κῦμα θαλάσσης αὐτίκ’ ἔδυσαν 18.145 ; κατὰ σταθμοὺς δύεται slinks into the fold, 5.140 ; καθ’ ὅμιλον ἔδυ Τρώων 3.36 (rarely c. gen., κατὰ σπείους κοίλοιο δέδυκεν Od. 12.93) ; πάϊς ὡς ὑπὸ μητέρα δύσκεν εἰς Αἴαντα he got himself unto Ajax, i.e. got behind his shield, Il. 8.271 ; βέλος δ’ εἰς ἐγκέφαλον δῦ ib. 85 ; ἀκίδες δεδυκυῖαι διὰ φλεβῶν Plu. Crass. 25 ; in Prose and Trag. mostly with a Prep. (but δυόμενοι abs., diving, Th. 7.25), δῦναι ἐς θάλασσαν Hdt. 8.8 ; ἐς ἄντρον A. Fr. 261 ; ἁρμὸν… πρὸς αὐτὸ στόμιον S. Ant. 1217 ; κατὰ βάθος Pl. Lg. 905a ; κατὰ τῆς γῆς Id. Phd. 113c, etc. abs., εἴσω ἔδυ ξίφος the sword entered his body, Il. 16.340 ; δύνει ἀλοιφή sinks in (where however βοείην may be supplied), 17.392 ; — Med., δύου πάλιν Ar. V. 148. of Sun and Stars, sink into [the sea], set, ἠέλιος μὲν ἔδυ Il. 18.241, cf. Od. 3.329, etc. ; ἔδυ φάος ἠελίοιο 13.35 ; δύσετό τ’ ἠέλιος 2.388, cf. Il. 7.465, etc. ; ἀελίω δύντος Sappho Supp. 25.8 ; so Βοώτης ὀψὲ δύων late-setting Boötes, Od. 5.272 ; δείελος ὀψὲ δύων Il. 21.232 ; [σελαναία] δύεν Bion Fr. 8.6 ; πρὸ δύντος ἡλίου Hdt. 7.149 ; πρὸ ἡλίου δύντος D. 15.22 ; δυσόμενος Ὑπερίων (to mark the West) Od. 1.24 ; ἐδύετο εἰς τόπον [ὁ ἥλιος] Pl. Plt. 269a ; πρὸς δύνοντος ἡλίου towards the West, A. Supp. 255 ; metaph, βίου δύντος αὐγαί Id. Ag. 1123 (lyr.) ; ἔδυ πρόπας δόμος ib. 1011 (lyr.) ; δεδυκὸς ζῆν live in retirement, Pl. Lg. 781c. of clothes and armour, get into, Ἀρήϊα τεύχεα δ. Il. 6.340, etc. ; κυνέην δ. put on one΄s helmet, 5.845 ; δῦ δὲ χιτῶν’ 18.416 ; metaph, εἰ μὴ σύ γε δύσεαι ἀλκήν if thou wilt not put on strength, 9.231 ; so ἀνάγκας ἔδυ λέπαδνον A. Ag. 218 (lyr.) ; hence, trans., put on, ἀμφ’ ὤμοισιν ἐδύσετο τεύχεα Il. 3.328, etc. ; ὤμοιϊν… τεύχεα δῦθι 16.64 ; χιτῶνα περὶ χροΐ… δῦνεν Od. 15.61 ; χρυσὸν… ἔδυνε περὶ χροΐ Il. 8.43. rarely abs. with a Prep., ὅπλοισιν ἔνι δεινοῖσιν ἐδύτην 10.272, cf. ARh. 1.638 ; ἐς τεύχεα δύντε Od. 22.201. of sufferings, passions, and the like, enter, come over or upon, κάματος… γυῖα δέδυκεν Il. 5.811 ; ὄφρ’ ἔτι μᾶλλον δύη ἄχος κραδίην Od. 18.348 ; ἦτορ δῦν’ ἄχος Il. 19.367 ; ὀδύναι δῦνον μένος 11.272 ; κρατερὴ δέ ἑλύσσα δέδυκε madness is come over him, 9.239 ; δῦ μιν Ἄρης Ares, i.e. the spirit of war, filled him, 17.210 ; μιν ἔδυ χόλος 19.16.
v. δύο.
α, ον, weighing two obols Gal. 13.92, al.
Ion., Ep., Lyr. ; Att. δώδεκα, twelve, in all genders, Il. 2.637, Hdt. 1.16, Pi. N. 4.28, etc. ; οἱ δώδεκα θεοί Aeschin. Socr. 5, Com.Adesp. 39.9 D. ; — also δυόδεκο, IG 5(2).3 (Tegea, iv BC).
ον, worth twelve oxen, Il. 23.703.
ή, όν, belonging to the δυωδεκάς 1, Dam. Pr. 276.
ον, running the course twelve times, τέθριππα Pi. O. 2.50.
= δωδεκάεθλος.

ίδος, Att. ; Ion. δωδεκηΐς, ίδος, and δωδεκῄς, -ῇδος, ἡ, sacrifice of twelve victims, SIG 2438 D 37 (Delph.), SIG 3604.9 (Delph., ii BC), Porph. Abst. 1.22, etc. ; as Adj., θυσίαι Eust. 1386.48 ; hence name of a sacred mission to Delphi, SIG 773.2 (i BC).
v. δωδεκάμηνος.
ον, divided into twelve parts, AP 7.641 (Antiphil.).
υ, of twelve cubits, εὖρος Oppian. H. 2.143.
ουν, twelvefold, IG 14.644 (Brutt.).
ιος, formed of twelve united states, Ἴωνες Hdt. 7.95.

άδος, ἡ, the number twelve, Procl. in Euc. p. 174 F. ; group of twelve divinities, Dam. Pr. 348.
twelfth part, of the signs of the zodiac, Arat. 555 (pl.), 703 ; of an hour, AP 9.779, 782 (Paul. Sil.).
v. δωδεκαταῖος.
ές, having twelve walled cities, λαός Tim. Pers. 247.
(sc. μήν), έος, ὁ, twelfth month, IG 14.425 iv, 427 ii (Tauromenium).
v. δωδέκατος.
= δωδεκέτης, Leg. Gort. 12.34.
ον, holding twenty-two measures, τρίπους Il. 23.264.
υ, twenty-two cubits long, Il.15.678.
v. δίδωμι.
δικαίως, ὁσίως, Hsch.
v. δυώδεκα.
ου, ὁ, twelve times victorious in the Actian games, BGU 1074.23 (iii AD).
ον, of twelve oxen, θυσία IGRom. 4.555 (Ancyra).
ον, with twelve altars, ναός Lyd. Mens. 4.2.
ον, bent twelve times, τέρμα the post (in the race-course) that has been doubled twelve times, Pi. O. 3.33.
τό, dodecagon, Plu. 2.363a.
ον, twelve fingers long or broad, Apollod. Poliorc. 178.3 ; of twelve digits, of the apparent diameter of sun and moon, Cleom. 2.3 ; δ. ἔκφυσις the duodenum, Herophil. ap. Gal. 2.572, Ruf. Anat. 42.
ὁ, leader of twelve, X. Cyr. 3.3.11 ; codd. have -δεκάρχας, δεκαδάρχας in ib. 2.4.4.

ον, sold at twelve drachmae, οἶνος D. 42.20.
privileged to pay as poll-tax only twelve dr., POxy. 258.8 (i AD), al.
ον, twelve palms long, κέρα AP 6.96 (Eryc.).
ον, (< ἕδρα) with twelve surfaces ; δωδεκάεδρον, τό, dodecahedron, Euc. 11 Def. 28, 13.17, Arist. Cael. 307a16.
ον, conqueror in twelve contests, Sammelb. 2134.4, APl. 4.99 (also δυωδεκάεθλος Nonn. D. 35.335).
ίδος, ἡ, cycle of twelve years, τοῦ Διός Gp. 1.12 tit. ; pl., title of Orphic work, Suid.

ές, or δωδεκαέτης, ες, (< ἔτος) lasting twelve years, χρόνος J. AJ 15.9.6.
twelve years old, Plu. Comp. Lyc. Num. 4, 2.198c.

ἡ, space of twelve years, Ptol. Tetr. 206 ; ὑπὲρ τῆς δ., title of a speech of Demades.
age of twelve years, BGU 592i3 (ii AD).
ον, having twelve signs, οὐρανός Lyd. Mens. 4.67.
ον, of twelve days, Eust. 128.13.

ον, of twelve Gods, cena, Suet. Aug. 70. Subst. δωδεκάθεον, τό, temple of the twelve Gods, Inscr.Cos 43.
medicine compounded of twelve ingredients, Paul.Aeg. 7.11.
primrose, Primula acaulis, Plin. HN 25.28.
Adv. twelve times, Ar. Pl. 852, Arist. Fr. 347, DC. 60.7, etc.
ον, holdingtwelve κλῖναι, Anaxandr. 41.11.
ον, with twelve springs, Cratin. 186, Philostr. VS 1.22.4.
ον, dub.sens., Sammelb. 1958.
ον, of twelve clauses, Sch. Ar. Eq. 821.
ον, of twelve threads, X. Cyn. 2.5.
ον, of twelve months, τέλος Pi. N. 11.10 (but δυω- codd.) ; -μηνον, τό, year, Thd. Da. 4.26, POxy. 506.15 (ii AD) ; — poet. δυωδεκάμ-, twelve months old, Hes. Op. 752.
ον, (< μηχανή) knowing twelve arts or tricks, ἄστρον E. Fr. 755 (lyr.) ; of a courtesan, Ar. Ra. 1327 (et Sch.), cf. Pl.Com. 134.
δωδεκαμν<α>ιαῖος, α, ον, weighing twelve minae, Hsch. s.v. πέλεκυς.
ον, of twelve forms, Olymp. in Phd. p. 199 N.
ον, of twelve labours, epith. of Heracles, Lyd. Mens. 4.67.
ον, of twelve fathoms, Hero Geom. 4.12.
παιδος, ὁ, ἡ, with twelve children, λοχείη APl. 4.132 (Theodorid.).
Adv. twelve times πάλαι, ever so long ago, Ar. Eq. 1154 ; cf. δεκάπαλαι, μυριόπαλαι.
υ, twelve cubits high, κολοσσοί Hdt. 2.153 (δυω-); σιρός Anaxandr. 41.28, cf. BCH 35.243 (Delos, ii BC), Philostr. VA 4.16.
multiply by twelve, Heph.Astr. 2.2.
ὁ, multiplication by twelve, Cat.Cod.Astr. 4.44.
ον, twelvefold, Plu. 2.1028c ; also δωδεκαπλασίων, ον, gen. ονος, Orib. Fr. 102.
ον, gen. ονος, = δωδεκαπλάσιος.
τό, twelve-sided figure, v.l. in Gal. Anim. Pass. 2.3.
ουν, = δωδεκαπλάσιος, Papp. 609.
ὁ, ἡ, πουν, τό, gen. ποδος, twelve feet long, Men. 364, Gal. 10.33.
ου, ὁ, v. δωδεκάδαρχος ; — also δωδέκαρχος, Hsch. s.v. δεκαδάρχαι.
= δωδεκάρχης.
άδος, ἡ, group of twelve, Pl. Lg. 756b. = δυωδεκαΐς, Hsch. (pl.).
ον, having twelve moons, ἐνιαυτός Sch. E. Tr. 1075.
ον, of twelve times, in music, Aristid.Quint. 1.14, Sch. Ar. Nu. 456 cod. Ven.
ον, twelve-oared, Plu. Caes. 38.
ον, of twelve strips of leather, σφαῖρα Pl. Phd. 110b, Plu. 2.1003d.
ον, twelve stades long, etc., Posidon. 18 J., Str. 13.1.36.
ον, (< ἵστημι) weighing twelve times as much, Pl. Hipparch. 231d.
ον, with twelve stories, πύργος Ps.-Callisth. 2.18.
(sc. οἶκος), ὁ, colonnade of twelve columns, Milet. 7.59 (Didyma).
ον, of twelve syllables, Ἀλκαϊκὸν δ. (sc. μέτρον) Heph. 10.3, 14.4.
ἡ, name of a district in Egypt, OGI 210.5, 670.5, Ptol. Geog. 4.5.74.

α, ον, on the twelfth day, in twelve days, δ. ἀνεβίω Pl. R. 614b, cf. Thphr. HP 7.1.3 ; δυωδεκαταῖος ἀφ’ ὧτέ νιν οὐδὲ ποτεῖδον Theoc. 2.157.
twelve days old, Hes. Op. 751 (in poet. form δυωδεκαταῖος), Arist. HA 567a5.
τό, twelfth part, [χώρας] Pl. Lg. 848c, cf. IG 12(7).237.56 (Amorgos, ii/i BC), Ph. 1.673 ; sign of the zodiac, Hipparch. 2.1.7, Ptol. Tetr. 93, etc.
ον, = δυωδεκάμοιρος, Man. 4.167 ; — also δωδεκατήμορος, ον, PHib. 1.27.122 (iv/iii BC).
= δωδεκατημόριος.
η, ον, twelfth, Il. 24.781, etc. ; δ. τόκοι, 8⅓ %, SIG 364.74 (Ephesus, iii BC), etc. ; — Ep. δυωδ-, Il. 1.493, etc. δωδεκάτη, ἡ, = Χόες, Hsch.
ἡ, fixed circle of twelve divisions through which the zodiac is supposed to revolve, Vett.Val. 179.33, Cat.Cod.Astr. 5 (3).89, al.
ον, bearing twelve times a year, Luc. VH 2.13.

ον, with twelve petals, ῥόδα δ. Thphr. HP 6.6.4.
with twelve leaves, κλάδος PMagBerol. 2.67.
ον, of twelve tribes, τὸ δ. the twelve tribes of Israel, Act. Ap. 26.7.
ον, with twelve strings, ὄργανον EM 813.43.
χουν, holding twelve χόες, PRev. Laws 40.11 (iii BC), al.
Adv. in twelve ways, An.Ox. 2.3. (Theognost.).
ον, of twelve hours, Secund. Sent. 4, S.E. M. 10.182. δωδεκάωρος, ἡ, circle of twelve animal figures typifying the double hours of the Chaldaean νυχθήμερον, Teucer in Cat.Cod.Astr. 7.195, al.
ὁ, = Dodecember, month invented by Licinus, DC. 54.21.

ου, or δωδεκετής, οῦ, ὁ, twelve years old, Call. Epigr. 21 (δωδεκένη Meineke), Plu. Aem. 35 ; — in form δωδεχέτης, IG 4.51 (Aegina), Annuario 4/5.467 (Halic., iv BC) ; — fem. δωδεκέτις, ιδος, AP 11.70 (Leon.).
έως, ὁ, = χοεύς which held twelve cotylae, Hsch.
ΐδος, ἡ, Ion. for δυωδεκαΐς.
ἡ, period of twelve days, IG1². 374.89.
ους, ἡ, a ship with twelve banks of oars, Callix. 1.
-ῇδος, ἡ, Ion. for δυωδεκαΐς.
ον, with twelve knobs, πόπανον IG2². 1367.
= δωδεκέτης.
v. Δωδώνη.

ἡ, Dodona, in Epirus, the seat of the most ancient oracle of Zeus, Il. 16.234, Od. 14.327, Hes. Fr. 134, 212, A. Pr. 830, etc. ; heterocl. forms Δωδῶνος, ῶνι (as if from Δωδών), S. Fr. 460, Tr. 172 ; Δωδώναθεν Pi. N. 4.53 ; Δωδώνηθε Call. Del. 284 ; a nom. Δωδώ, Simm. ap. Str. 8.5.3. ; — Adj. Δωδωναῖος, α, ον, Il. 16.233, A. Supp. 258, Cratin. 5. ; prov., Δωδωναῖον χαλκεῖον chatterbox, Eust. 335.45 ; — fem. Δωδωνίς, ίδος, S. Fr. 456, Hdt. 2.53, Pherecyd. 90 J.
ίδος, v. Δωδώνη.
ὁμοία, Hsch.
ὦτα (Cret.), Hsch.
ὑπόβλητος, Hsch. ; cf. δωλοδομεῖς.
οἰκογενεῖς, Hsch. (cf. δοῦλος and ἐβάθη· ἐγεννήθη, Id. ; Lith. gim͂ti ΄to be born΄).
Dor., = δοῦλος, Leg. Gort. 1.1, al. ; voc. δῶλε Theoc. 5.5.

ατος, τό, (< δέμω) house, πατρώϊον ἵκετο δ. Il. 21.44, etc. ; mainly poet., but once in Hdt., 2.62 (pl.), and in late Prose (v. infr.), but never in Att. Prose ; also, chief room, hall, θάλαμον καὶ δ. καὶ αὐλήν Il. 6.316, cf. Od. 17.329, al. ; hence, pl. for a single house, 2.259, freq. in Trag., A. Ag. 607, S. Tr. 332, E. Or. 301, etc. of the gods, ἀθάνατοι Ὀλύμπια δώματ’ ἔχοντες Il. 2.13, etc. ; κλυτὰ δ. βένθεσι λίμνης, of Poseidon, 13.21 ; freq. of Pluto, δῶμ’ Ἀΐδαο the nether world, Od. 12.21 ; ὦ δῶμ’ Ἀΐδου καὶ Περσεφόνης S. El. 110 ; Πλούτωνος δ. E. HF 808 (lyr.) ; of a temple, Pi. P. 4.53, A. Eu. 242, etc. ; pl., Hdt. 2.62, S. OT 71. δῶμα Καδμεῖον, i.e. Thebes, ib. 29.
housetop, LXX De. 22.8, Ev. Matt. 24.17, Babr. 5.5, POxy. 475.22 (ii AD), etc.
household, family, A. Ag. 1468 (lyr.), S. OT 1226, etc. ; cf. δῶ.
Aeol. for Δημήτηρ.

τό, Dim. of δῶμα, Ar. Ra. 100, IG 12(8).442.8 (Thasos), Jul. ad Them. 263a.
chamber, bedchamber, Ar. Lys. 160, Lys. 1.17, 24, Pl. R. 390c, and so prob. in X.Eph. 2.1, Procop. Arc. 23.
housetop (cf. δῶμα Ι. 4), J. BJ 2.21.5, Hdn. 1.12.8.
ου, ὁ, of, belonging to the house, Ποσειδῶν Paus. 3.14.7, IG 5(1).497, al. (Sparta) ; Ἀπόλλων Sch. Pi. N. 5.81 ; fem., δωματῖτις ἑστία A. Ag. 968.
Pass., have a house built for one, to be housed, δεδωμάτωμαι οὐ σμικρᾷ χερί Α. Supp. 958.
ἡ, structure, ἐνηλλάγη ἡ δ. πᾶσα τῆς βασιλικῆς IEJ 11.184 (Sepphoris, vi AD).
ruin the house, cj. for σωματοφθορέω, A. Ag. 948.

build, ARh. 2.531, IG 14.1868, AP 7.142 ; — more freq. in Med., ib. 11.400 (Luc.), Coluth. 287, Orph. A. 570 ; metaph, build up, restore to life, τινά Lyc. 48 ; — Pass., δ. ἐκ λίθων Antyll. ap. Orib. 9.13.6 ; of a statue, to be set up, App.Anth. 2.534 (Halic.).
ατος, τό, chamber, δω[μ]ήματι τύμβου Benndorf-Niemann Reisen in Lykien p. 80 No.59 (Sidyma).
εως, ἡ, building, Hsch.
ύος, ἡ, building, Hsch.
ορος, ὁ, builder, Man. 6.415.
Dor. for ζωμός, Epil. 3 (prob. l.), EM 316.56.
δώνακι, v. δόναξ.
v. ζωός.
(sc. μῆλον), τό, = Lat. duracinum, a kind of peach, clingstone, Gp. 3.1.4, 10.13.1.
σπλήν (Maced.), Hsch.

Ion. δωρεή, ἡ ; δωρειά in earlier Attic Inscrr., IG1². 77, al., δωρεά first in ib. 22.1.68 : — gift, present, esp. bounty (= δόσις ἀναπόδοτος Arist. Top. 125a18), Hdt. 2.140 ; δωρεὰν διδόναι Id. 6.130, A. Pr. 340 ; πορεῖν ib. 616 ; δωρεῖσθαι Pl. Plt. 290c ; δ. δέχεσθαι, λαμβάνειν, Isoc. 6.31, 15.40 ; ironically, θάνατόν τινι δωρεὰν ἀποδοῦναι Antipho 5.34 ; δ. ἔχειν S. Aj. 1032, D. 18.312 ; ἐν χάριτος μέρει καὶ δωρειᾶς D. 21.165 ; δωρειὰν καὶ χάριν ib. 172, cf. Pl. Lg. 844d ; of a legacy, D. 27.41, 65 ; δωρεαί privileges and immunities, opp. δῶρα, gifts in cash or kind, Philostr. VS 2.10.4.
estate granted by a king, fief, Phoenicid. 4.7, PSI 5.511.4, 518.2 (iii BC). acc. δωρεάν as Adv., as a free gift, freely, Hdt. 5.23, prob. in And. 1.4 ; μηδὲν δ. πράττειν Plb. 18.34.7, cf. LXX Jb. 1.9 ; δ. λειτουργεῖν Test.Epict. 4.27, cf. Inscr.Prien. 4.17 (iv BC) ; so κατὰ δωρεάν IG 7.2711.13, al. (Acraeph., i AD) ; ἐν δωρεᾷ προσνεῖμαι Plb. 22.5.4 ; but γῆν (ἀμπελῶνα, etc.) ἐν δωρεᾷ ἔχειν to hold land by a royal grant, PRev. Laws 36.15 (iii BC), cf. 43.11, 44.3.
to no purpose, for naught, Ep. Gal. 2.21.
α, ον, held by royal grant, γῆ Sammelb. 1178a, 1178b, cf. 3937, 3938 (iii BC) ; v. δωρεά ΙΙ.
ή, όν, concerning grants, γράμμα PMasp. 13.26 (vi AD).
ή, όν, = δωρεαστικός, ὁμολογία Sammelb. 4678.13 (vi AD).

fut. -ήσω Hom. Fr. 17 ; aor. ἐδώρησα Hes. Op. 82, Pi. O. 6.78 : — give, present, δῶρον Hes. l.c. ; present one with, θυσίαις Ἑρμᾶν Pi. l.c. ; — Pass., aor. δωρηθῆναι to be given or presented, Hdt. 1.87, Isoc. 4.26 ; in pf. Pass., παρὰ θεῶν δῶρα ὑμῖν δεδώρηται Pl. Plt. 274c ; and of persons, to be presented with a thing, χώρῃ Hdt. 8.85, cf. S. Aj. 1029. more freq.
Med. δωρέομαι, ῥεῖα θεὸς… ἵππους δωρήσαιτ’ Il. 10.557 ; δωρέεσθαί τί τινι present a thing to one, Hdt. 2.126, 5.37, A. Pr. 253, X. An. 7.3.20, etc. ; σπέρμα εἰς Πελοπόννησον δωρήσασθε Id. HG 6.3.6 ; also δ. τινά τινι present one with a thing, Hdt. 1.54, 3.130, A. Pr. 778 ; δ. τινά to make him presents, Hdt. 1.55 ; pf., δεδώρηται Pl. Ti. 46e, Lg. 672b, X. Cyr. [5.2.8]. in pres. and impf. also, offer, E. Supp. 875.

ατος, τό, gift, present, Hdt. 7.38, etc. ; c. dat. pers., A. Pers. 523, Eu. 402, S. Tr. 668 ; pl., E. Or. 123, etc. — Rare in Prose, X. Hier. 8.4, Arist. EN 1099b11, and later, Ph. 2.9, Ep. Jac. 1.17.
ή, όν, = δωρητικός, DH. 8.60, Vett.Val. 41.3.
ῆρος, ὁ, giver, AP 6.305 (Leon.).
οῦ, ὁ, benefactor, IG 12(2).645b64 (Nesus, iv BC).

ή, όν, concerned with giving, Pl. Sph. 223c.
munificent, Ph. 1.254.
όν, of persons, open to gifts or presents, Il. 9.526. of things, freely given, δ., οὐκ αἰτητόν S. OT 384, cf. Plu. Cor. 16.
dress like a Dorian girl, i.e. in a single garment open at the side, Anacr. 59. = Δωρίζω, Anacreont. 10.6, Philostr. VS 1.24.2.
ή, όν, poet. for Δωρικός, πόλεμος Orac. ap. Th. 2.54.
to be archon of the Dorians, SIG 668.12 (Delph., ii BC), 770B 2 (Delph., i BC).
τά, festival at Cnidus, GDI 4271 (Cedreae) ; — also Δώρεια, ib. 3660 (Cos).
έως, ὁ, Dorian, descendant of Dorus son of Hellen, IG 12(5).225 (Paros) ; pl., Δωριεῖς, Ion. -ιέες, Att. -ιῆς, οἱ, the Dorians, Od. 19.177, etc. as Adj., = Δωρικός, Pi. P. 8.20.
Dor. Δωρίσδω, imitate the Dorians in life, dialect, etc., speak Doric Greek, Theoc. 15.93, Str. 8.1.2, Plu. 2.421b ; — Pass., to be written in the Doric dialect, δ. τὰ Ἀλκμᾶνος ADysc. Synt. 279.25.
ή, όν, Doric, Hdt. 8.43, Th. 3.95, etc. ; Comp. -ώτερος ADysc. Adv. 159.27. Adv. -κῶς Id. Pron. 48.27, S.E. M. 1.78 ; Comp. -ώτερον ADysc. Synt. 159.16.
α, ον, also ος, ον Pratin. Lyr. 1.17, Arist. Pol. 1276b9 ; — Dorian, Pi. O. 3.5 ; ἁπλοῦν τε καὶ Δ. Plu. Lys. 5, etc. ; esp. of the Dorian mode in music, Arist. Pol. l.c., 1290a22.
= λεοντοπέταλον, Ps.-Dsc. 3.96 (also δωρίς ibid.).

ίδος, ἡ. fem. Adj. Dorian, ἐσθής Hdt. 5.88 ; φωνή Th. 6.5, etc. ; hence, Δ. νᾶσος the Dorian island, of Aegina and Peloponnesus, Pi. N. 3.3, S. OC 696 (lyr.), etc. (with or without γῆ) Doris, in Northern Greece, Hdt. 8.31, Plu. Them. 9, etc. Δ. κόρα a Dorian damsel, E. Hec. 934 (lyr.). (sc. κοπίς) Dorian knife used at sacrifices, Id. El. 819. Δωρίς, = ἔχιον, Dsc. 4.27.
= λεοντοπέταλον, Ps.-Dsc. 3.96 (also δωριπτερίς ibid.).
Dor. for Δωρίζω.
ὁ, speaking in the Doric dialect, Demetr. Eloc. 177.

Adv. in Dorian fashion, Δ. ζῆν Pl. Ep. 336c.
in the Dorian dialect, λαλοῦσι Δ. Call. Iamb. 1.354. ἡ Δ. ἁρμονία the Dorian mode or measure in music, Arist. Pol. 1340b4 ; so Δ. alone, Pl. R. 399a ; in Ar. Eq. 989 (lyr.) with a play on δῶρον.
ἀγών, ὁ, game in which the conqueror received a present, Plu. 2.820d.
ἡ, dub.sens. in Ostr. Strassb. 277.11, al. (ii AD). [To be deleted (Suppl.)]
ον, giving dinner, παῖς δ., i.e. a waiter, Ath. 15.701b.
ου, ὁ, one that takes bribes, LXX Jb. 15.34.

accept as a present, esp. take as a bribe, ἀργύριον πολλόν Hdt. 6.72 ; χρυσόν Pl. R. 590a ; κατὰ πεντήκοντα τάλαντα Ar. V. 669. abs., take bribes, Hdt. 6.82, D. 18.45, etc. ; ἐπί τινι Lys. 21.22, D. 18.49. c. acc. pers. (only in later Gr., for δωροδοκοῦσιν is f.l. in Ar. V. 675 and δωροδοκοῦντας (abs.) is interpol. in D. 9.45), corrupt by bribes, DS. 13.64, Arr. Epict. 4.1.148, Luc. Pisc. 9, etc. simply, bestow gifts, AP 9.335 (Leon.) ; c. acc., ib. 12.204 (Strat.). Pass., of persons, to have a bribe given one, Cratin. 128, cf. Plb. 6.56.2, DH. 4.55 (as v.l.) ; also ταῦθ’ ἁπλῶς δεδωροδόκηται this has been accomplished by bribery, D. 19.329 (v.l. -ηνται); τὰ περὶ τὴν Εὔβοιαν δωροδοκηθέντα the bribery in the matter of Euboea, Aeschin. 3.221 ; τὸ δεδωροδοκημένον χρυσίον Din. 1.66.

ατος, τό, acceptance of a bribe, corruption, D. 18.20, 31.
bribe, καταλαβεῖν Pl.Com. 119.

ἡ, taking of bribes, freq. in Oratt., as And. 4.30 ; δωροδοκίαν καταγνῶναί τινος Lys. 21.21 ; δωροδοκίας κατηγορεῖν Aeschin. 2.3 ; pl., ibid. ; also, giving of bribes, corruption, in pl., DC. 39.55, 50.7.
Adv. in bribefashion, Ar. Eq. 996, with a play on Δωριστί.

ον, taking presents or bribes, corrupt, Pl. R. 390d, D. 18.61 ; Com., δωροδόκοισιν ἐπ’ ἄνθεσιν ἵζων Ar. Eq. 403. Act., bribing, Sch. Pl. Alc. 2.149a, cf. AB 242.
munificent, Aret. SD 2.12.
give presents, Aq. Ez. 16.33.
ου, ὁ, giver of presents, λάθας δ. AP 12.49 (Mel.).
τό, receptacle for offerings, alms-box, Zonar. s.v. κορβωνᾶς.
bribe, LXX Si. 32 (35).12 ; — Pass., ib. 3 Ma. 4.19.
ἡ, bribery, Aq. De. 10.17, Sm. Ps. 25 (26).10.
one who bribes, Gloss.
take presents, Eust. 91.17.
ου, ὁ, greedy of gain, LXX Pr. 15.27.
ἡ, taking of presents, Com.Adesp. 987, DC. 39.55.

τό, (< δίδωμι) gift, present, gift of honour, ἀγλαὰ δ. Il. 1.213, etc. ; votive gift or offering to a god, φέρε δῶρον Ἀθήνῃ 6.293, cf. LXX Ge. 4.4, Ev. Marc. 7.11 ; βωμοὶ δώροισι φλέγονται A. Ag. 91 ; ποῦ μοι τὰ… δ. κἀκροθίνια ; Id. Fr. 184 ; δῶρά τινος the gifts of, i.e. given by, him, θεῶν ἐρικυδέα δ. Il. 20.265, cf. Od. 18.142 ; δῶρ’ Ἀφροδίτης, i.e. personal charms, Il. 3.54, 64 ; δ. Κύπριδος E. Hel. 363 (lyr.) ; δ. τῶν Μουσῶν καὶ Ἀπόλλωνος, of μουσική, Pl. Lg. 796e ; c. gen. rei, ὕπνου δ. the blessing of sleep, Il. 7.482 ; δῶρα presents given as tribute, 17.225 ; δῶρον τοῦ ποταμοῦ, of the land of Egypt, Hdt. 2.5. δῶρα presents, as retaining fees or bribes, D. 18.109, Jusj. ib. 24.150, Arist. Ath. 55.5, SIG 953.7 (Calymna), etc. (the usual sense of the word in Att. Oratt.) ; hence in Att. law, δώρων γραφή an indictment for being bribed, Aeschin. 3.232, etc., cf. Harp. ; δώρων κριθῆναι to be tried for taking bribes, Lys. 27.3 ; δώρων ἑλεῖν τινα to convict him of taking bribes, Ar. Nu. 591 ; δ. ὀφλεῖν to be found guilty of taking bribes, And. 1.74 ; δώρων δίωξις Plu. Per. 32. in pl., good qualities, talents, τὰ βασιλέως δ. Lib. Ep. 19.
front part of palm, Poll. 2.144.
hand΄s breadth, palm, as a measure of length, Nic. Th. 398, Vitr. 2.3.3, Milet. 7.57 (Didyma) ; cf. δεκάδωρος.
γραφή, ἡ, indictment of a ξένος for bribing the judges to declare him an Athenian, Lys. Fr. 196 S., Hyp. Fr. 20, Arist. Ath. 59.3.
bringpresents, Orac. ap. D. 43.66.
ον, devouring gifts, greedy of presents, Hes. Op. 221, 264, Plb. 6.9.7.

bring presents, τινί Pl. Phdr. 266c, cf. Euthphr. 14e, prob. in Epigr. ap. Ath. 5.209e (Archimelos) ; give as presents or bribes, τί τινι Ar. V. 675, cf. DC. 40.53. δ. τινά present him with gifts, Ael. VH 1.32.
ἡ, bringing of presents, v.l. in Ep. Rom. 15.31, Alciphr. 1.6 (pl.), Poll. 4.47.

ή, όν, = δωροφόρος, Pl. Sph. 222d.
given as a present, στολή Ael. VH 1.22.
ον, bringing presents, Pi. P. 5.86, f.l. in Epigr. ap. Ath. 5.209e (Archimelos) ; tributary, Euph. 78.
Dor. for δωρέομαι, Theoc. 7.43.
= σίον, corrupt in Ps.-Dsc. 2.127.
ἡ, = δόσις, only in nom., Hes. Op. 356.
κακὰ διδούσαις, Hsch.
ον, life-giving, Mus. Belg. 16.70.
ἡ, administration of justice, IGRom. 3.563 (Tlos).

ον, referring disputes to a court, Hdt. 6.42.
subject to jurisdiction, δ. παρασχεῖν τοὺς ἠδικηκότας Plb. 4.44.3, cf. UPZ 121.14.
or δοσίπυγος, ον, = κίναιδος, Suid. s.v. ἀφέλεια.
οντος, ὁ, fut. part. of δίδωμι, always going to give, always promising ; hence Δώσων as a name of Antigonus II, Plu. Cor. 11.
ἡ, fem. of δωτήρ, Linus ap. Stob. 3.1.70, Arat. 113, Man. 2.447, Nonn. D. 19.45.
ῆρος, ὁ, giver, δωτῆρες ἑάων givers of good, i.e. the gods, Od. 8.325, Hes. Th. 46, etc. ; voc. δῶτερ ὑγείης Rev.Arch. 1911.439 (Thrace).
ου, ὁ, = δωτήρ, Hes. Op. 355.
receive or collect presents, Hdt. 2.180.

ἡ, gift, present, Il. 9.155, Od. 9.268, Hdt. 1.61 ; δωτίνην δοῦναι give as a free gift, ib. 69, cf. Them. Or. 21.260d.
rent in kind, IG 4.841.8, 11 (Calauria, iii BC).
τό, shortd. Ep. form for δῶμα, house, dwelling, Hom. only in nom. as Od. 1.392, and acc. as Il. 1.426. — As pl. for δώματα, only in Hes. Th. 933.
δώς, φέρνη, Hsch.
ύος, ἡ, Ion., = τροφή, Suid. (leg. ἐδητύς).
οῦς, ἡ, Giver, name of a Nereid, Il. 18.43, Hes. Th. 248.
ορος, ὁ, = δωτήρ, δῶτορ ἑάων giver of goods, addressed to Hermes, Od. 8.335, h.Hom. 18.12, cf. Luc. Sat. 14 ; to Zeus, Call. Jov. 91 ; θεοὶ τούτων δώτορες ἀμφοτέρων Thgn. 134, cf. E. Hyps. Fr. 7.5.

or repeated ἒ ἒ ἒ ἔ, an exclamation of pain or grief ; woe ! woe ! A. Ag. 1114, etc. ; always doubled either once or twice and better written ἐέ (as in cod. Med. of A. and S.), or (where the metre requires an iambus) ἐή S. OC 149 ; but ἠέ cod. Med. in A. Th. 966.
v. οὗ.
Ep. and Ion. for ἦν, impf. of εἰμί.

exclam. of surprise or displeasure, ha! oho! esp. before a question, ἔα, τί χρῆμα ; A. Pr. 300, E. Or. 1573 ; ἔα, τίς οὗτος… ; Id. Hec. 501, cf. 733, al. ; ἔα, τίς ἔσθ’ ; Ar. Pl. 824 ; sts. extra versum, E. Hec. 1116, Med. 1005, al. ; sts. doubled, ἔ. ἔα, ἄπεχε A. Pr. 688 (lyr.) ; ἔα [ἔα], ἰδού S. OC 1477 (lyr.). — Rare in Prose, ἔα, ἔφη, σοφισταί τινες Pl. Prt. 314d ; ἔα, τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί ; Ev. Luc. 4.34.
v. ἄγνυμι.
v. ἄγνυμι.
part. ἑαδώς, v. ἁνδάνω.
ἀλγεῖ, Hsch.
v. εἴλω.
λυπηρόν, λυτήριον, Hsch.
v. ἁλίσκομαι.
v. ἁλίσκομαι.

(so early Attic Inscrr., as IG1². 3.20, εἰάν sts. after BC 400, ib. 22.28.17, cf. PEleph. 1.8, 10 (iv BC)), also contr. ἤν and ἄν, v. ἤν, ἄν² [α], which by crasis with καί become κἄν : — if haply, if, regularly folld. by subj. ; for its use and for examples, v. εἰ B. ΙΙ, and ἄν¹ B. Ι. 1.
in Hellenistic and late Greek, = ἄν after relative Pronouns and Conjunctions, as ὃς ἐάν whosoever, LXX Ge. 15.14, PTeb. 107.8 (ii BC), Ev. Matt. 5.19, al. ; ὅσος ἐάν PPetr. 3 p. 120 (iii BC), Ev. Matt. 18.18 ; ὅστις ἐάν Ph. 1.220, M.Ant 9.23 ; ὅπου ἐάν Ev. Matt. 8.19, etc. ; ὅθεν ἐάν Gp. 1.3.3 ; folld. by ind., LXX 1Ki. 2.14.
[The second syll. of ἐάν is long, S. OC 1407, Ar. V. 228, Sopat. 6.9.]
v. ἁνδάνω.
ον, (< ἑανός, ὁ) wearing a thin robe, Ἠώς Antim. 84.

[ᾱ] ή, όν, Ep. Adj. (never in Od.) : — fine, of fabrics and materials for wearing, ἑανῷ λιτί with fine linen, Il. 18.352, 23.254 ; πέπλος ἑανός 5.734, 8.385 ; ἑανοῦ κασσιτέροιο tin beaten out fine, 18.613 ; ἱμάτιον Sappho (?) 122.

[ᾰ] ὁ, fine robe, once in nom., ἀμφὶ δ’ ἄρ’ ἀμβρόσιος ἑανὸς τρέμε Il. 21.507 ; νεκταρέου ἑανοῦ 3.385 ; ἑανῷ ἀργῆτι φαεινῷ ib. 419 ; ἀμβρόσιον ἑανόν (acc.) 14.178 ; ἑανῶν πτύχας ἱμεροέντων h.Cer. 176 ; λεπταλέῳ ἑανῷ ARh. 4.169 ; ἑανοῖς χρυσειδέσι Hymn.Is. 109 ; also with the first syll. long, εἱανοῦ ἁπτομένη Il. 16.9 ; cf. ἴανον. sail, λῦε ἑανοῦ πτέρυγας Lyr.Alex.Adesp. 20.9.
[Hom. always makes ᾱ in the Adj., ᾰ in the Subst. ; but later poets use ᾱ or ᾰ, as suits the metre, as Orph. A. 877, 1223.] (Cf. ἕννυμι ; the Subst. has the digamma, Il. 14.178, 21.507, whereas the Adj. has not, 18.352, 613, 23.254.), Myc. we-a2-no-i (dat. pl.)
v. εἰ B. ΙΙ.
ἦσαν, Hsch.
v. ἄγνυμι.

or εἶαρ (Hsch. ἦαρ, ἴαρα), τό, in Alex. Poets, blood, λύθρῳ τε καὶ εἴαρι πεπλήθασι Call. Fr. anon. 20 ; Αἰακίδαο εἴαρος Euph. 39.3 ; τὸ δ’ ἐκ μέλαν εἶαρ ἔλαπτεν Call. Fr. 247, cf. Nic. Al. 314, Oppian. H. 2.618 ; cf. εἰαροπότης, εἰαροπῶτις.
juice, εἶαρ ἐλαίης Nic. Al. 87 ; ἐκ λύχνου πῖον ἔλειξαν ἔαρ Call. Fr. 201. (Cypr. acc. to Hsch. ; identified with ἔαρ spring, by EM 307.44, Suid. ; cf. Skt. ásṛk, gen. asnás, Lett. asinis ΄blood΄.)
ἐπλησίασεν, Hsch.
τὰς κανθαρίδας, Hsch.
(-δροπος Bgk.), ον, plucked in spring, Pi. Fr. 75.6.
Bgk. for ἐαρίδρεπτος.

pass the spring, X. An. 3.5.15.
bloom as in spring, Ph. 2.99 ; — Med., λειμῶνες ἄνθεσιν ἐαριζόμενοι Pl. Ax. 371c.
to be like spring, μετοπώρου ἐαρίζοντος Ph. 1.13, cf. 2.643.

ή, όν, Ep. εἰαρινός (also ἠαρινός h.Cer. 401, PPetr. 3 p. 152 (iii BC)) ; in other Poets, ἠρινός : — of spring, εἰαρινὴ ὥρη springtime, Il. 16.643, cf. Plb. 3.34.6 ; εἰαρινὰ ἄνθεα Il. 2.89 ; πλόος εἰαρινός Hes. Op. 678 ; θάλπος ἐαρινόν the heat of spring, X. Cyr. 8.6.22 ; ἄνεμος ἠρινός Sol. 13.19 ; ἠρινὰ φύλλα Pi. P. 9.46 ; λειμῶνος ἠρινοῦ στάχυν E. Supp. 448 ; ἐ. πυλαία IG 9(1).111 (Elatea) ; τροπαί Ph. 2.163 ; μῆλα ἐ. apricots, PCair. Zen. 33.13 (iii BC) ; — neut. as Adv., in spring-time, μέλισσα λειμῶν’ ἠρινὸν διέρχεται E. Hipp. 77 (s.v.l., ἐαρινή Sch.) ; γῆ ἠρινὸν θάλλουσα Id. Fr. 316.3 ; ἠρινὰ κελαδεῖν, of the swallow, Ar. Pax 800 (lyr.). Adv. ἐαρινῶς Hsch. s.v. ἦρις ὡς.
ῥόδον, Hsch.
τό, ewer, IG 12(3).450a1 (Thera, pl.) ; ἐαρόν, Hsch.
ές, flourishing in spring, λειμῶνες Mosch. 2.67.
ον, spring-coloured, fresh green, ἴασπις Orph. L. 267.
α, ον, poet. for ἐαρινός, Nic. Th. 380.

τό, Hom. (only gen. ἔαρος), etc. ; contr. ἦρ Alcm. 76 ; gen., dat., ἦρος, ἦρι, Lyr. (Alc. 45), Att., and prob. Ion., cf. Hdt. 1.77, Hp. Epid. 1.1 (but ἔαρος is found in codd. of Hdt. 5.31, 7.162, al., Hp. l.c.) ; poet. gen., dat., εἴαρος, εἴαρι (metri gr.), Alcm. 26, h.Cer. 174 (nisi leg. ἤαρος), and later Poets (whence was formed late nom. εἶαρ Numen. ap. Ath. 9.371e, Ter.Maur. 653) ; cf. Hdn. Gr. 1.408 (Hes. used ἔαρ as a monos., and ἔαρι as a trochee, Op. 492, 462) : — spring, ἔαρος δ’ ἐπιγίγνεται ὥρῃ Il. 6.148 ; ἔαρος νέον ἱσταμένοιο early spring, Od. 19.519 ; ἔαρι πολεῖν Hes. Op. 462 ; ἅμα τῷ ἔαρι at the beginning of spring, Hdt. 5.31, cf. Th. 4.117, 6.8 ; πρὸς ἔαρ Id. 5.56, etc. ; πρὸς τὸ ἔ. ib. 17 ; περὶ τὸ ἔ. Id. 3.116 ; ἐξ ἦρος εἰς Ἀρκτοῦρον S. OT 1137 ; prov., μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ Cratin. 33 ; also of the prime, flower of anything, ἔφηβοι… ἔ. τοῦ δήμου Demad. Fr. 4S., cf. Hdt. 7.162, Arist. Rh. 1411a3 ; ἔ. ὁρόωσα looking fresh and bright, Theoc. 13.45 ; γενύων ἔ. the first down on a youth΄s face, AP 6.242 (Crin.) ; ὕμνων ἔ. the freshest, brightest of their kind, ib. 7.12 ; τὸ ἔ. τῶν πτερῶν, of a peacock, Luc. Dom. 11.
(ϝεσṛ-, cf. γέαρ, γίαρ[ες], Lat. vēr, Skt. vasantas, Lith. vasara ΄summer΄.)
Ep. 3 pl. of εἰμί.
Ion. and Ep. impf. of ἐάω.
Dor. part. fem. of εἰμί.
ἑωσφόρος, Hsch.
Ion. 3 pl. pres. of ἧμαι.

α, ον, (< ἐάω) to be suffered, E. Ph. 1210 ; c. inf., ἐατέος ἐστὶ φεύγειν Hdt. 8.108, cf. Pl. R. 401b. ἐατέον one must suffer, E. HF 173, etc.
to be let alone or given up, ἐ. ὁ πλοῦτος Id. Hel. 905, cf. Ph. 1.564. τὴν πόλιν ἐατέον τῆς κατοικίσεως we must let it alone as to foundation, Pl. Lg. 969c ; one must dismiss from one΄s mind, Id. Grg. 512e ; one must omit, Str. 2.5.18.
Ion. 3 pl. impf. of ἧμαι.
ὁ, incorrect form for αὐτάδελφος, CPR 1.155.
ητος, ἡ, self-hood, Procl. Theol.Plat. 5.37.

ῆς, οῦ, ἑαυτῷ, ῇ, ῷ, ἑαυτόν, ήν, ό, pl. ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, ἑαυτούς, άς, ά ; Ion. ἑωυτοῦ SIG 57.44 (Milet., v BC), etc. ; also ωὑτῆς Herod. 6.84, ωὑτέου Aret. SA 1.7 (Ion. ἑωυ- by contraction of ἕο αὐ-, from which also Att. ἑαυ-, freq. written ἑατοῦ in Pap. and Inscrr., as SIG 774.2 (Delph., i BC) ; Att. contr. αὑτοῦ, etc., which is the usual form in Trag., though ἑαυτοῦ, etc., are used (though rarely) when the metre requires, A. Pr. 188 (anap.), al. ; in Att. Inscrr. αὑτοῦ prevails after BC 300 ; Cret. ϝιαυτοῦ Kohler-Ziebarth Stadtrecht von Gortyn p. 34 ; Dor. αὐταυτοῦ, αὐσαυτοῦ ; Thess. εὑτοῦ (dat.), IG 9(2).517.16 ; gen. pl. ηὑτῶν Schwyzer 251 A 44 (Cos)
reflex. Pron. of 3rd pers., of himself, herself, itself, etc. ; first in Alc. 78, Hdt., and Att. (Hom. has ἕο αὐτοῦ, οἷ αὐτῷ, ἑαὐτόν) ; αὐτὸ ἐφ’ ἑαυτό (v.l. -τοῦ) itself by itself, absolutely, Pl. Tht. 152b ; αὐτὸ ἐφ’ αὑτοῦ ib. 160b ; ὅταν τὸ ἐφ’ ἑαυτὸν ἕκαστος σπεύδῃ Th. 1.141 ; αὐτὸ καθ’ αὑτό Pl. Tht. 157a ; αὐτὰ πρὸς αὑτά ib. 154e ; ἀφ’ ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῦ, of themselves, himself, Th. 5.60, X. Mem. 2.10.3 ; ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῦ, v. ἐπί; ἐν ἑαυτῷ γίγνεσθαι, ἐντὸς ἑαυτοῦ γ., v. ἐν, ἐντός; παρ’ ἑαυτῷ at his own house, ib. 3.13.3, etc. ; esp. with Comp. and Sup., ἐγένοντο ἀμείνονες αὐτοὶ ἑωυτῶν they surpassed themselves, Hdt. 8.86 ; πλουσιώτεροι ἑαυτῶν continually richer, Th. 1.8 ; θαρραλεώτεροι αὐτοὶ ἑαυτῶν Pl. Prt. 350a, cf. d ; τῇ αὐτὸ ἑωυτοῦ ἐστι μακρότατον at its very greatest length, Hdt. 2.8, cf. 149, 4.85, 198. in Att., Trag., and later, αὑτοῦ, etc., is used for the 1st or 2nd pers., as for ἐμαυτοῦ, αὐτὸς καθ’ αὑτοῦ τἄρα μηχανορραφῶ A. Ch. 221, cf. S. OT 138, etc. ; for σεαυτοῦ, μόρον τὸν αὑτῆς οἶσθα A. Ag. 1297, cf. 1141, Pl. Phd. 101c (v.l.), Ph.Mech. Bel. 59.16, etc. ; so in pl., τὰ αὑτῶν (= ἡμῶν αὐτῶν) ἐκποριζώμεθα Th. 1.82 ; δώσομεν ἑαυτούς Epicur. Sent.Vat. 47 ; ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς by ourselves, LXX 1Ki. 14.9, cf. PPar. 47.26 (ii BC), 2 Ep. Cor. 7.1, etc. ; ἑαυτῶν, = ὑμῶν αὐτῶν, PPar. 63.128 (ii BC). pl., ἑαυτῶν, ἑαυτοῖς, etc., is sts. used for ἀλλήλων, ἀλλήλοις, one another, διάφοροι ἑωυτοῖσι Hdt. 3.49 ; παρακελευόμενοι ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Th. 4.25, etc. ; καθ’ αὑτοῖν one against the other, S. Ant. 144 (anap.) ; πρὸς αὑτούς D. 18.19 ; περιϊόντες αὑτῶν πυνθάνονται Id. 4.10, cf. Pl. Ly. 215b.

found only in Il. 13.543 ἐπὶ δ’ ἀσπὶς ἑάφθη καὶ κόρυς and 14.419 ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἀσπὶς ἑάφθη. (Acc. to Tyrannio ap. Sch. A, = ἥφθη, upon him was fastened, i.e. to him clung, his shield ; acc. to Aristarch., connected with ἕπομαι, shield and helmet followed after ; ἑ- Aristarch., ἐ- most Mss. ; possibly connected with ἰάπτω, was hurled over him ; glossed by ἐκάμφθη, ἐβλάβη, Hsch.)

contr. ἐῶ Il. 8.428, etc. ; Ep. εἰῶ 4.55 ; Ep. 2 and 3 sg. ἐάᾳς, ἐάᾳ, Od. 12.137, Il. 8.414 ; inf. ἐάαν Od. 8.509 ; impf. εἴων, as, a, Il. 18.448, Od. 19.25, Th. 1.28, etc. ; Ion. and Ep. ἔων Hdt. 9.2, ἔα Il. 5.517, 16.731 ; also ἔασκον or εἴασκον, 2.832, 5.802, etc. ; fut. ἐάσω [α] 18.296, etc. ; aor. εἴασα (εἴασεν is v.l. for εἴασ’ in 10.299) 24.684, etc. ; Ep. ἔασα 11.437 ; pf. εἴακα D. 8.37, 43.78, Cerc. 17.35 ; — Pass., fut. ἐάσομαι in pass. sense, E. IA 331, Th. 1.142 ; aor. εἰάθην Isoc. 4.97 ; pf. Pass. εἴαμαι D. 45.22. — Hdt. never uses the augm. in this Verb. [α in pres. and impf., α in fut. and aor. even in Ion. (so prob. in Anacr. 56, 57 ; forms with -ασσ- occur as vv. ll. in Hom. and Parm. 8.7). Synizesis occurs in 3 sg. ἐᾷ Il. 5.256, in 1 subj. ἐῶμεν 10.344, and prob. in ἐάσουσιν Od. 21.233 ; also in Trag., in imper. ἔα S. OT 1451, Ant. 95, Ar. Nu. 932 ; ind. ἐῶ Id. Lys. 734 ; Hsch. has the form ἦσεν· εἴασεν, cf. ἦσαι· παῦσαι]
suffer, permit, c. acc. pers. et inf., τούσδε δ’ ἔα φθινύθειν leave them alone to perish, Il. 2.346 ; αἴ κεν ἐᾷ με… ζώειν Od. 13.359, etc. ; ἐᾶν οἰκεῖν Th. 3.48, cf.
